It was quite delicious and I would definitely drink it again! As far as energy goes, I definitely felt energized without feeling jittery​ or shaky. product_title: Fischer & Wieser Specialty Foods Sweet Onion and Garlic Marmalade, 10.5 Ounce
review_headline: A delicious and very healthy condiment
review_body:
This is an excellent version of a great topping for grains, a sandwich spread or a bruschetta topping. It is absolutely delicious, and I try to always keep some on hand.

If you have an hour and a half of time to watch the onions cook, you can make a version at least as good as Fischer and Wieser can make -- and the aroma while cooking is wonderful. My recipe is based on one from "The New York Times".

Ingredients:
2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil (I do not use oil but just water -- in several taste tests, people cannot tell the difference between oil and water prepared onions. And, it is much safer to add the olive oil after cooking -- you will get more taste and the risk of cancer from heating olive oil is lessened.)
2 pounds sweet onions, quartered lengthwise, then cut across the grain in thin slices
Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste -- add near the end because the onions will dramatically change flavor with cooking
2 to 3 garlic cloves, minced
2 teaspoons fresh thyme leaves, or 1 teaspoon dried thyme
1 tablespoon capers, drained, rinsed and finely chopped (a source of salt that affects the "to taste" comment above.)

Technique
1. Heat the olive oil (or water) in a large, heavy nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add the onions. Cook, stirring, until they begin to sizzle and soften, three to five minutes. Add a generous pinch of salt (not in my world). Turn the heat to low, cover and cook slowly for 45 minutes, stirring often. The onions should melt down almost to a purée. Add the garlic, thyme and capers, and taste and adjust salt (later in my world, and then a big grained sea salt to add interest to the finished dish). Stir together, cover and simmer for another 15 to 30 minutes until the mixture is sweet and golden. Remove the lid; if there is liquid in the pan, cook uncovered until the purée is thick and the liquid is gone.

I wait until this point to salt to taste. The capers can sometimes add more saltiness than I like, even if I wash them before cooking.

Yield: Makes about 1 1/4 cups.

Advance preparation: This spread will keep in the refrigerator for at least a week, and it freezes well.(I freeze the spread in a ice cube container, break the frozen cubes out of the tray and then store the cubes in a plastic bag until thawed as my supply runs down.)

(If you don't use the olive oil, this is virtually calorie free and a good source of fiber.)

product_title: Orgain Sweet Vanilla Bean, Vegan (12-Pack)
review_headline: tastes a lot like vitamins (but good for you in general)
review_body:
This review is for the vanilla flavor, which tastes pretty much like some vanilla protein powder dissolved in cold water -- and that's basically what it is. The flavor is not bad, but it's not delicious, either. You can sort of detect a vitamin-like undertone to it.

The consistency is fairly thin -- thicker than water, but thinner than some other meal replacement-type smoothies I've tried. It leaves a little coating of something in your mouth. It's best when cold but I think it would probably work at room temperature, as well. (I had forgotten to chill mine before lunchtime, so I put it in the ice dispenser of my refrigerator for 15 minutes. That worked really well.)

This would be really good for people with dietary restrictions (vegans, people with celiac disease, etc.). It says "hypo-allergenic" on the package, and is free of gluten, dairy, and soy. However, what I cannot figure out is how it would be for people with nut allergies. That information is just absent from the package. (I don't have nut allergies, but I know they can be quite serious, so I would have loved to have been able to help with that. I went to their website and the information isn't there, either.)

The protein levels are excellent, and this is supplemented with a lot of vitamins and minerals. However, it doesn't have very much fiber, so if you were thinking of using these shakes as meal replacements, you'd want to eat some fruit with them, or eat full meals at other times of the day.

Overall, not a bad option for vegans, or other people in a hurry to get out the door in the morning. I just wish it tasted a little better.

review_headline: Great, Safe Product.  Best from the USA, by far.
review_body: We like this product.  My child has been using this formula since 12 weeks old to supplement his breastfeeding.  I did extensive research (we were initially against any type of formula, but due to my milk containing very little fat, we had to supplement) and concluded that this was the best formula offered in the USA. Update:  I just read this description for the product on Amazon and noticed that it said "no measuring spoon was provided in order to avoid toxic exposure due to plastic."  Well, all six cans that I've purchased had contained a measuring scoop.  In fact, the cans that expire October 2016 have a new measuring scoop which is rounded on the bottom; which is a real pain as we portion our scoops on the kitchen scale.   FYI: make sure you're measuring these scoops out to exactly 8.5g or your child WILL become constipated. We weighed some scoops that came directly from the can and can get as much as 10+ grams with each scoop!  If you're making a 6oz bottle, that's an extra 4.5g!!!  That is way too much extra in every bottle. As most of us know, this product does have a higher​ casein protein content than breast milk, therefore it can be constipating at first, but with all that extra powder; no wonder!!

product_title: Matcha Green Tea Powder
review_body:
I am a new fan of Matcha green tea!

I am an avid tea drinker, and I have had Matcha used in recipes while dining out but I had never tried it at home for myself. Wow, this actually taste great! The color is vivid green..can be a little off putting to the little ones but htey love watching me drink it and I have been able to get them to try it. I think the taste is similar to green tea but bolder and stronger.

The tea powder itself is a very fine powder. It only takes 1/2 teaspoon with a cup of water to make so a little goes a long way. Because it is a fine powder, it is easy to use in smoothies, muffins, or other recipes. Now it will color whatever you are using it in, so you won't be able to slide it past the little ones if you were thinking of boosting their snacks or beverages with it.

Besides drinking it just as a tea, try using it in your morning smoothie. My basic smoothie recipe is a cup of milk, half a banana and a handful of frozen fruit. To this I will add protein powder for a power boost before heading off for the day. Now I add in a little Matcha to my morning smoothie and it is wonderful.

According to the product information, Matcha is great for boosting your energy and helping you stay focused. Personally, I just love the taste and that it is a natural product.

If you have ever wanted to give matcha a try, this brand is great. I would recommend this and think you would enjoy your new discovery.

product_title: Ekobrew Stainless Steel Refillable K-cup for Keurig 2.0 and 1.0 Brewers, 2- Count
review_headline: The best reusable cup, works with 2.0
review_body:
I have a Keurig 2.0 and was using the plastic reusable cups before. They worked fine, but I used to wonder what plastic chemicals are leaking into my coffee. It's probably not much, but stainless steel construction gives me more peace of mind.

These cups are constructed well, easy to clean and the orange sticker, to fool the 2.0 machine into thinking a high priced original K cup is being brewed, work perfectly. I particularly like that these cups have just the right amount of holes to filter the coffee just right. My previous plastic cups let the coffee out too fast which made weaker coffee.

Tip for stronger coffee: if you are like me and prefer a strong dose of caffeine in the morning without filling your belly with a large cup of coffee, you would like this. After you fill the cup with your favorite coffee and close the lid, take 4 small spoons of hot water and slowly put it in the cup from hole in the top. Make sure to rotate the cup a few times after each spoon of hot water. It will make sure the coffee is soaked and does not leak. Let it sit for 2 minutes or so before brewing it. You will notice the difference!

One more thing I like about these cups is that there is no paper filter to soak up the coffee oils and keep them from going into your coffee. This coffee tastes much more full bodied!!

Oh and I hand wash them after each use. Don't want to put it in the machine. Hopefully the Orange stickers and some original k cup lids will last a long time!!

review_body:
I wasn't expecting too much from the V8 energy, but was pleasantly surprised. The only way I could think to get a good idea of how much energy this really gives was to replace my Monday morning coffee with this drink. I expected to be groggy and running on empty all day, but was super impressed by how I felt. I was awake, alert, and had plenty of energy to get me through the day. Assuming it was a fluke, I again replaced my morning coffee with V8 Energy the next couple of days with similar results. I have purchased several of these 6-packs since initially trying it, and will continue to do so.

There are two flavors of the diet version of this drink, and I have tried both of them. The cranberry flavor is pretty good; it tastes a little bit like watered down cranberry juice but not in a bad way. The strawberry lemonade flavor isn't the best. I drank all six of them, and would drink it again if I didn't have a choice, but I won't go so far as to say it tastes good. Plus, it's a weird not-found-in-nature yellow color when I poured it into a glass and that put me off.

Finally, I really like they they only have 3 carbs per can, which is awesome for my low-moderate carb lifestyle. Overall, I give these 5 stars!

review_headline: Closest to Callard & Bowser originals that I've found in 10+ years of looking
review_body:
Ordered on 23 July. Estimated delivery was "Wed, Aug 19 - Tue, Sep 1". Arrived on 01 August via airmail. Very pleased with that.

I am enjoying one of these as I write this review. Here are my thoughts on the similarity to the Callard & Bower originals.

Like many others, I enjoyed the original Callard & Bowser licorice toffees and was very sad when they went away. I have tried many, many licorice toffees in pursuit of something similar. At this point, I've probably tried about 40 or 50 different products. I've also resorted to making my own licorice toffees with various recipes I've found on the internet, with mixed results. Usually the homemade versions end up a little too buttery.

These are the closest commercial product I've found. They are not 100% the same, but they are the closest.

The differences are:

1. Shape. These are oblong and circular. The shape is meaningless to me, but it is a difference.

2. Color. These are a muted black, with no hint of green. The color is also meaningless, but it is a difference.

3. Texture. Now we're starting to enter "things that matter" territory. Texture is very, very similar, but slightly softer than the original C&B toffees. Not enough that a C&B devotee will care, and it's very close. I'd say they are 95% as firm as the original C&Bs. I'm fine with this.

4. Taste. Probably the most important characteristic. Very close to the original C&B, but with a less strong buttery component. Having read a ton of "how similar to C&B?" reviews over the years, I know this is important to most people, myself included. This is the difference I think most people will care about. It's not a large difference, but it is a difference. My estimate is that it's about 90% as buttery-flavored (how's that for a description?) as the originals. The licorice taste component is all there.

I'd say these are about 95% the same as the C&B originals with regard to things that you'd care about. I doubt anyone longing for the original C&Bs would be disappointed with these. I'm very happy to have found them.

While I'll keep looking for the holy licorice grail that is the full-on 100% DNA matching C&B clone, I'll continue to order these as my #1 replacement. Even if I never find the grail, I can certainly be happy with these while I continue my search.originals with regard to things that you'd care about. product_title: Melitta Coffee Maker, Single Cup Pour-Over Brewer with Travel Mug (Pack of 2)
review_headline: So far this is one of the worst products I have purchased on Amazon
review_body:
So far this is one of the worst products I have purchased on Amazon. My wife broke the original glass thermal carafe that came with our Bonavita (which was awesome) and this is "supposed" to be the replacement. Here are the problems.

1. There was no vent hole or venting of any kind. So, pouring coffee with the lid on was nearly impossible. It would start fine, but as soon as the vacuum inside developed, the flow would all but stop. I had to drill my own vent hole to fix this problem.

2. Pouring from the open carafe is a messy proposition. Using the carafe to fill the coffee maker with water or to fill your thermos after brewing is a nightmare. The lip on the open carafe seems to encourage the coffee to roll right around the top lip and onto the floor, counter, and/or sink.

3. Possibly the most important, IT DOES NOT KEEP THE COFFEE HOT. I am writing this just after brewing this morning and have found the outside of this "thermal carafe" to be nearly the same temperature as the coffee inside. There is little or no thermal isolation.

I could maybe deal with failure on one of these points, but to fail at every major point is just ridiculous. Maybe I was spoiled by the nearly perfect original Bonavita glass lined carafe, but under no circumstance is this even a moderately acceptable replacement.

product_title: Navitas Naturals Organic Maca Powder, 1 Pound Pouches
review_headline: High quality but the taste really takes some getting used to!
review_body:
When I purchased this product on Oct. 30, 2014, it was $21.49. I see that it is now listed as $70.45! Let me say upfront that there is NO WAY I would have paid that much, although my local health food store is also charging a ridiculously high price. So I'm taking off one star for the new price, and one other star for the taste.

This is the first time that I have purchased Maca power but I am sure this is the real deal. The texture is fine and even. It is "gelatinized" which means it has been processed in such a way that it doesn't upset your stomach. It didn't upset my stomach, but eaten straight and plain, it tastes like cigarette ashes. Not good at all. I was regretting my purchase even at $21.49 per pound, but when I saw the new higher price I decided to give it another go. This time I mixed it with cocoa powder and added it to my smoothie, with bananas, macadamia nuts, ice, water, kale and a little sugar. The taste was HIGHLY improved when I mixed it with cocoa powder. Still. I tried to serve hot cocoa with a bit of maca powder to my boyfriend and he did not care for it at all! I am thinking of using my capsule machine and just making capsules out of the remaining powder rather than trying to mix it in with stuff in the future. But I haven't completely decided.

review_headline: Good heat profile, but flavor falls apart with food.
review_body: This is the funniest hot sauce bottle labeling I've ever seen; very entertaining, front and back.  However the label is very misleading.  This stuff is indeed hot, but hardly overwhelming, both going in and going out, despite labeling that this stuff is hotter going out than going in.  The label claims that one drop is too much, and to use with caution.  I submit that anyone who would even consider tasting something with that kind of warning on the label would have absolutely no issue tasting this stuff.  I've been eating it by the spoonful with no issues.  As mentioned earlier, it's hot, but not painfully so, in fact it's a good heat.  The flavoring is good too, when taken by the spoon.  Slightly sweet to offset the heat, and rather tasty.  The flavor profile kind of falls apart and gets lost in the food if I add it to something like chicken or beef. review_body:
My concern is for this line, apparently from the packaging in the description--This noodle was mad with the selected pure materials under the observed Rules of Health and was found eligible by Inspector. (Copied from product package) Product of P.R.O.C.

So, is this P.R.O.C. as in Peoples Republic Of China? Go look at Wikipedia yourself, China's got a bad track record on glass/cellophane noodles. First, they were caught adding lead based whiteners to the noodles, then a few years later caught again for adding a poisonous bleach type chemical that was even illegal in China itself as a food additive. Then caught in 2010 for adding far more aluminum than allowed within European laws on exports. Umm, no thanks, I'd prefer to buy food from a producer that *does care* whether I live or die. God knows what is blended in with the noodles if they came from China.

Even the statement is poorly worded--as a precursor to quality? "Made" not "mad" and "by a qualified inspector" not "by Inspector". If you can't get the statements correct, it begs if you can improve over your track record.

product_title: Frontier Tea Bag, 16 Ounce
review_body:
I trust all European, and/or German certified products, especially when it comes to organic certification. The Europeans are much stricter when it comes to any organic products. Never heard of Egyptian chamomile, cotton yes (doubtless the best). Chamomile NO! Anything organic from third world countries is usually suspect since they don't take regulations overall very serious.
As far this product goes, it's excellent in taste, aroma and flavor. Another thing, German regulators are much stricter in all food related requirements. Additives that are allowed in the US and most other countries are not allowed in Germany. Some regulations vary in different EU countries too, but Germany is at the top of the list as far as health and environmental issues are concerned, not just in Europe, but world-wide!
As far as some of the flowers "deteriorating" that is normal and not a flaw for all delicate dried flowers. Brew the tea, let it settle, then I recommend a very fine sieve, like some great ones from England, etc. You can also line a regular sieve with organic filter paper.

product_title: Seeds and Things Carolina Reaper Pepper 10 Seeds - This pepper rates an average of 1,569,300 Scoville heat units
review_body:
I ordered these seeds from Seeds And Things, on August 30, 2014 and they arrived five days later. I sowed 2 of the 20 seeds on September 05, 2014. Germination of both seeds followed 9 days later. By October 20, 2014 the two seedlings were big enough to transplant into their final 12" wide x 11" tall pot. I grew the plants in my bedroom under a 42 watt CFL over the winter. They became magnificent specimens with large, glossy leaves, and producing lots of flowers that would fall off the plant. No fruit ever set while the plants were indoors.

On April 09, 2015, I placed my potted plants outside for the first time. For a week or so, any flowers produced would simply fall off the plant before setting fruit. I was quite thrilled when several of the flowers finally didn't fall off, and instead dropped their petals to make way for little green pods. The two plants together seem to produce 8 - 20 pods at any one time. The first pod started to ripen on June 08, 2015, to be followed by dozens more. The earliest pods did not look like the images I saw online, so I was initially worried these might not be Carolina Reapers. However, later pods that developed looked exactly like the images of Reaper pods online abroad, and the images on this item's product page. My plants are producing an abundance of uselessly hot peppers, and are about 3 feet tall now. Shortly after I placed these plants outdoors, they were toppled over by wind. They continued to grow and produce pods. They even sprouted more stems from the base, and now you can't even tell they were ever damaged.

After a few of the pods got torn off one of my plants by an unknown pest, I decided to slice one and see just what these peppers were capable of. The pod I cut open was about half mature size and still green. I expected it to be a pretty hot, but probably not hotter than I could handle, being immature and unripe. I placed a small slice in my mouth and chewed once. The flavor and smell was strongly of Habanero. It did not actually seem to burn my mouth, but instead caused sharp, stinging pain in all the soft tissue in my mouth as if I had chewed razor blades. I had to spit the pepper slice out, and my mouth hurt for about 30 minutes. Pretty unique effect, but culinarily useless in my opinion.

I have been giving all the mature red pods to my uncle who (somehow) enjoys eating ultra-hot peppers. He buys and consumes exotic sauces and enthusiastically consumed some fresh Trinidad Scorpion pods I got for him last year. He'd been closely following my Reaper project, and was exited to finally try one of the pods. I watched him slice and consume one of my bright red fully mature Carolina Reaper pods. His face turned deep red, he took on a concerned, silent expression, and his eyes watered as he chewed. He did not speak for a few minutes, and when he did, he confirmed in a raspy voice that these are the hottest fresh peppers he's ever eaten.

If you're looking to try growing the Carolina Reaper, these seeds are genuine and they turned out to be easy to grow.. product_title: San Francisco Bay One Cup
review_headline: Good coffee, their PODs don't work for me.
review_body:
This coffee tastes great. However, I am unlikely to purchase this or any San Francisco Bay OneCup product again. While the "OneCups" are better for the environment, they present a storage issue for myself. Most of the pod is exposed to the air, and the company provides a plastic cup and lid to store each bag of 10 pods in. If left out of the sealed bag or plastic cup, the coffee smells great but it would probably lose its freshness rapidly. Especially in my case, where I only use 2 pods per day. I have my V1.0 brewer in a tight space, on top of a storage drawer. The drawer is open to the air, so I can't store their product there, and once I open the bag of ten, I need to use it within the week, as I'm not sure the air in the cup will not affect the freshness of the exposed pods. Again, if I brew more than 2 cups a day, I'm going to have a fight with the wife, as my doctor would like me to be off caffeine.

Like I said to lead off, this coffee is very good when brewed at 8oz, 12oz, and 12 oz over ice. It does not taste burnt, like most Starbucks and some Pete's does to my taste buds. I disappointed that I won't be a repeat customer of their coffee, as I like what the company has done to take on the Keurig/Green Mountain monster did with using DRM to limit what can be brewed in their V2.0 machines. Another favorite coffee seller of mine, Community Coffee just went over to the dark side and appears to have reached a licensing deal with the consumer bully. Just wish their pods were more compatible with my logistics requirements.

I gave them 4 stars for their taste and their consumer friendliness, but could not give them 5 stars due to issues that truly mine, but may impact other potential purchasers also.

product_title: Food Should Taste Good Multigrain Tortilla Chips, 1.5 Ounce -- 24 per case. by Food Should Taste Good [Foods]
review_body:
I buy these locally, but I wanted to post here and say how good I think these are. That, and mention that you may want to look for them at your local grocer or Target (or wherever you shop). I can get these at either Target or Safeway for between ~$3.50 and $5 for a 5.5-ounce bag depending on the day, and you can check the expiration date when you buy locally. Buying directly from Amazon is a good way to go, though, as I know that they'll make it right if you get a bad batch from them. Prices fluctuate so much on Amazon, though, that you certainly may find them cheaper here than locally. There are multiple product pages on Amazon for these chips, so be sure to check around for the best price and bag size for your needs.

I really like the flavor, texture, and size of the Multigrain version (and it's the only one that I've tried, although I've seen some of the others). They have a nice, healthy taste to them - not overly salty or oily, and I love the addition of the seeds. Btw, the seeds aren't obtrusive or make them more difficult to eat. Instead, they just add some nice additional taste to the corn. Although not triangular like a lot of tortilla chips, the shape is still good for dipping into salsa.

I enjoy these chips either with salsa or simply plain. They taste good, and while likely still not a health food :), they sure seem healthier to me than a lot of the regular corn tortilla chips that I get.

Two big thumbs up from me for the Multigrain. I highly recommend them.

review_headline: Adds a Nice Flavor to Your Tuna Dish

I've tried all three prime fillet varieties, and this was my favorite. I am a tuna lover! I will eat tuna salad on a sandwich, in a wrap, and as a patty melt. I also loved to use tuna in pasta dishes and in salad. My love of tuna is what made this sound so great. For the sun dried tomato variety, I thought I would indulge my tuna melt craving. I opened up the can and drained the oil. I usually prefer my tuna in water, so this was a bit of a disappointment to me. The tomato flavor is pretty prevalent in this, so I miss a bit of the tuna flavor. What I do love is the tuna is in nice meaty chunks instead of a pulverized mush. It didn't matter much for my sandwich, but this was a nice benefit for salads where it was nice to have the chunks front and center. I think it adds a new depth of flavor without going overboard. It held up well to the heating on my melt and tasted delicious! I won't make it my every day tuna, but I think it would be great if I'm looking to make something a little nicer.

review_body:
Arizona Palmer Zero, Half and Half, Tea and Lemonade, 23 Ounce (680 mL) (Pack of 24), from AriZona.
Before we even get started, this product contains Sucralose (Splenda), which is not good for your health. See this website: ARTICLES.MERCOLA.COM/sites/articles/archive/2009/02/10/new-study-of-splenda-reveals-shocking-information-about-potential-harmful-effects.aspx. Sucralose causes weight gain, and may seriously interfere with your prescription medications.

All those health problems, to avoid the tooth decay, weight gain, and Type II Adult Diabetes, caused by too much sugar. Sugar, and especially High Fructose Corn Syrup (HFCS), have their issues, and should be used in moderation, if at all, -but nothing as bad as sucralose, saccharin, aspartame, and other artificial sweeteners. Processed foods in general contain far too much sugar and salt than is good for our health. We should try to cut down on the amount of sugar and salt we consume from all food sources.

If you are still interested in this Arizona Arnold Palmer Zero, Half and Half, Tea and Lemonade, I will give you a summary. It is too sweet. It contains pear juice, which is good as a food, but it is not listed on the front label. Why would it even be needed or used? It may be an effort to cover up the taste of the artificial sweetener. This tea also contains acacia gum, and I do not like foods containing gums of any kind. And finally, this tea just tastes strange. Buy something else, or better yet, make your own tea, and add the juice from a slice of lemon. Refrigerate it after it cools off. Only the good stuff, and cheap as well!

review_headline: main virtue this product has is that the pistachios are SHELLED for you
review_body: The only thing I would take off for would not be right to take off for. That is that I love these nuts heavily salted and these were not salted. However, as we know, it is lousy for your health to be consuming heavily salted nuts. However, it is easy enough to buy the salted version if you want to throw caution to the wind. The main virtue this product has though is that the pistachios are SHELLED for you. I first started eating these nuts back when you could only get them in the dyed pink shells. So after gorging on them, I was left with pink hands. The pink dye fell into disfavor and these nuts started being sold in their own natural shells, which is a plain off white shade. No more pink hands. But if you are binging on pistachios, you will tear your nails up. I don't care because I have short, unpolished nails. For a person with manicured hands, these nuts in the shells are a disaster. Enter the shelled ones. I must admit that I love the unshelled ones. product_title: Miracle Noodle Gluten-free Shirataki Pasta
review_body:
So let's get one thing out of the way: When you open the bag of noddles the funk seeping from the bag may be a turn off to you, but don't let your nose get in the way. Just drain those bad boys, wash them with cold water (the instructions say 2 minutes, but it the smell offends you one extra minute wont hurt), blanch them in hot water and let them sit on a paper towel for 3 minutes. Once you have done that, the smell fades and you are ready to mix them into whatever recipe you desire.

For a carbohydrate addict currently on carb restriction, these noodles were a Godsend. As of today I have used the angel hair in a chicken stir-fry recipe that allowed me have the texture of a noddle without the consequences of carbohydrate overload. The noddles took on most of the seasoning, almost better than a regular noddle. I am not sure if I will be able to afford a regular shipment, but I know I will order this again.

product_title: Douwe Egberts Aroma Rood Ground Coffee, 17.6-Ounce
review_headline: Has changed my life....(well sort of!) lol
review_body:
Recently, we ordered coffee after a meal in a large casino. Coffee, in my opinion has always been nasty, bitter, never enjoyable, certainly not good tasting! I drink it because I NEED it to wake up, not because I like it. I won't even waste sugar or expensive creamers in coffee, why try to make it something its not? I just swallow the bitter pill and get on with my mornings! However, THIS CUP of coffee changed all that. It was delicious! I was shocked. I never knew coffee could taste like this. I drank it down and ordered another cup. I also asked the waitress for the name of this incredible brew....she wrote it down for me. It was Douwe Egberts, she told she thought Wal-Mart sold it. Boo! :( Deal breaker for me! It takes MUCH more than a cup of coffee to make me need anything badly enough to go into a Wal-Mart! And now that Wal-Mart has gotten so "PC" with their refusal to make a confederate flag cake, but DID make an ISIS flag cake....I was more than happy to add them to my growing list of corporations we are boycotting! lol Corporations need to stay out of politics and personal, moral decisions, IMO. (Forgive my ranting, I know I am only rating a coffee!)
To get to my point, I remembered today that Amazon sells groceries...and I am happy to see they sell my new favorite brand of coffee! I am ordering some today and look forward to enjoying it very soon, cuz Amazon ALWAYS delivers quickly! Try it! Its not just another cup of coffee...it will take your mornings to a whole new level! And you won't have to got to Wal-Mart! How awesome is that?

product_title: TruVibe 100% Organic Raw Cacao Nibs, Fair Trade, Criollo Cacao
review_headline: Great product & what seems like a good company, too!
review_body: I had been eyeing cacao nibs for a while, but it wasn't until I decided to do a little "sugar reset" experiment where I eliminated sugar/sweet foods for a few weeks (you know, cause it just sounded like such good fun! ha) that I decided to splurge and give them a try. I figured they'd be a good option if I wanted a bit more of a decadent snack that was still 100% unsweetened. The package came promptly, as ordered, and it was exactly what I was hoping for! They're a little bitter -- my boyfriend, especially, thought I was nuts for liking them after he took a spoonful -- but they really add a nice, complex earthiness to a dish. I mix them into my overnight oats (rolled oats, peanut flour, chia seeds, hemp seeds, some buckwheat, homemade almond milk, and the cacao nibs) and can't get enough of it. I've also sprinkled them over a spoonful of all-natural peanut butter. I haven't tried baking with them yet, but overall, very pleased with the purchase. The bag is also pretty big (I got the 16oz) and seems to last. Bonus points for being fair trade AND organic, a combo I had some trouble finding on Amazon.

review_headline: I thought that these were package nicely and were very fresh
review_body:
I use Cardamom in several recipes that I make and I have been needing whole cardamom for a while...once I found that these were organic, I decided to give it a try! I thought that these were package nicely and were very fresh. I was quite pleased with the amount I received and think that the price is on point for an organic, fresh, quality whole cardamom.

Here is a recipe we use in our house :
Cardamom Honey Chicken Recipe

Ingredients
Marinade
4 Tbsp honey
2 Tbsp sherry
1 teaspoon cardamom seeds, ground
1 teaspoon peppercorns, ground
Chicken
6 chicken breasts, or one whole chicken, cut into parts
2 Tbsp Olive oil
1 lemon, thinly sliced
Salt and pepper
Method
cardamom-chicken-1.jpg cardamom-chicken-2.jpg
If a recipe calls for ground cardamom, it is best to start with whole pods. Break open the pods to release the tiny brown and black cardamom seeds. Use a spice grinder or mortar and pestle to grind the seeds.
1 Preheat oven to 390°F. Warm the honey, stir in the sherry, cardamom and peppercorns. Place marinade and chicken in a large bowl, coat chicken with marinade. Cover with plastic wrap and let sit at room temperature for 30 minutes.
2 Heat olive oil in a large frying pan at medium high heat. Sear the chicken, skin side down, until golden.
cardamom-chicken-3.jpg
3 Place lemon slices in a roasting pan. Lay the chicken pieces on top. Brush with the marinade. Season generously with salt and pepper. Place in the oven and bake until done, approximately 15 minutes for breasts, 20 minutes for thighs, wings, and drumsticks. Remove from oven and let rest for 10 minutes before serving. Pour out drippings from the pan into a gravy boat for gravy.
Serve with rice, mashed potatoes, or couscous.

It is delicious and tasted especially good using these organic fresh green Indian whole cardamom! I highly recommend and will be repurchasing in the future!!

review_headline: This set is everything you need!
review_body:
The set arrived in perfect condition, with everything placed just perfectly. The presentation was awesome. After removing all items from the box and doing an initial cleaning, I couldn't resist having an immediate cup of matcha tea. I followed the included instructions to prepare my tea and found it to be simply delightful. It gave a nice froth upon mixing and I could tell it was a tea of extraordinary quality.
The aroma was very sweet and pleasant. I just kind of held the bowl of tea under my nose for a while before taking my first sip to really take that wonderful aroma in. The color was a nice forest green and it was quite what I expected, having had matcha before. I was pleasantly surprised upon taking that first sip, because oh it was so wonderful. It had such a delicate sweetness that quite matched its aroma. It was quite smooth with very little aftertaste, unlike some other matcha teas I have encountered.
The cleanup was also very easy. The bowl and whisk are easy to clean and store. I love this set and have used it everyday since I received it. I am quite satisfied with my purchase and highly recommend it to both beginners and those who have enjoyed matcha for some time.

review_headline: This is indeed the best TVP I've ever used
review_body: This is indeed the best TVP I've ever used.  Why?  Because it digest so well compared to Bob's Red Mill brand.  Bob's is a good product, too, but it is granular whereas this UNFI TVP is more flakey like corn flakes.  I believe this is why it is noticeably easier to digest than Bob's.  Decent price, too, although I do wonder that the price of all TVP jumped up a while back because Sam's stopped selling the bargain pack of Boca burgers.... so people turned to TVP which possibly drove demand. That's just a theory though.  I don't know that for certain but the two events did occur simultaneously.  I do, however, know this TVP digest better than Bob's.  My favorite way to eat it is to mix it 1:1 with boiling water and add taco seasoning, chili powder, and some liquid smoke.  But it's also good to mix it 1:1 with boiling water and add sausage seasoning.... which can be used to make a vegetarian version of "sausage & eggs" and/or the sausage flavored TVP is also good on pizza.

review_headline: NOT HULLESS, NOT OK FOR DIGESTIVE ISSUES
review_body:
NOT HULLESS. Bogus marketing BS. Certainly NOT OK for diverticulosis. Here's the truth: the hull is thin, so when the kernel pops, the hull literally turns itself inside out, so all you see is beautiful popcorn. If you break one apart, you see that the hull has separated into many small pieces, and they are all embedded in the popcorn. So you can indeed eat it and have no hulls stuck in your teeth. The hulls go silently into your intestines where they do their damage just like Orville's. The proof is in the bottom of the bowl, where you find the partially popped kernels and see what's really going on. Big BOO to the marketing department. It is actually very good popcorn. But BIG BOOS to the vendor for saying ok for those who have digestive issues.

Note to vendor: show me the data.

product_title: NurturMe NurturMeals Organic Dry Meal Pouches, 2 Count
review_headline: A good choice for a "first food" cereal, if you can find it
review_body:
There are two versions of the quinoa cereal, even though the packaging is nearly identical. One is just quinoa, and the other is quinoa with organic and natural minerals, vitamins, and iron fortification. The simple, quinoa-only one was my daughter's "first food" when transitioning, and it couldn't have been a better experience. She l-o-v-e-s the stuff, even still after a period of pureed fruits and vegetables. It's been relatively tough to find, though, and I've seen vendors mix up which version of the cereal they have available (iron or no iron). I've only been able to find the non-iron/quinoa-only version in these single-serving packs. I'm thinking this is the only way they sell this version.

My experiences with the iron-fortified version is the exact opposite: baby hates it, doesn't mix well (gelatinous blobs), tastes terrible (isn't easy on the nose, either), and comes in a multi-serving pouch. It's also, unfortunately for me, easier to find at stores than the individual packs of the quinoa-only version.

With the growing concerns of synthetic arsenic levels, artificial fortifications, GMOs, and other variables lurking around your baby's diet and down the supermarket aisle, shelf-stable alternatives to self-prepared items come under a lot of fire, due or undue. This product (the quinoa-only version) is such a value to have. The trend of quinoa as a first-food/infant cereal is a growing one; until some of the more prominent get in on the game, I'll be using the NurturMe lines.

I've seen vendors use stock photos of both versions when selling the stuff. The stuff seems new and obscure, but make sure you're getting the right version. You might find this product is currently more difficult to procure than you think...

You can make your recipe as simple as brown some meat (I like chicken the best so far) and pour on the sauce. Simmer a bit and serve. I put it over rice to soak up all the amazing juice. The sauce is medium thick. The recipes on the back suggest adding corn. I've tried chopped cherry tomatoes...very good, or you could go crazy and add a bunch of Mexican inspired ingredients. Avocado would be great on top.

The flavor is excellent. Doesn't taste like it came out of a jar at all. Medium spicy. If you like really hot, you can certainly add some heat with peppers of any sort.

It could work in or over a burrito but not so much for tacos unless you add plenty of meat for substance.

product_title: Jade Leaf - Organic Japanese Matcha Green Tea Powder, Classic Culinary Grade (For Blending & Baking)
review_headline: It's definitely an art to be mastered...
review_body:
It took a few tries to get the right latte consistency and flavor, but now that I have it down I can officially say it's delicious. First attempt, I misread the recommendation and used a full teaspoon for one cup (8oz boiling water) then added a bit of milk - big mistake! Tasted like wheatgrass! Whatever you do, DON'T overdo it! Reattempted with 1/2 tsp, as it calls for, this time with only 3oz water and 5oz warm milk trying for a "true" latte. Too thick, and still a bit grassy. Third time's a charm: precise 1/2 tsp (level, not heeping) with a full 8oz boiling water, then added a generous amount of nondairy vanilla coffeemate, and BINGO. Perfection!

And for those saying the small bag couldn't possibly be 30 servings - you may need to refresh your memory of dry unit measuring, as 1/2 tsp is a very small amount of powder. There could possibly be even more than 30 servings, if you measure precisely or even prefer a milder taste and use a tad less. Matcha is unlike regular teas and is very, very potent, being that you are consuming the powdered tea leaves themselves as opposed to just the extract. So you shouldn't really use more than 1/2 tsp per serving anyhow.

Cheers!

product_title: McCormick Skillet Sauce Chili
review_body: The Smoky Applewood BBQ Chicken variety of McCormick Skillet Sauce is a fairly quick and easy way to make a barbecue flavored chicken dish.  First of all, I reviewed the ingredients list and nutrition panel. While I am not a believer of the "HFCS Will Be the Death of Us All" fear mongering, I do note that it is second on the ingredients list, with water being the first. The rest of the ingredients are fairly typical for barbecue sauce, and indeed, tasted directly out of the pouch the sauce tastes like a thin sweet barbecue sauce. A standardized "serving" will give you 8 grams of sugar and 320 mg of sodium (13% RDA).  Preparation couldn't be easier: a pound and a half of browned boneless chicken breasts or thighs, with or without onions as you desire, and simmered with a packet of the sauce until hot. There is also a slow cooker preparation method.  I prepared it with a pound and a half of skinless boneless chicken breasts. After sautéing some diced onion and green pepper, I browned chicken breasts as directed, poured in the pouch of sauce, covered, and simmered until everything heated through. I served the chicken with rice and spooning some of the sauce over each.  The resulting supper was judged to be "just okay" by both Mrs. Boilermate and me. There were no strange, unpleasant, or offputting flavors in the sauce before or after heating, and there were no unpleasant aftertastes.  But how does it compare to a similar dish using regular bottled barbecue sauce instead of this product? First off, we both thought the sauce was a little too sweet and lacked the "punch" of our two favorite barbecue sauces, [[ASIN:B000M78N2I Bone Suckin BBQ Sauce]] and [[ASIN:B00061EMX4 Dinosaur Bar-B-Que Original Sensuous Slathering BBQ Sauce]]. Despite a fairly high sodium content, we both thought it tasted a bit bland, and neither of us detected any bacon flavor.  The first ingredient of the Bone Suckin and Dinosaur sauces are tomato paste and crushed tomatoes respectively. Neither sauce has any added water. It should also be noted that both of these alternatives have about one third of the sodium that this sauce has per serving.  Bottom Line While the preparation was easy and the resulting dish was reasonably good, for us it was not enough new and different for us to use this product instead of our favorite barbecue sauce. Overall score: just short of 3.5 stars.

product_title: McCormick Skillet Sauce Chili
review_headline: Real spices, good texture, Tex-Mex taste.
review_body:
I make my own enchilada sauce, and this tastes reminiscent of what I make by hand. It has a good thick texture that holds up well in cooking, with occasional discernible bits of onion in it. It uses tomato puree, which I'm not totally thrilled about, but it's fine if you need a premade taco sauce and you're okay with it tasting like something out of a lunchroom. It doesn't require much cooking at all--just heat it up and through and serve it.

They are correct; this makes an excellent taco salad as well, though I think it'd work better with a little more ground beef. I don't see any reason why this couldn't be used with ground turkey or chicken, either. It'd work anywhere you use enchilada sauce or taco sauce. I think it'd also make a fine Tex-Mex condiment like those packets of taco sauce one gets from chain fast-food restaurants.

Ingredients: water, tomato puree, spices, garlic, onion, modified corn starch, salt, sugar, lactic acid, citric acid. 25 calories, 1g sugar, 320mg sodium, <1g protein, 0g fat. I was a little weirded out by the inclusion of sugar in this preparation as well. The packaging is a soft-sided plastic envelope like one of those Capri-Sun juice packets; though the pic makes it look like there's a screwcap on the right side, there isn't. You just tear off the corner of the envelope and use it. I didn't have any trouble with the packaging either.

I will be looking out for the other varieties they offer of this sauce; it seems like it uses plain ingredients and quick, simple preparation to make fast, tasty meals. This is like an upscale version of the dry packet taco seasoning mix, and aside from some ingredients that I wouldn't normally use myself, it all looks pretty honest.

review_headline: Do some research on the first ingredient in this.
review_body:
First ingredient is organic brown rice syrup which apparently may contain high levels of arsenic.. Doing a quick search of this ingredient brings up some potential hazards...

What is Arsenic?

Arsenic is found in varying amounts in rock structures and in residue left over from when arsenic-based pesticides were legal. It cannot be created nor destroyed so what we have on Earth is what we’re stuck with forever. “Arsenic hotspots” like Bangladesh, have dangerously high concentrations of arsenic in rock structures, and therefore, water supplies and soil.

Rice is naturally better able to assimilate arsenic, more so than wheat or other grains. Brown rice, used in brown rice syrup, has high concentrations of arsenic because the outer shell is still intact, where in white rice, it’s removed.

Inorganic Versus Organic Arsenic

And then there’s inorganic versus organic arsenic. According to the FDA, “There are two general types of arsenic: organic and inorganic. The inorganic forms of arsenic are the harmful forms, while the organic forms of arsenic are essentially harmless.” This is because the body absorbs inorganic arsenic and urinates out organic arsenic. However, some scientific studies have shown that dimethylarsinic acid (DMA) and monomethylarsonic acid (MMA), two organic forms of arsenic may also be a health hazard. Inorganic arsenic is more dangerous because the body actually absorbs it. Inorganic arsenic is what’s found in the water supply, that’s why it’s carefully regulated. Water is tested constantly to ensure it’s at safe levels no higher than 10 ppb. Well water, on the hand, is not tested.
Arsenic/Brown Rice Syrup Takeaway

Here’s my take: Rice, especially brown rice, absorbs arsenic from the soil. There’s not too much you can do about that. But you can take steps to minimize your risk. The Consumer Reports study notes that rice grown in the U.S. has heightened levels of arsenic when comparedto rice grown in India and Thailand, though arsenic was found in samples from all over the world. As a result, until arsenic levels in rice and other foods are regulated by the FDA, only use brown rice syrup in moderation.

After doing a lot of research it just seems like even the supposedly good baby formulas still could potentially contain harmful ingredients. The only formulas I've been able to find that seem to be free and clear of most harmful ingredients are made over in Europe.

product_title: Suja Juice Fresh Start Program
review_headline: eh...Just OK, as far as juice cleanses go
review_body: Dear fellow buyers,  these are reviews of the product, not reviews of juice cleanses in general or for posting of your personal health diaries.  There are many message-boards and forums for the latter.  That said, the quality of these juices ismarginal.  I'm sure they are cold-pressed and organic, but the primary juice in most every one is Apple Juice.  Apple juice is the cheapest juice and has only limited nutrients, as compared to Kale, Celery, Carrot and various other premium juices.  All of these juices taste pretty sweet (to an experienced juicer at least), which is another sign they are mostly just apple juice.  If you go to your local juicer (they are most places nowadays), you will find the green juices that are predominately greens, (e.g. Kale, Collards, etc.) are quite pungent, intense and bitter.  It takes some getting used to but it is far more nutritious than just apple juice.  This stuff is OK for a 3-day cleanse, I suppose, but I wouldn't recommend going longer than that on this program.  This may not be the best juice cleanse, but it is a fast, quick, easy juice cleanse for the masses.

product_title: Ginger People - Gin Gins Chewy Ginger Candy Original
review_headline: This is the one to beat!
review_body:
As a fan of ginger beers, ginger ales, ginger drops, and ginger chews (but NOT ginger bread or boys), I have no trouble awarding Gin-Gins a "high-five.". It's clearly the "best of breed" for the following reasons: 1. individual wrappers prevent drying-out of the candy yet are quick and easy to tear apart; 2. each candy is sprinkled with a light, powdered sugar to prevent sticking of the candy to the paper wrapper; 3. the individual candies are not so small that 2-3 pieces are unsatisfying nor so big that a single piece needs to be trimmed to a mouth-sized morsel; 4. the texture is as close to perfection as it gets--chewy (satisfying that oral instinct) without being sticky; rubbery but yielding to the mouth's digestive juices prior to being perceived as a foreign invader.

Finally, the most important feature deserving commendation--taste. The ginger is plenty spicy and "hot" but not so much that it neutralizes or, in effect, burns away, the taste buds for the next half-minute (a complaint I have against extreme hot pepper sauces like Mclhenny's Tobasco Sauce). Ginger should never be so hot that eating it becomes the heroic act of a masochist. I can't buy the notion that the therapeutic benefits attributed to ginger increase with the displeasure, or even pain, of eating it. Gin Gins have an agreeable but temporary "burn" that disappears in time for the taste of ginger to emerge as a clear winner.

In short, upper-scale ginger candy for the discerning palate.

The only reservation one might have about Gin Gins might be their relatively high expense. But the individual who can limit his intake to no more than several per day will be generously repaid by a superior product. (Should they exhaust the budget too quickly, give JuJu Fruit candy a try--seriously. At best, you'll stay within budget; at worst, you'll set yourself up for renewed pleasure with your next order of ginger.)

review_body:
This was my second time ordering Viva Labs Organic Extra Virgin Coconut Oil. After my first jar of this oil was all gone, I decided to try coconut oil from Walmart. It was a little cheaper. However, it was inferior to Viva Labs. So, I gave my Walmart coconut oil to my sister, to use as a moisturizer. And, ordered the 54 ounce jar of Viva Labs coconut oil. This is the one I am sticking with. I use this oil in various ways:
1. To brush my teeth. I mix it with baking soda, and keep the mixture in a small container in the bathroom.
2. As a moisturizer "as is", or mixed with Shea butter.
3. Coffee enhancer. I add about one teaspoon to a large cup of coffee.
4. Hair conditioner. I rub the oil into my hair, and leave on for a couple of hours or overnight. First I scoop a heaping teaspoon into my hand, and let the warmth of my hand almost liquify the oil.
5. To brush my dogs' teeth. They enjoy the taste, so they tolerate having their teeth brushed a lot easier.
6. Good for our and my dogs' health, so I give them a teaspoon of the coconut oil daily.
7. I've used this coconut oil as a base for homemade sunscreen.
8. I top hot popcorn with melted coconut oil and salt.
9. I've cooked with coconut oil (instead of butter or other oil). Both on top of the stove and in the microwave. This coconut oil does not smoke in the pan.
Viva Labs is the company I'm sticking with for my coconut oil.

product_title: Healthworks Chia Seeds 3lb 6lb Parent
review_headline: Awesome deal for this little superfood!
review_body:
I've been eating chia seeds for about 2 years now; mainly in chia pudding, but also in chia jam (using the chia gel in place of pectin), in smoothies, or in my low-carb version of oatmeal, or, as I like to call it, "Fauxtmeal". I used to only be able to find chia seeds at stores like Whole Foods, where I had no choice but to pay the Whole Foods price. Recently, chia seeds are EVERYWHERE, from Walgreens to Wal-Mart.

Even stores like Wal-Mart can't beat HealthWorks price. I've bought the cacao powder from HealthWorks before and been completely satisfied, and the same is true for the chia seeds. I like that they are pesticide/chemical-free, and the price is impossible to beat, even when buying chia seeds from the bulk bins at local natural shops.

The resealable package is nice, but I keep my chia seeds in a wide-mouth quart mason jar with a plastic screw lid. That being said, the seal on the bag is nice and strong, and the plastic material thick, so don't be afraid of spills.

Pro tip: If you ever spill chia pudding/gel all over your clothes, scrape as much off as possible before tossing everything in the washer/dryer. These little buggers get EVERYWHERE and are a colossal pain to fish out of the dryer trap.

product_title: Gourmesso Flavors - Nespresso compatible flavored coffee capsules
review_headline: Try these if you love chocolate
review_body:
Gourmesso offer a large range of coffee blends, graded for intensity from 3 to 10. I have now sampled twelve varieties and there isn't one I did not like. Even their Decaf tastes great. Personally, I prefer their strongest blends because I am used to Italian coffee, especially first thing in the morning, but my friends are very pleased with the medium-body choices that we have been discovering. All the flavoured varieties (called Soffio, or Breath in Italian) are of Intensity 5, with a well-balanced medium body, full of flavour but very smooth and easy to take. The beans are mostly Arabica with some Robusta to give added body. This Soffio Cioccolato variety was a pleasant surprise for someone like me, crazy about chocolate. I half expected it to be too bland, but the chocolate character is there, nicely added to a good base of velvety coffee. A great choice with a chocolate-based dessert.

Each package contains five pouches of two individual capsules, sealed in foil. You cannot go wrong with dosage and preparation and the capsules work perfectly in Nespresso brand machines. The Gourmesso brand was quite a discovery, especially given the comparatively low price. These flavoured coffee blends are distinctive and different but the they still taste of coffee, which is very important to me. It's also good to see the Fairtrade logo, reminding us that commerce does not have to be heartless. I can easily recommend these flavoured capsules to anyone who enjoys a slightly decadent coffee experience, and some variety in their espresso or cappuccino fix.

review_body:

They are harmful for young kids and boring for older kids. Not one of the 4 kids taking part in the Easter Egg hunt liked these so they were all thrown out.
Save your money and fill your own plastic eggs with stickers, jelly beans, or party favor toys. Or at the very least buy eggs with good reviews. I made the mistake of thinking brand name (Oriental Trading) was worth paying more because I would get a better product. NOT SO!

product_title: Jus By Julie 3 Day Blended Juice Cleanse with Free *Overnight Shipping
review_body:
I got this through a groupon. I split it with my friend and we both paid $125 each for a 3 day cleanse (that included shipping). The juices came cold and seem to be packaged thoughtfully. I have to be honest though, the only juice I liked was the choco-nana dinner juice (or was it peanut butter?). The rest were waaay too mouth puckeringly sweet. Also, I was really hungry for most of the time and got a little light headed regularly. I bike commute so I guess I needed a few more calories than they provide. I supplemented with a few pea pods, an apple, and a few nuts (felt like I really needed protein). Still, the juices are high quality and if you like really tart/sweet things, you might be able to stomach them.

I will not do this again. I need to eat every few hours or I get spacey so this just did not cut it. I'm just sticking to raw food cleanses in the future!

product_title: Chocolate Salted Butter Caramels Gift Tin (Caramels de France) by La Maison d’Armorine
review_body:
Melt in your mouth caramels; as a kid we had very few caramels so I learned to let them linger in my mouth for hours. As a codger I still do. These held their shape and their flavor for over two hours -- wonderful.

These caramels were included in the Paris Box sold by trytheworld.com. Apparently Amazon does not sell this subscription service to boxes of foods from different countries, but based on this box and a box of Moroccan foods, I can recommend trytheworld highly.

trytheworld writes: "This delectable recipe was born in the summer of 1946 when the French celebrated the return to leisure at the beach in Brittany. Maison d'Armorine makes these salted butter caramels using Breton butter and Brittany's famous fleur de sel. For any French gourmand, each bite of these chewy caramels evokes childhood memories of seaside holidays."

The house has a marvelous website with many interesting factoids; I love Google's translation of certain passages:

"The quality of different specialties based on natural materials (cane, Breton salted butter, sea salt ...) and some trade secrets (old copper cauldrons ...) that artisans have been passed from generation to generation.

"A tradition narrated by Academician Hervé Bazin in his novel "matrimony": "Render unto Niniche what is Niniche and to Caesar what is due to him." [The joke is based on this factoid from Wikipedia: " The niniche Quiberon is a small lollipop round all in length, made ​​by La Maison d'Armorine since 1946 at Quiberon , was awarded best candy in France in 1946."]

"And taste buds, for sure, no mistake ... 60 years after the creation of the family business in Quiberon, time seems to have stopped in the small échope installed facing the ocean, where almost nothing has changed ... " .maison-armorine.com/

"The New York Times" carried a charming story on caramels from Brittany in early 2014; nytimes.com/2014/01/19/travel/a-salty-sweet-buttery-taste-of-brittany.html:

We didn’t come for the miles of shoreline, the promise of seafood feasts or the many history-rich towns. Even the dramatic views and craggy cliffs weren’t a draw. There was only one thing that lured my husband, Mahir, and me to Brittany in northwestern France: salted butter caramel candies.

Sweets have always tested my resistance, but salted butter caramels have left me defenseless since I first tasted them in a Paris shop selling handmade candies more than a decade ago.

There’s no shortage of salted caramel iterations in my hometown, New York City. What was once an exotic-sounding indulgence now seems ubiquitous, from salted caramel chocolate bars sold at the corner drugstore to restaurants offering their rendition of it in cakes, ice creams and sauces.

But the original buttery wrapped candies that I fell hard for, called caramels au beurre salé, originated in Brittany, and I decided to enjoy them in their most authentic form in the place they were born.

With a population of 3.2 million in an area that’s roughly 13,000 square miles, Brittany hugs the Atlantic Ocean and is famous for its beaches and picturesque coastline. Our visit was concentrated around the Lorient area on the southern coast, which has several notable caramel candy shops.

Eating handmade caramels in Brittany is a longstanding ritual in France, according to the New York-based French pastry chef François Payard, who grew up in Nice. “I remember visiting the area in the summer with my family as a young boy, and everyone used to visit their favorite caramel shops to have the candies,” he said. “Nowadays, very few of them still exist.”

He was right. We found bakeries, stores and restaurants selling caramels, but no caramel-only spots. Even the establishments that started off exclusively selling candies haveexpanded to cookies and other sweets. I also discovered that making salted caramel candies the old-fashioned way by hand is a laborious process that only a handful of candy makers have maintained, and machines have intervened as interest in these treats has become global.

Our goal was to try to find caramels where taste wasn’t compromised by relying too much on modern technology. The superior ones were rich on the palate with their quality ingredients, luxuriously velvety and just slightly sticky, and our search led us to five places where offering them in their best version possible is a priority.

The first caramel maker we met, Maelig Georgelin, owns the elegant patisserie Au Petit Prince in the tiny village of Étel and handcrafts every step. His old-school methodology might suggest that his is a longtime endeavor, but the 30-year-old is one of a few young pastry chefs in Brittany who are reviving an increasingly rare craft.

When we walked in the door of the compact shop, we were greeted by a case of refined desserts behind glass — macarons, napoleons and assorted cakes — along with a line of people waiting to buy them. We had an appointment with Mr. Georgelin and expected to do a tasting and interview, but he had other plans.

“Instead of telling you about my caramels, I thought I would have you help me make them,” he said as he led us to his kitchen on the second floor. He told us that although the chefs creating caramels usually have their own techniques, most caramel candy recipes have the same steps and ingredients: the region’s famous salted butter, heavy cream, sugar, glucose and sometimes vanilla extract and a hint of fleur de sel, also from the area. “It’s the quality of cream, whether it’s regular or double fat, and the cooking temperature of the mixture, that’s the difference between caramels,” he said.

He said he believes that using double cream with 30 percent fat from a small dairy nearby and having the patience to heat the butter, cream and sugar to 230 degrees is what sets the 1,500 caramels he makes a year apart from others. Stirring the sugar until it transformed into a gooey, clear mixture was the first step before we added the other ingredients, and as Mahir and I took turns stirring over Mr. Georgelin’s tiny stove for more than a half-hour, the aroma of the bubbling mixture became intoxicating. “I grew up making caramels with my mother in our kitchen; it’s the only way I know how, and I want to preserve this integrity in my work,” he said.

Spreading the mixture on cookie sheets and evening it out with a spatula follows, and then a one-day cooling in the refrigerator. Then, Mr. Georgelin and one other employee do the cutting and wrapping by hand. The slightly irregularly shaped pieces with their imperfect clear wrapping served to us by their beaming creator were especially tempting. And, with their creamy feel and finish, their taste was a highlight of the trip.

Our next stop was Kerjeanne, a large and uninspiring-looking bakery in the village of Belz that is a 15-minute drive from Étel. Here, locals hurry in to pick up Breton specialties like butter biscuits and cakes, and half the shop is lined with tacky mugs and key chains to entice tourists. Emmanuel Dumaire, 50, purchased the store in 2008 from the family who started it 50 years ago, and he employs Lydia Justum, 45, who was one of the first caramel candy makers when Kerjeanne began making them in 1985. The difference is that she now has gadgets to help her out.

Although she heats the sugar over a small stove top and also cuts manually with a knife, an electric mixer heated to 210 degrees and a wrapping machine speed up the process. “I’m trying to stay as true to the old way as much as I can, but I was spending hours on just the wrapping and blending, so the machines help me a lot,” she said.

Her homemadehandiwork wasn’t lacking in taste — the candy was chewy but not overly so and had an agreeable, slightly crunchy texture with bits of sugar that had not completely melted down.

We spent much of the next day in the resort town of Quiberon, which is known for its numerous caramel shops and is a scenic 45-minute drive from Belz along the coastline in thick beach traffic. Although salted caramels have been a part of Brittany’s culture for more than a half-century — one of the oldest shops, La Maison Guella in Cancale in the north, opened in 1920 — the 60-year-old La Maison d’Armorine, based in Quiberon, is one of the names credited with popularizing them in the last decade.

Raymond Audebert started the business as a beach stand selling salted caramel candies and eventually opened a still-thriving storefront that faces the ocean and has a very old-fashioned feel with light wooden floors and walls and vintage candy tins lining the shelves. Mr. Audebert has since died, and his grandson Alain, 58, runs La Maison d’Armorine, which has expanded considerably since its early days and relies on machines to produce 30 million pieces a year. The work happens in a facility in Quiberon, where visitors can watch the several dozen workers through large glass windows execute the mixing in heated copper machines and the cutting and wrapping in another machine.

Gildas Peron, the sales director, emphasized that although the homespun touch wasn’t there, the company uses only the best butter, cream and other ingredients it can find. “What we use is what you would find in your grandmother’s kitchen in the country,” he said. The flavor certainly wasn’t lacking: The candies were especially creamy and, thanks to good fleur de sel, weren’t overwhelmingly sweet the way so many cheaply made wrapped caramels can be.

On our visit to Quiberon, we also stopped in at Henri Le Roux’s chic store on a quieter street away from masses of people on the beach. Mr. Le Roux, now retired, started off as a chocolatier in 1977 but created caramel candies after developing an affinity for Brittany’s salted butter. This turned into a machine-made endeavor in 1988, and the company was purchased by the Japanese cookie company Yoku Moku in 2006, but his signature product wasn’t less pleasurable for the change of hands. The caramels stood out from the others we tried because of their crushed almonds, hazelnuts and walnuts, which made for an appealing combination of crunchy and smooth.

An unexpected caramel discovery came on our last day when we were on the back patio of our countryside hotel, Château de Locguénolé in Kervignac, enjoying the panorama of expansive forest. Olivier Beurne, the executive chef of the property’s Michelin-starred restaurant, walked by and asked if we had yet tried the caramel candies he makes for guests. We were aware of his talents with French cuisine but not with caramels.

He led us into the large kitchen, where a cookie sheet tray of the candies was sitting on the counter. He cut off a piece, still slightly warm, handed it to us — and the most decadent, sweet butter with just a touch of welcoming saltiness melted on our tongues. “I only make them when I have time, but I don’t want to lose the by-hand tradition,” he said.

product_title: Marathon Bar (Curly Wurly)- Bag of 20 bars by Indulgence
review_body:
I live in the states - that unfortunate place where the citizens are subjected to Cadbury chocolate made by Hershey's, thinking that they're eating UK Cadbury. So laughable. The difference between Cadbury and Cadbury by Hershey's is night and day. It's the difference between water and salt water. It rather looks the same, but the taste tells you that something is dreadfully wrong. And there's no way around it, supposedly. Unless one goes to a specialty store or brings it over the pond themselves, finding true Cadbury is next to impossible. The creme egg, the mini eggs, the dairy milk bar... Hershey's. Yuck!

And then there is this guy: The Curly Wurly bar

I first heard of Curly Wurly bars through the BBC (Vicar of Dibley). Extremely glad that I did! This is one of a handful of Cadbury chocolate that I can get that is made in the UK and shipped to the US. I will never buy my Cadbury from Hershey's ever again. I don't know what those maniacs did to the recipe, but one lick is enough to propel someone into a diabetic coma.

The chocolate in this bar is sweet, but not too sweet. It's smooth. Subtle. I dare say "sexy". It forces you to savor it as it molests your senses with its delicate deliciousness. Do not get me started on the caramel lattice work. YUM! Buttery. Luscious. Sweet, but not over-powering.

I bought these bars for my husband, who has only ever had Cadbury by Hershey's. I honestly wish I had video taped that moment when I dropped a bit of it in his mouth. He, quite literally, had a choco-gasm. Ladies and gents, we have a convert!

I love the fact that I got these bars for less than a dollar each and that they arrived 10 days ahead of schedule. The arrival time was between April 22 and May 5th (I believe). I ordered them I think the 24th of March. The bars arrived today, April 10th. Being that they are shipping from the UK, I find that extraordinary. I really didn't expect them so soon. They came VERY well packaged, wrapped snuggly in British newspaper (which is extra awesome. And I swear even their newspaper is made of finer quality paper.) Someone took the time to gently wrap these bars so that they arrived in as good condition as possible. And the box size was a perfect fit. The seller really does put a lot of thought into the item being sent - something else one rarely gets in the US. Will definitely be purchasing again in the future! And from only this seller.

product_title: Oscar Mayer, Thick Cut, Fully Cooked Bacon, 2.52oz Box (Pack of 4)
review_headline: Very Good, But An Expensive Way To Buy Bacon.
review_body:
Oscar Mayer, Thick Cut, Fully Cooked Bacon, 2.52oz Box (71g) (Pack of 4), by Oscar Mayer.
I just started buying this Oscar Mayer bacon variety, because the Hormel Microwavable uncooked bacon slices in four heavy plastic packages of four slices, is no longer available in my local Star Market. These Oscar Mayer bacon slices are listed as “Thick Cut”, but in reality, the cooked bacon is about the same thickness as the regular bacon slice that you would get after cooking a slice from an average one pound package of bacon. (The Oscar Mayer Original Fully Cooked Bacon is almost paper thin.) These slices are cooked about two thirds of the way through, a long ways from crispy, and are more like cold cuts. To make them even slightly crispy, you will still have to cook them in a microwave or frying pan, but you will eliminate most of the greasy bacon smoke and grease spatter. At Star, the Oscar Mayer 2.52 ounce package of Fully Cooked Thick Cut Bacon was $3.99, while the uncooked one pound package of Oscar Mayer Thick Cut Bacon was $6.99 for about 6.4 times as much bacon. You definitely have to pay a lot more than you would have to pay for a pound of uncooked bacon slices, but that is the price you pay for convenience. The pre-cooked bacon itself is reasonably lean, and tastes very good. Each slice contains about 125mg of Sodium (salt). I like four slices per serving, and at 500mg, that is about the same amount of salt that you would find in an average hotdog. That is still a lot of salt, and anyone on a low salt diet may want to restrict themselves to one or two slices per serving. Thankfully, this variety is not flavored with sugar. Processed foods in general contain far too much salt and sugar than is good for our health.

product_title: Baby's Only Organic Dairy with DHA & ARA Formula, 12.7 Ounce
review_headline: TLDR: Best "organic" option for baby formula on the market.
review_body:
After reading about how Earth's Best gets their DHA and ARA, I couldn't give it to my son anymore. It's really a shame that corporate greed and profit trumps providing a quality product in today's world. Even those entrusted to safeguard public welfare turn a blind eye to matters of irresponsible behavior. All we can really do is educate ourselves and vote with our dollars.

I did the best I could reading up on the various "organic" offerings for baby formula. The one concern about Baby's only is that it's listed as "Toddler's formula" to get around guidelines for baby formula. The company says it's their belief that a baby should have one year of breast feeding. As much as we would've prefered that ourselves it just was not an option. Another is the test that showed higher levels of arsenic in their brown rice syrup than recommended. This has seemingly been addressed.

Even with these concerns, Baby's only is the best option in the market in my opinion. My son enjoys it and while he is still under one year of age has no issue digesting it. We currently have 10 containers shipped a month via Amazon subscription. The containers themselves are small and I will warn you to watch your hand on the inside lip as I've been cut by it.

product_title: NAT VAL BKFST BSC Breakfast Biscuit, Blueberry, 8.85 oz
review_headline: Crunch-chewy - but they taste too manufactured to me
review_body:
I am a big fan of the Nature Valley Granola bars. The granola bars have been around for along time. Now one of the trends (and it seems like Belvita was on the cutting edge) is to make these breakfast biscuits. Pocket sized and protein packed cookie-like snacks that are posited as breakfast substitutes. The concept is great for people on the move or who won't take the time for a more substantial breakfast.

The biscuits themselves are what I would call "crunch-chewy". They are not completely crunchy or completely chewy. This variety seems overtaken by blueberries that although they fall near the bottom of the ingredient list smell and taste like they should be near the top. Honestly though, this blueberry flavor and the texture of these seem far too manufactured for me. Truth be told, I am a huge fan of the Belvita varieties anf find that these do not live up to them. They look similar but taste totally different.

In the future, I would take a pass on these and stick with Belvita (both the crunchy and soft variety) or Nature Valley's Granola Bars.

product_title: Typhoo Decaf 80 Bags 3 Pack
review_headline: Great Decaf Option for Tea Lovers
review_body:
My cardiologist told me to lay off the caffeine, so I desperately went about trying to make a proper pitcher of strong, sweet iced tea, per my Southern Midwest upbringing requirements, without the caffeine.

I got pretty close -- I was using Twinings Decaf Irish Breakfast Tea up until now -- but it was never quite the same. To me, decaf just always seems to be... lacking. On a whim I went looking for better/stronger options. That is how I first learned about Typhoo, and was thrilled to find it on Amazon.

For a decaf option, this is definitely the best I have found yet. It brews up strong and dark, with no bitterness. I have served it at many dinner occasions to date, and it has passed muster every time. In fact, my boyfriend drank it for months and was very surprised to discover it had been decaf all along.

I still want to give PG Tips Decaf a whirl, but this bulk pack ensures I will be swimming in Typhoo for quite awhile... ah well!

product_title: SalsaCrazy Habanero Salsa - Dominate the Dance Floor Habanero Salsa Hot Sauce,16 fl oz.
review_body:
Habanero peppers are one of my favorite foods – it used to be jalapenos, but once I discovered the spicy-sweet flavor of habaneros, there was no going back. I live up north (aka the land of "we don't like flavor"), so it can be challenging to find habanero products in stores around here - so I'm very grateful that this habanero salsa is available (and I don't even have to get out of my pajamas to get it!)

This salsa has a heat index listing of 9 out of 10 – in other words, have the milk close at hand for this one! I think I'm pretty tough when it comes to spicy food, but this one had me reaching for the milk after the third or fourth bite. Not that I'm complaining, mind you! If you like heat in your food, you're going to LOVE this salsa! This is a thicker, chunky style of salsa (just the way I like it), and I love the inclusion of corn, which I haven't seen in the salsas I've purchased off the shelf at the grocery store. The corn adds a great touch of sweetness to the fiery flavor of the peppers, it's SO good!

This salsa is great with tortilla chips, but you know what I liked even better? Using it as a cheeseburger topping! ). The heat is less extreme when you eat the salsa this way, so it's a great way to give a burger a kick without overheating more sensitive palates. I'm going to try it as a blackened chicken topping next!

I received this product in exchange for my honest review; all opinions are my own.

I'm very impressed. It smells wonderful, exactly as you would expect 100% almonds to smell. The consistency is like fine corn meal, with a pleasant texture, not crunchy or grainy but somehow richer and moister than wheat flour.

I like wheat flour, so I'm not going to knock it. This Almond Flour is very good, and just a completely different experience than wheat.

This is packed in a very sturdy, thick plastic bag with a self-sealing ziplock top, so it's reusable and you can leave it in its original bag without worrying about humidity or bugs.

Sample sent for testing and impartial review. I'm totally pleased with this. Because it's rich, its best use may be as a partial substitution for other flours, or as a flavoring. Delicious stuff.
