product_title: Back To Nature Non GMO
review_headline: not my favorite Back to Nature crackers
review_body:
I've had a couple of other kinds of Back to Nature crackers and liked them. This kind tastes good, but isn't my favorite type because of the nutrition.

These have a fairly simple ingredients list (allowing for the fact that the flour they use is enriched). I do wish they were whole grain, but they're not, and as a result, they don't have a lot of fiber or protein. They do have 230 mg of sodium per serving, which seems high. They taste a little salty and would be much better with savory spreads/toppings (unless you're going for that salty-sweet combination that's been popular lately). You can see the full ingredients list and nutrition facts panel in the product images.

These are maybe a touch oily on the outside but it doesn't really transfer to the fingers. They're pretty thin and have a nice crunch (I think they're supposed to be kind of like healthier Wheat Thins or something). I ate them with natural peanut butter (the kind you get out of the grinder at Whole Foods) and that was a wonderful combination.

There were a lot of broken crackers in the box, unfortunately. If you have dietary restrictions, these are vegan and kosher. These are peanut and tree nut and dairy free and are manufactured in nut-free facilities, so you should be safe eating them if you have a nut allergy. Obviously they're wheat crackers so they contain gluten.

In the end, while these did taste pretty good, I probably won't buy them again because I prefer to consume whole grain crackers instead. If the whole grain/nutrition aren't as important to you, you may find you really like these.

review_headline: The absolute best tasting gluten free pasta ever!
review_body: Barilla's gluten free Rotini is by far the best tasting best texture gluten free pasta!  I have a lot of experience with wheat and gluten free pasta's.  I started eating wheat free back in the 90's long before gluten free became trendy and I was eating quinoa before most people had even heard of it. Back then it was very hard to find wheat free foods. I was put on an allergy free diet by a doctor after finding I had many food allergies.  Now back to this pasta.  The taste is as close to regular pasta as you can get.  Most rice pastas are gluey and gloss, and corn pastas need to be rinsed very well because the pasta is swimming in corn starch.  Somehow Barilla has made this pasta which is a combination of white rice and corn flours without those unpleasant problems.  I have found you can even cook 2 boxes at once without any starch overflow from the pot.  Also this pasta does not quickly overcook like most gluten free pastas do.  The package says it is a product of Italy and made in a gluten free facility.  Unfortunately my allergies have only gotten worse over the years and I now sneeze my head of and my nose runs like crazy when I eat rice so I can no longer eat this pasta.  If you aren't allergic to rice or corn I highly recommend Barilla's gluten free pasta to anyone on a wheat or gluten free diet.

product_title: Yellow Split Peas
review_headline: Looks like yellow corn and is high in lutein and zeaxanthin like yellow corn
review_body: This product is slightly less delicious than yellow corn but these yellow peas are quite delicious - delicious enough.  Both yellow corn and yellow peas are high in the carotenoids, lutein and zeaxanthin, which have been shown to greatly benefit eye health in humans.  By contrast, green peas are high in several forms of lutein but do not contain any zeaxanthin.  Both green peas and yellow peas are much healthier for us to eat than yellow corn, which is slightly healthier for us to eat than white corn because yellow corn is much higher in carotenoids than white corn.  The main reason that peas are much healthier for us to eat than corn is that both green peas and yellow peas are legumes.  Real populations of real people who eat any species of legumes have been shown to be much, much healthier than people who don't eat any legumes.  The 2nd reason is that peas are much less likely to contain cancer-causing mycotoxins (such as aflatoxins, fumonisins, ochratoxins, zearalenone, patulin, citrinin, ergot alkaloids, and tricothecenes) from pathogenic molds (such as Aspergillus and Fusarium) than corn.  When compared against green peas, yellow peas taste quite different - yellow peas have a more fruity, ripened taste than green peas.  Also, green peas tend to always be infected by fungi called, white mildew (white spots), but yellow peas tend not to have this problem.

review_body: If you enjoy this chocolate the way all high-quality chocolate should be enjoyed (let it melt slowly in your mouth), the slightly-smokey mild-to-medium-spicy chili and deep dark chocolate flavors meld perfectly without requiring other flavors to make it delicious.  I typically prefer 70-85% chocolate (not too sweet).  Some chili bars add cinnamon and/or orange flavors and are usually sweeter (55-60% cacao).  While that's nice sometimes, this bar is the one I prefer when true dark chocolate is on my mind.  It melts smoothly without the waxy feeling like some bars have.  FYI, you can probably find this bar for less (around $8) at your local Whole Foods.  BTW, if you want your mouth to burn thoroughly, eat some good Thai food, not chocolate.  I've had spicier bars, and the spice simply overwhelmed the chocolate flavor--why pay for chocolate that you can't even taste?

product_title: Twinings
review_headline: Not the same as the last box I ordered, not as good.
review_body:
I've been drinking this exact tea for about 2 years now. As such, we've been buying this bulk box for that long, as both my husband and I are big fans. So, it was a surprise to me when we needed to reorder the box, that everything seems to have changed. The packaging is completely different for the individual tea bags and as another noted, the box isn't wrapped in plastic as before. The individual teas are now wrapped up with their tag in the wrapping paper, something I've only seen done in American tea brands. It might seem little, but it's annoying to have to carefully tear the edges of the tag so I can have something to dip by.

I also found the tea to be seriously lacking in flavor. I'm someone who prefers their tea strong, and Twinning English Breakfast was by far the easiest to make this way. It brewed very quickly, and was quickly a strong tea if left just a little longer. I now have to brew twice as long as before just to get it close to the way it was, just one box before. I then went to rebrew used bags, 2 of them mind you, and I ended up having to just throw them away it was so weak. It tasted gross to be more precise. I'm VERY disappointed, as this my 'good 'ol stand by', of all my teas. Now, it's no better. I'm actually going to write Twinnings, which if I remember correctly, might be the same company as Nestle tea, 'Nestea' brand, which i personally also find gross.

product_title: Barilla Veggie Elbow Pasta
review_body:
I'll tell it too you straight--I like to try weird food. And this definitely qualifies. Even just the concept of this "veggie pasta" is just bizarre. What does it say about us as a species that we have to trick ourselves into vegetables by hiding them as something else? It makes me laugh, and I want to try it.

As you can see from the box, this is carrots, squash, and tomato mashed into instant pasta. According to the box, that makes up to 25% vegetable in each noodle. Obviously there is nothing natural about this process--this is food born from a laboratory. If you are looking for healthy eating you are 100% better off just making a tasty pasta dish with these same tasty vegetables. But hey, that's not why we're here, right?

The pasta takes longer to cook, and is more gummy than usual instant pasta. The taste is different; I couldn't identify any particular vegetable taste although if you read the reviews everyone seems to spot something different. I'm marking that up to the placebo effect personally. I bet if you served these blind few people would be able to identify the ingredients. The flavor interferes with the sauce, so you aren't going to want a light sauce with this. If you have a nice heavy sauce it will mask both the gumminess and the odd taste.

It was fun to try these. Almost like the Star Trek food I imagined as a kid. But they aren't tasty enough to try twice, and the health benefits are dubious. You are far better off just eating your vegetables!

product_title: Tea Beyond Tea Samplers
review_headline: Love the Tea, Love the Pot
review_body:
I received this combo box of Tea Beyond teas for review, along with their glass teapot and infuser with the pink butterfly on the lid. I must admit that they had me at the butterfly. The little teapot holds two good-size cups, which is about what each flower can do well. The instructions say that you can pour a second batch of water over (carefully to not disturb the flower), but I think the delicate flavor was lost on a second batch. It's OK if you just use it to warm say half a cup of the first batch. There is great play value in watching the flower unfurl in an all-glass pot. The aroma is lightly perfumed and the flavor is like a delicate green tea. I was not able to discern much difference in flavor among the various \\"flower buds\\" but I thought they were all lovely, and am using them as a treat for myself or to share with a friend, since my husband doesn't like green tea.

I really liked the loose teas - Jasmine Green, Black Caramel and Black Earl Gray. They were all made of whole leaves, with no tea dust - really high quality. Because of this, they may need to steep a bit longer than most people may be used to, but the resulting flavor is clean, fresh, aromatic and rewarding. My English husband prefers a more robust flavor, so he will stick with the Earl Gray, which had lemon peel in it, rather than the oil of bergamot that most people associate with it. I thought it was pleasant but not memorable and not really what I think of as Earl Gray. My favorites were the Jasmine green tea and Caramel Black.

Getting back to the teapot - it wasn't just about the pink butterfly, which, by the way, you need to hold down when you pour or the lid will fly away. It is just a great little pot for one or two cups. It is well-designed with a no-drip spout, feels comfortable in the hand when you pour, and because the infuser is glass as well it will always be clean and not affect the flavor. I like being able to watch it to see when it is brewed, and you can also watch the little tea flowers bloom. It is definitely going to my best friends next Christmas, with the tea of course.little tea flowers bloom. It is definitely going to my best friends next Christmas, with the tea of course.

product_title: Taste Nirvana Juice, Coco Aloe, 16.2 Ounce (Pack of 12)PLUS FREE BONUS 1PC PENCIL POUCH
review_headline: BEST Coconut Water by far! 7 Brands Reviewed Below.
review_body:
I have tried many different coconut waters, and Taste Nirvana Coco Aloe is by far the best tasting and most refreshing! I get light-headed when I'm working too hard. I sit down, sip on the coconut water, and by replacing my electrolytes, I am back on my feet in 30 minutes. What a difference this has made in my life!
For reference, here are the coconut waters I have tried, and a ranking of how they taste. Hopefully this will be helpful:
Taste Nirvana Coco Aloe ($23.99 regular price or $22.12 Subscribe & Save for 12-16.2 ounce cans): light and refreshing with small, sweet pieces of aloe pulp. Didn't think I'd like the pulp, but it is delicious! Also, I much prefer the 16 oz. metal cans to the 11 oz. cardboard cans.
Taste Nirvana Real Coconut Water ($29.06 reg. or $24.70 Subscribe & Save for 12-16.2 oz. cans): Same delicious and refreshing taste as above, but it's more expensive than the Coco Aloe and the aloe pulp adds a sweet and refreshing taste to the coconut water, so I would stick with the Coco Aloe.
Vita Coco Coconut Water ($15.52 regular price or $13.19 on Subscribe and Save for 12-11.01 oz. cardboard boxes): Authentic, slightly sweet taste. Great price, especially if you buy monthly. I'm not a fan of the cardboard containers, but Vita Coco tastes almost as good as Taste Nirvana. I usually have one of each daily, and save the Vita Coco for moments that an 11 ounce drink would be satisfying.
Vita Coco Cafe Latte ($32.31 reg. or $27.46 Subscribe & Save for 12-11.1 oz. cardboard boxes): As a coffee lover, thought I might like the taste, which is similar to bottled Starbucks drinks, but I didn't like it enough to order again, especially at that price.
O.N.E. Coconut Water, Natural Flavor ($23.88 reg. or $20.30 Subscribe & Save for 12-16.9 oz. cardboard containers): This order arrived with dents in the box, so the cardboard tops were pushed in and the flaps lifted up on some. None spilled though. The flavor is pleasant, but has a mildstarchy taste to it. Pleasant flavor, but not as good as Taste Nirvana or Vita Coco.
Wai Koko 100% Pure Coconut Water ($25.99 for 12-17.5 oz. metal cans): This company takes pride in their Polynesian history, and the part that coconut water played in keeping hunters hydrated. I decided to try their coconut water and was very disappointed. This tastes like the starchy liquid surrounding canned corn. I can't describe it better. I have had fresh coconut milk in Puerto Rico (a man shimmied up a coconut tree with a machete between his teeth, cut down a ripe coconut, came down, cut the top off and handed me the coconut with a straw. Even at tropical temperatures, the coconut water (or milk) has a distinct slightly sweet taste that quenches your thirst and fills you up. Wai Koko's coconut water tastes nothing like fresh coconut, nor like any Amazon or supermarket brand I have purchased. I opened a second can to make sure that the first one wasn't spoiled, but they were the same. Starchy and undrinkable. O.N.E. coconut water has a mild starchy taste that is slightly similar, but only a slight hint of that flavor. I do not know whether coconuts grown in Hawaii taste that different from coconuts grown in Thailand, for example, where many coconut waters are made, but I would not order Wai Koko again.
Coco Libre Pure Organic Coconut Water, Natural flavor ($28 for 12-11 ounce cardboard boxes): I tried it because it is organic, but the price is too high for 11 ounces, and they do not offer a Subscribe & Save 15% discount. It has a very mild, pleasant taste, but I prefer the overall flavor or Taste Nirvana Coco Aloe. And although buying organic is appealing to me, for the amount of coconut water that we drink each month, it is just too expensive for the smaller size, and the taste isn't quite as good as I would expect for something that I drink daily.

product_title: Baron's Kosher 100% Pure Ground Sesame Tahini 16-ounce Jars (Pack of 2)
review_headline: The most delicious tahini I've ever had
review_body:
This is the best tahini I've ever had. I've had other tahinis, some directly from the Middle East (via friends), and some purchased in the grocery store. What I don't like about those is that they totally separate, and you've got concrete on the bottom and oil on top. It's always hard to get it mixed back up. This brand was mixed, no separation. It's a thinner tahini; I don't know what they did to make it so much better. And the flavor...omg. I always liked tahini IN things or as the base of dressings, but never to take a bite. I also don't like peanut butter. But I had to restrain myself from just eating it...it was that delicious. (Eating a spoonful like people do with peanut butter.) It's thinner than peanut butter, which isn't my experience of twenty plus years of using tahini. But I LOVE this consistency. So much easier to work with. Seriously, this stuff is the best ever, and I don't think I'll ever use another brand unless Amazon stops selling it.

I did have an unfortunate issue, but I didn't reflect that in my five-star rating. Both jars were leaking. Slowly. It took me forever to realize that both jars were leaking because I had them sitting side by side in the pantry. I would pick the open one up to get some tahini, and there would be a puddle of stuff. I kept thinking I was somehow not getting the lid on correctly, but eventually I realized both were leaking. The unopened one, I finally discovered, has a vertical slice, like it was done with a carton opener (but it's so perfectly straight, I think it had to be by machine). I can't find the hole in the second one, so it's got to be a pinhole somewhere. I think this was just a freak occurrence, bad luck. And Amazon did a fine job of making it right...I've returned the two jars and have another set ordered. Amazon expedited the shipping on it.

review_headline: Crunchy and salty + Nutella = delightful snack ....

So I jumped at the chance to try one of my favorite snacks in a new way: a little packable pack complete with pretzel sticks. You get a dozen or so crispy pretzel sticks that work perfectly to scoop out the chocolate-y/hazel nutty goodness. The combination of the slightly salty pretzel sticks with the smooth creamy Nutella spread just works.

These are NOT terribly \\"diet friendly,\\" though -- the small pack contains 270 calories, so it's not the kind of things I can enjoy too often. But for a planned special treat, it will work. At least I won't be tempted to overindulge since the portion is controlled by the packaging.

review_headline: Great, if you know what you are getting into...
review_body: I will get to detailed opinions of Lavazza's dark roast Gran Filtro coffee, but first here is the summary:  Fantastic coffee that is slightly over roasted.  It is GREAT but not perfect like the normal Gran Filtro.  I bought this 2 pound bag after having tried and LOVED Lavazza's regular Gran Filtro coffee for my daily pour-over brew.  The regular roast hashints of caramel which are absolutely fantastic.  Overall, the flavor is an almost perfect balance of nuts, subtle spice, and wonderful sweet caramel.  These seem to be the same beans just roasted a little more. This dark intense roast has a slight burnt taste to it.  Much like you would taste in a *$ brew.  All this to say, do not over-brew this coffee.  Stick with a coarse grind which will allow for a shorter brew time.  Now, if you want coffee perfection, then go with the original Gran Filtro.  You cannot get any bitter taste no matter how fine the grounds nor how hot your brew water is.  That blend is coffee perfection!  On the other hand, if you are used to a darker brew and have a taste for some slight bitterness - then this dark roasted Lavazza will likely be a step-up from what you are used to.  I will be drinking and enjoying all 2 pounds of this coffee one cup at a time.  Let me know if you have any questions.

review_headline: The Many Things You Can Do With A Wonderbag
review_body:
I use it more than I thought I would. Different type of cooking but it works just like a crock pot. The rule of thumb, if you can cook it in your crock pot you can cook it in the Wonderbag. I can actually cook more in the Wonderbag than I can in the crockpot like rice, it comes out perfect in the Wonderbag. You can also use it to keep items cold. Don't bother getting the cookbook that is on Amazon for the Wonderbag a cookbook just as good comes with it and there's so much more recipes on the internet. When looking for recipes also look at themal cooker recipes, it's the same concept. This is big so you need a place to store it, the Wonderbag isn't something that folds up. I keep mine on top of the fridge, it looks pretty good there, adds a pop of color in my kitchen.
Other uses for a Wonderbag.
Cooks, keeps things warm, heat things up, keeps things cold. On the road cooking, have a long car trip, throw some meat and veggies in the Wonderbag and cook it on your way there. Use it to store yarn, or plastic bags when not in use. Show it off like a kitchen decoration. I raise my bread in my Wonderbag. It's a cat magnet. Have fun with it.
Please feel free to add any other uses for the Wonderbag I may have missed. Lets see how many things the Wonderbag can do.

product_title: Butler Soy Curls
review_body:
Some context on who I am, so you know what kind of tastebuds are reviewing this product. I *was* vegetarian for a long time, but that was years ago. The past three weeks I've been trying out veganism to the best of my ability. Over the years, I've tried everything to help with eating tofu. I've frozen it, pressed it, seasoned, deep fried, and marinated it. It still tastes bland and is sometimes almost tolerable. Seitan, on the other hand, has better texture, but doesn't agree with me.

I found a local vegan diner who had these on their menu. I kept seeing them mentioned but had no idea what they were. Attached to the diner was a grocery store and I bought these as a splurge with low expectations. They looked like fritos, they were so stiff and crunchy looking. That night I looked them up online and followed directions from their website. I meal prepped and threw them in vegan pho, curry, and stir fry.

They absorbed some water and their crunchy, hard texture turned soft, but not too soft. Imagine really fluffy chicken. Maybe something akin to a mcnugget, but before it was battered and fried? They absorbed flavor appropriately when cooked. It didn't fall apart like tofu does, you actually have to chew it. It's not tough by any means, but it has some darn texture thank goodness.

I have only cooked these in somewhat soupy recipes, so I have full confidence that these curls do well in that environment. I have yet to grill or batter and fry them, but I bet they taste pretty good battered too. The website suggests fajitas and I think that will be my next endeavor. I only added a few to each meal for the week, but now that I have confidence in them, I'm going to make them more of a star of the meals.

I can't think of any drawback to cooking with these other than cost, perhaps. However, each bag contains 8 servings and I think that's on the money for what you need as part of a main dish with lots of veggies. This is, however, the best meat replacement I have tried--especially for something that you can easily make at home.

product_title: Nutiva Organic Hempseed Oil
review_body:
I bought this oil because I've been researching hemp oil for anxiety and depression. I received it about 4 days ago and have been taking a teaspoon- a teaspoon and a half every night for 4 days. (Everything I've read up on suggests starting in small doses and working up to a tablespoon every day to see how it affects you.)

Taste wise, it's certainly not a bad taste, but it is STRONG! It's a very herbal, earthy, nutty taste that definitely lingers. On the flip side, it's very easily disguised and covered up by other foods.

I am on 50 mg of Zoloft for anxiety and depression and wasn't sure how this would react with the Zoloft, so far no bad effects. The first night, after taking a tsp, about 30 minutes later, my self-deprecating thoughts seemed to lighten greatly. Maybe it was a placebo effect, maybe not.

Now, 4 days later, I definitely have more energy, and while still depressed, I feel like I can get up and accomplish things better than I could before. I feel like some of my brain fog has lifted and it's much easier to push away the self-deprecating thoughts. Perhaps this is working in tandem with my Zoloft? I just know I feel better, like I can deal with my depression better, and I'm only 4 days into taking this.

It's not going to cause any ill effects, so why not buy a bottle and try? I don't regret this purchase at all.

Oh, also, my anxiety seems to have lessened a bit as well.

product_title: 64oz Organic Whole Ground Golden Flaxseed Meal Bob's Red Mill (4 Pounds Total)
review_headline: A Good Deal on a Great Product!
review_body:
This is a great deal on Golden Flaxseed Meal! I use this product in all of my baked goods.

I replace from 1/4 to 1/3 of the flour with flaxseed meal in every loaf of bread that I bake, in all of my cakes, pastry and muffins. It gives my breads a little more texture and chewiness but more importantly, it adds to the flavor without changing it. I don't buy nuts because of the price but adding flaxseed meal gives baked goods a slightly "nutty" taste and I've never had it go stale or rancid on me.

This is a good way to add those omega 3's and fiber to your diet. I especially like Bob's Red Mill brand because of their overall quality. product_title: Gerber Good Start Soothe Powder Infant Formula
review_headline: It seemed like her GI problems just became worse
review_body: I have my life back!    To make a long story short, after a couple of days in the NICU after my little one was born, she was addicted to bottles and refused to nurse.  Furthermore, due to a cesarean section, despite my pumping efforts, I have never been able to pump what she needs so I have no choice but to supplement with formula.    We started with Similac for Supplementation and when she was having gas and constipation during her first week of life, we switched to Similac Sensitive.  I know this works for many babies, but not mine.  It seemed like her GI problems just became worse.  We tried prune, pear and apple juices (per our pediatrician's recommendation) but still, nothing worked.  Frustrated, I did some homework and found that this product might be what we were looking for.    We have only been using Gerber Good Start Soothe for 24 hours but our lives have already changed.  We were so fed up with the constant straining and crying that our poor baby was enduring that we bought this formula late at night and gave her 2 ounces when we came home, then put her to bed.  She, for the first time in a very long time, slept in.  She did not spend the entire next morning grunting and crying like she usually does and tonight, she had her first bowel movement in 4 days.  There has been no fussiness at all today.    Like I said, I know every baby is different but if you are struggling with finding the right formula for your little one, I'd recommend giving this one a try!    Review update - 9 days later:    I no longer think that this formula is a miracle but I DO still think it is great and it is what we will continue to feed our baby as a supplement to breast milk.  As it turns out, it did not help our little one with her constipation, rather, it was a coincidence that she was able to go to the bathroom shortly after starting on it.  We are still working with her pediatrician to help her with that but it seems we've found a solution.  Also, it is true that the formuladoes not mix very well or very easily.  There are usually chunks of formula in her bottle that I struggle with, which is annoying.  Other than that, I'd still recommend it because it DOES help with our baby's gas.  She is still sleeping better and is not always crying out in pain.  Our pediatrician said that it is a good product so we'll continue on with it.

product_title: Simply 7 Pomegranate Chips
review_body:
These are odd. They're a lot like potato chips (first two ingredients are potato flour and potato starch) but they're pink and they have a slightly fruity flavor. I don't hate them, but I don't love them either, and if I am going to eat potato chips, I think I would prefer something without the fruit.

There's nothing particularly pomegranate-like about the flavor, it's more of a generic fruit flavor to me (there is some added sugar, as well). The nutrition information is available in one of the product images; these are rather high in fat and have no fiber and very little protein -- they're mostly starch. Sodium is not bad (130 mg) for chips, but there's really no nutrition in these. (Also, for what it's worth, I would guess most of the color is coming from the beet powder in these, as opposed to the pomegranate.)

These are vegan, kosher, and gluten-free, if any of those are important to you. I do appreciate the all natural ingredients and lack of preservatives. However, I'm just really not a fan. There are healthier snacks out there.

product_title: Bulksupplements Pure Stevia Powder
review_headline: and again it is good stuff. I have an old Kal brand container ...
review_body:
bought it again, and again it is good stuff. I have an old Kal brand container that I pour it into for use at work, and another Kal brand container I pour it into at home. Those containers are 1.3 oz each, and this bag (100g) is 3.5 oz. Well more than enough for two containers that'd be far more than the price of this bag. The taste is also quality! I use two of the little scoops (I have two of them, not sure if this comes with it or not) which tastes about like I put two teaspoons of sugar into my coffee. by the way, the 90% part isn't how much stevia is in it, it's how much of a concentration of stevia extract it is. (not using the right terms, but yeah) It's next to impossible to get 100%.

So everyone knows, the reviews saying how it's bad because it doesn't dilute in their beverage is a little post-haste. Stevia doesn't dilute well in cold beverages unless it's stirred very well. It does dilute though, it just takes effort. The chemically taste people talk about? That happens when you use far too much, or you drop it directly on your tongue. It's an intense sweet taste, don't expect it to be exactly like sugar.

product_title: Krusteaz Light & Crispy Belgian Waffle Mix, 28 Ounce ( Pack of 4 )
review_headline: Butter is the key to tasty waffles!  Review contains helpful hints.
review_body:
You won't find a better mix! Use 1 1/2 C mix, 2/3 C water, 1 egg and 3T oil per 3 belgian waffles.

Hints-

Mix well and let it sit for about 5 minutes to incorporate some air into it. Then scoop into the mix without disturbing it and pour on ready iron. If you have trouble with the mix pouring out the sides there isn't enough air in the mix meaning you either didn't wait long enough to let it rise or you're stirring or disturbing the mix too much when scooping out the batter.

If you don't have a timer on your iron, wait until steaming decreases to remove waffle.

If you really want a tasty waffle, don't even think about using oil. Melted butter tastes 100% better and releases much easier than oil.

Put them in a warm oven with the door cracked open to keep them crispy while continuing to cook them.

A 28 oz box makes 10 7" waffles according to the directions. I have the Waring pro double waffle iron and one box makes 12 waffles.

product_title: Delba Famous German Pumpernickel Bread, 16.75 Ounce (Pack of 12)
review_body:
I just recently found these breads by chance. I was at a Wegman's (grocery store in NY) and they were out of my favorite bread by Dimpflmeier Bakery (a great Toronto bakery with old world breads). I went to the international section and found Mestemacher. The familiar bricks of bread were there and I didn't want regular yeast bread. I tried this type of bread before but was disappointed with the texture. That's what throws people off initially, sometimes for good. My mistake, I didn't toast it. This bread is not that good cold (or even room temp). You can eat it this way, but it tends to be very crumbly. The solution is simple, toast it, a toaster oven is best. I use the dark setting, but toast to your liking. Toasting binds the bread together and the problem with being crumbly disappears.

The next issue is using this bread as a sandwich. If you look at the picture on the package, they don't treat it as a traditional two-slice sandwich. That's because it works a lot better as a single layer.

Toppings. I'm enjoying experimenting with what tastes good on this bread. Some people like it with butter, but I'm not really a fan. I read a review where someone recommended a single layer of lunchmeat with no condiments. So far that's been the best, that and with a couple of slices of tomato. I've tried cream cheese, pimiento spread, butter, and sliced cheese. So far the single layer of lunch meat (pastrami in my case) was perfect. It adds a little moisture. The bread and meat go perfectly together. I'd never try that with regular bread, but you don't need it with this Westphalian style bread.

I've now tried my Feldkamp Pumpernickel. It costs more than the Mestemacher and I have to say I don't have a preference between the two pumpernickels, except for the price. The Mestemacher is a lot cheaper, especially if you plan to make this part of your diet (which I do). Don't get me wrong, the Feldkamp tastes great. If they were the same price I wouldbuy the Feldkamp. It may have a little more pronounced pumpernickel aroma. I say may because I couldn't tell for sure.

I may continue to buy Dimpflmeier Bakery Klosterbrot locally, but Mestemacher and Feldkamp are going to be in my pantry from now on. The advantages are too large to ignore. No preservatives, high in protein and fiber, whole grain, low gluten, and long shelf life (unopened). Since it's preservative free you have to store it in the fridge and use it within four of five days. It has a 6 to 12 month shelf life unopened. That's the ultimate in convenience and a good reason to buy through subscribe and save.

The last and most important reason to buy this bread is simple, it tastes fantastic.

product_title: Hot Tamales, 4.5 pounds Fierce cinnamon
review_headline: UGH! Make sure you read the ingredients!
review_body:
I had the urge for some cinnamon hard candies and found none at my local supermarket. However, there were the Hot Tamales, basically cinnamon-flavored jelly beans. Have always like them, so I got a box. What a mistake! THEY ARE AWFUL! There is no hint of cinnamon taste what so ever, just a peppery heat. And, if you read the ingredients you will see why: "Sugar, corn syrup, modified food starch. Contains less than 0.5% of the following: Artificial flavors, medium chain triglycerides, carnauba wax, fruit juice from concentrate, (pear, orange, strawberry, cherry, lime, lemon) sodium citrate, pectin, citric acid, malic acid, fumaric acid, red #40, yellow #5, (tartrazine) yellow #6, red#3,blue#1" Oh and it's gluten-free!
It should be gluten-free, as there is very little in this list of chemical products that are related to food in any way. Rather, they're more like a high school chemistry project gone wrong. How about carnauba wax? You will find that in Simonize car polish (and a very good polish it is!) and in furniture polish too. Medium chain triglyceride? Found in horse milk - OK if you're a horse I guess.

So why did they have to mess with the hot tamales? Cost. It’s cheaper to have a tanker truck pull up to your factory and dump off a load of chemicals than to pay for good natural flavors.

product_title: Dechunxian China Top Ten Famous Teas
review_headline: Drink One of China's Favorite Teas
review_body:
Environment is crucial to tea drinking. A beautiful place, a wondrous brew calms and nurtures the spirit.

When I lived in Tucson Arizona, I had the good luck to be able to drink wonderful tea in a Chinese Tea Shop called Seven Cups on 6th Avenue. During my short time in the city, I was happy to experience Cloud-fog tea--an everyday Chinese tea that was so popular in its native country it rarely made it out of China.

The area where it is grown is the Lushan Mountain area in the Jiangxi Province where a perpetual cloud hangs over the landscape--this misty climate slow-grows and hydrates the tea bushes resulting in leaves that are filled with abundant plant chlorophyll and sweet/unusual flavor development.

The Cloud-fog tea has a buttery flavor that may be reminiscent of asparagus sprouts--however, do not over kill this tea with too hot water--it will become bitter. Rich with tannins and Vitamin C, it requires delicate handling--water temp around 140 degrees--abbreviated seep time. Sip and savor.

Happily, this interesting tea is now available through Amazon! Recommended.

I combined a bag of this with a bag of their calming tea (since I was stressing about being sick) and by the end of the cup I seriously felt like a different person. I'm still under a blanket, and I still don't feel 100%, but now I can focus on things other than how miserable I'm feeling. If you feel a cold coming on, seriously try this out.

product_title: GoGo squeeZ Applesauce on the Go, Apple Raspberry Lemon Twist, 3.2-Ounce Portable BPA-Free Pouches,(12 Boxes with 4 Portable BPA-Free Pouches Each)
review_headline: SAFETY CONCERN with corners of pouches!  Actual product is great, but packaging needs immediate improvement!
review_body:
The product itself, I give 5 stars. These are great on-the-go healthy snacks for kids and adults alike. This is one thing I can ALWAYS get my picky preschooler to agree to. I order these in bulk with Subscribe & Save. Much cheaper than in grocery stores.

I deducted stars because I have an extreme SAFETY CONCERN in regards to the corners of the packets. They are manufactured to have rounded corners, but I have been "knicked" more than once by sharp pieces that splinter off of the should-be-rounded corners. This happened when I was opening the boxes and removing the packets from the box to place in the fridge.

After tending to a minor puncture wound that bled slightly, I inspected all of the packets from all of the boxes I ordered. Almost all of the packets had this problem. Some at the top of the packet, others around the bottom. Please see photos for details. Although it doesn't look like much, it is extremely sharp and feels like a needle! It can puncture and scratch skin to a point where minor bleeding occurs.

I trimmed the sharp "splinters" off of all the packets before giving them to my son. I thought this might have been a manufacturing defect with one order, but I have been experiencing the problem over and over with multiple orders. I even bought a box of GoGo Squeez at the grocery store to check the packaging quality, and those packets also had the sharp edges. I haven't had this type of problem with any other brands of squeezable products (Plum Organics, Happy tot, etc.)

I hope that GoGo Squeez checks their Amazon reviews. I noticed that the company did change their caps (used to be a small cylindrical cap, now looks like a small airplane propeller) and I can assume they did so due to concern over choking hazards. Even after changing the cap design, they still include a warning on the back of the packet. They also include contact information on every packet. They seem like a company that does care about consumers and desires feedback regarding their product. I will e-mail them regarding this issue and update my review after hearing back from them.

*******UPDATE****** 1-17-15
I contacted GoGo SqueeZ and sent them photos of my packets. They were prompt and professional in their response. They apologized for the defective items I received and offered to replace them. I will continue to purchase this product & I will post updates if the problem with jagged edges continues.

*******UPDATE******* 4-20-15
GoGo SqueeZ has awesome customer service and I did receive a box of replacement product as promised. Sadly, the packs continue to have the same problem with the "pokey edge." I would estimate that approximately 20% of the pouches I purchase have a noticeable puncture risk. I always go through the box and round off the edges with a pair of scissors. The product itself is great, and the customer service was helpful. I also appreciated their willingness to send a replacement box. The defect with the packaging is not enough to turn me off of GoGo SqueeZ, I just really hope that whenever it comes time to evaluate/replace/upgrade the manufacturing machines (or presses? or basically whatever seals the packages together in the production line) whoever is in charge of quality control makes the necessary tweaks to help the package corners be more safely rounded. Until then, I handle the pouches more cautiously and hope that my review has helped others prevent any punctures! Take care.sires feedback regarding their product. product_title: KIND Healthy Grains Bars Healthy Grains Bars
review_body:
I like the KIND bars because they are non-GMO, gluten-free, and they avoid food dyes, unsafe preservatives (they use vitamin E instead), and contain no natural or artificial flavoring.

I have tried KIND bars in five different flavors:

Vanilla Blueberry
Dark Chocolate Chunk
Peanut Butter Dark Chocolate
Maple Pumpkin Seeds
Oats and Honey with Toasted Coconut

Of these flavors, I like Maple Pumpkin Seeds and this flavor, Oats and Honey, the best because they taste, to me, like oatmeal cookies. I liked the ones containing chocolate second best, and the blueberry least. I have grown so used to the taste of these bars, I no longer like Kashi meal bars, which had been my favorites before discovering the KIND bars.

These bars may seem to some a bit dry, but I personally like the texture, because I like the combination of chewy and crunchy.

Note that the suggested retail price for these bars is $4.99, and anything above that price is unreasonable. They can be found online as low as $3.29, and quite commonly at $3.99.

Ingredients: Whole grains (gluten-free oats, brown rice, millet, gluten-free oat flour, buckwheat, amaranth, quinoa), tapioca syrup, evaporated cane juice, honey, coconut, non-GMO canola oil, brown rice syrup, gum acacia, sea salt, natural vitamin E.

Allergen Information: Made in a facility that uses peanuts, tree nuts, soy and sesame seeds.

Nutrition Facts:

Fat 4 grams (no trans fats)
Carbohydrates 25 grams (sugars 7 grams, fiber 3 grams)
Protein: 3 grams

Calories: 150 (minus 12 calories for fiber, net 138)

product_title: Monster Energy Drink
review_headline: Good product, shifty delivery (and packing). I may end my automated reordering.
review_body:
The drink itself is good. Its is citrus-y but tastes extremely sweet. Its like drink pancake syrup. I sip it and since the can contains 2 servings (read the label) I don't feel so bad for being a girl and sipping it for an hour or so while working. My biggest issue is delivery.

UPS ===
My first order was via UPS. I had no problems and the box itself was delivered in pretty good shape. I wish that Amazon would have added more padding than just putting it in a box with 6 inches above with absolutely no fill. boxes always get stacked funny during shipment and some cans were dented. No real biggie.

USPS ===
My second order was a disaster. I had the same packing as UPS so its typical for Amazon. Both (2) boxes were ripped, soaked and both shipments were handled such that 2 cans in each delivery burst. Of course now we have weakened boxing and sweet syrup over all the other cans. Many cans are dented badly so those will be first to be consumed. At least my carrier put them in plastic trash bags as she didn't want sticky all over her van. I had to physically wash all the cans due to the ruptures. Thanks USPS!

product_title: Baby’s Only Organic LactoRelief with DHA & ARA Toddler Formula
review_headline: Formula changed so daughter hates it now ;-p
review_body:
April 2016 Update:

I had given Baby's Only LactoRelief a 5 star review but had to come back and change that since they changed their formula to add DHA & ARA. We were part of Amazon's subscribe and save program so we would get regular deliveries of this formula for our daughter. The Amazon website still displays the original can but all the shipments we got were for the new formula. I'm annoyed with Baby's Only for eliminating the regular LactoRelief completely, instead of just introducing a LactoRelief with DHA & ARA as an additional formula option. I had left a message with Nature's One the makers of Baby's Only and actually go a call back from their customer service department. They were really nice and helpful in recommending the Soy formula since it is the closest in taste to the original LactoRelief. They even offered to send a free sample of their Soy formula for my daughter to try. Hoping it will be a suitable substitute.

My daughter has a milk protein allergy. She was on Allimentum at first but hated the taste so much that she refused to eat most of the time. We then switched to Nutramigen, she seemed to tolerate the taste at first but after a week she started to refuse it as well. We were pretty frustrated since she needed to improve her weight gain. Allimentum and Nutramigen was suppose to be better for her digestion, but it didn't help if she refused to drink them. That is when we decided to try Baby's Only LactoRelief, it had a mild smell like flour or oatmeal, at least that was what it smelled like to us. It was also mildly sweet like rice cereal so our daughter really took well to it. She has now been on the LactoRelief formula for almost 2 months without issue. Of course every baby is different but thus far this has worked great for our child. We mix the formula with bottled water (room temperature) since tap water, even filtered still seems to have issues allowing the formula powder to dissolve easily. I would suggest pre-scooping the desired amount of formula in a bottle and just mixing with bottled water when needed. We like that better than premixing the complete formula, since that means you have to store it in the fridge, and than having to reheat it when needed, which thickens the formula and makes it less appetizing for the baby.ping the desired amount of formula in a bottle and just mixing with bottled water when needed. product_title: Melitta Java Jig, Reusable K-Cups for Keurig K-Cup Brewers, Uses Melitta Paper Coffee Filters,2 cups and 30 filters
review_headline: Cheaply made, but works well--with a bit of practice
review_body:
Well this item works as promised but there is a bit of a learning curve.
1. Getting the filter onto the base was a problem at the beginning. You see, the filters come nearly flat out of the box making it nearly impossible to get right. I kept putting it on off centered. I finally found that turning the inner plastic piece upside down, putting the filter over it, HOLDING ONTO THE FILTER with two fingers, and finally pushing the outer plastic piece on top worked. I'm going to make a video when I have some time.

2. Once your coffee is done and it's time to dump the grinds, it becomes nearly impossible to remove the lid. The plastic is so very thin and the seal so very tight, a strong fingernail or a knife was needed to remove it. After slicing my finger I looked for a better way. I then turned the cup upside down, and pushed the lid off from the bottom. That worked well.

Now, this product is cheaply made. It looks like less than a penny of plasic was used to make this. By weight, the disposables have more plastic than this reusable. I'm sure that one of these days, I will accidentally crush it. Still, it does make a good cup of coffee. I hope it lasts a year or two!

One last thing. I have never had any filters pierced as others have. Perhaps that was an older design.

product_title: Premium Grade Black Tapioca Pearls (6.6 lb) [Bubble Tea]
review_headline: I love boba, and if you can get these at ...
review_body:
I love boba, and if you can get these at a decent price, great (as a person on a limited budget, I find it problematic when I pay $22 for a product, and the next day, it's only $12. Amazon doesn't *do* price adjustments.)

Also, because these come vacuum packed, you're not going to have 6.6lb of *usable* boba - a significant portion will crumble when you open the package and are pouring things out of the bag. If you attempt to use the partial-pearls or dust when cooking the boba, they'll turn into slime, which is bad. Instead, I use a pasta strainer to separate out the dust, and use the tapioca powder as a thickener in my other cooking (as I can't eat wheat flour anyways. Waste not, want not!)

While it's a bit more expensive, if you're looking for quality boba that won't crumble and is more dependable, my favorite brand is WuFu Yuan. 9oz bags are about $4.50.

product_title: Ferrero Rocher
review_body:
The first time that I tried this product was about 15 years ago on Xmas day. They were one of my favourite chocolates back then and after 15 years of trying newer chocolates these remain as one of my favourites.

The Gold Ferrero Rocher is made of a a whole hazelnut surrounded by delicious layers of crispy wafer, a creamy filling, smooth milk chocolate and finely chopped hazelnut pieces. They taste very full of flavour with luxurious taste and a perfect texture which makes them melt in your mouth very quickly and easily.

You can get this product in different sizes and they also do 2 other flavours but they are not as nice as the original but worth trying:

- Brown = Ferrero Rondnoir - A delicious combination of tastes and textures from fine wafer and rich creamy cocoa fillingto a dark chocolate covered hazelnut at its heart (The Brown is much harder and has an unique and satisfying taste once you crack the hard hazelnut centre).

- White: Confetteria Raffaello - Delicate layers of wafer, an elegant creamy centre and a toasted almond, all finished with a sprinkling of coconut (The White is much soften and has a really nice coconut and cream flavour).

I usually have these every Xmas for the family and they don't last very long. If you haven't tried them before I would recommend them.

review_body:
I purchased this locally on a whim after seeing the glowing reviews on amazon. I generally prefer to make my own coffee with fresh grounds, but I was looking for something quick for when I'm on the road. After playing chemist and mixing to exact proportions of a rounded teaspoon per 3 oz of water, I gave it a try. It smelled like coffee while mixing, except the taste was more like hot dogs mixed with coffee in a blender. Perhaps the other reviewers are hot dog fans? I personally did not like the kind of hot dog aftertaste. Which is strange because I love to get pure espresso from the coffee shops in my area and have never found one I didn't like or was at least palatable. I made a few more cups with varying amounts of powder hoping to get different results. I think if it were more of a hickory bacon flavor I would like it more. Otherwise, there are better powdered coffee mixes out there that taste like actual espresso.

Since there are so many glowing reviews, I will do my due diligence and purchase a second bottle from amazon and see if maybe I got a bad batch. Otherwise, only hot dog fans need apply.

product_title: Bakers & Chefs Bread Flour - 25 lb. bag
review_headline: BREAD flour is NOT all purpose flour
review_body:
It is important to note that this NOT an all-purpose flour.

Here in Indiana, we plant wheat it the fall and harvest it the following summer. It is good for cakes because it is a low-protein flour that stays sort. Out west they plant a different wheat that is high in protein. The gluten protein gets tough when it is exercised or unleaded.

Most of the flour you see in stores is all purpose flour, which is a blend of the two flours. Cake flour is often sold in 2-pound boxes, and you pay a premium for that. Bread flour tends to be more expensive because it is a specialty item. The BETTER FOR BREAD brand costs about twice what all purpose flour sells for.

It is hard to get bread flout except for suppliers to bakeries, etc., and they like orders of a pallet or more of flour. Amazon pricing is rather competitive for single bag mail order flour, and this is an excellent bread flour. I wish Aldi carried 10-pound bags of bread flour but they do not and I cannot justify a membership at Costco any more, so this is about the best option. I save money by buying yeast in one pound bricks, but I put too much work into baking to use anything but the best flour, and I know of none much better.

product_title: Stash Tea Company Red Berry Rooibos Chanakara Herbal Tea for Chakra 1, 18 Count Tea Bags in Foil
review_headline: nice, flavorful rooibos that stands up to long brewing times
review_body:
I often make tea, bring it to my desk, and then forget to remove the tea bag. So I am used to having teas that are pretty strong and have been brewed for a long time. When you do that with this tea, the rooibos flavor predominates. (Early on, you can taste the berry flavor more.)

This does not get bitter and stands up to long brewing times. The mixture of flavors works well together and is maybe a little bit tart, so you could add a little bit of sweetener to this if you wanted. In my opinion, it works better as a hot tea than an iced tea, but I tend to think that of all rooibos teas. (So if you happen to like iced rooibos, you may end up enjoying this tea iced, anyway.) You don't absolutely have to have sweetener, though, if you don't want it.

It's a pretty reddish color and it has a standard rooibos aroma. It does include rose hips and hibiscus as the second or third ingredients; these are pretty standard in herbal teas. Rose hips should add a little vitamin C and hibiscus teas have been said to lower blood pressure in some people (when consumed in large quantities). So this may have a few health benefits if you drink a lot of it.

Overall, I like this and would definitely buy it again. It's a good, solid rooibos blend.

product_title: Kirkland Ito En Matcha Blend Japanese Green Tea, 1.5g tea bags
review_headline: Excellent Choice For Green Tea On The Go
review_body:
Many people drink green tea for the taste and health benefits. I started drinking matcha for the health benefits, but now drink green tea because I have also come to love the taste. Although this is not the same as consuming whole leaf matcha, it is still a delicious and healthy beverage. I like these tea bags because they combine sencha and matcha teas in great nylon tea bags which lets the water flow through them better than paper; it also allows some of the powdered tea solids to be consumed (you will see residue on the bottom of your cup when you're done.)

This mix of tea is relatively sweet when compared to traditional matcha, which I find to be a bonus, and it is eminently more portable and easy to use than traditional matcha powdered tea preparation. Each of the tea bags is sealed for freshness and the paper tab has a notch to suspend the bag securely from the side of the cup.

For the price and convenience these tea bags can't be beat. If you're looking for a more traditional matcha powered tea, I suggest trying DoMatcha Second Harvest Matcha. If you want green tea on the go, though, the Kirkland sencha and matcha blend tea bags are a tasty and healthy bargain.

product_title: San Francisco Bay One Cup
review_body:
**Star-rating changed due to most recent update. Was 4 stars.**

We love San Francisco Bay coffee in our house, and at the price of this item (120 cups for $40) no one else even comes close. The breakfast blend is the wife's, I drink the fog-chaser.

This is a tiny niggle and I only mention it as a caution to the future. We switched to San Francisco Bay coffee in February of 2014 because all the previous brands had steadily increased their prices to a point that made it more reasonable to go back to our french press.
Our initial batch of San Fran was stellar and the pricing was remarkable. We were so happy with the purchase that we went back next month to start a subscription and found that the espresso roast was no longer unavailable and the price on many of the other types had doubled.
Then in April, the price came back down for many San Fran varieties (but no more large cases of espresso roast). While the coffee was still excellent, it was clear that the packaging and cups themselves had changed. Since then there has been at least one more revision to lower-cost (re:quality) packaging.
I assume this is all to maintain the pricepoint, which I greatly appreciate. But because the price, quantity and availability are regularly in flux, I am forced to comparison shop every time I need coffee. A true 1st-world problem, I know. My real concern is that they will eventually reach a rock-bottom materials cost and then raise the price again. You have been advised.

**Dec 03 2014 update**
Well, it appears that San Fran Bay's quest to find cheaper materials has finally bled into the coffee. I regularly purchase the fog chaser because it is practically mud, while I get their light Breakfast Blend for the wife. The new box I received of fog chaser is basically like drinking water. No flavor, no consistency, just colored water.
Considering that in the past month I found an even better deal on the San Fran bay coffee (120 for$40) I should have made the logical deduction that they had further reduced their own costs. I will no longer be buying this coffee. I suppose if you're not a fan of strong coffee this would be an acceptable drink, but since Fog Chaser is described as 'full-bodied' and 'a real eye-opener', it's clearly not meant for or marketed toward them.

product_title: Numi Organic Tea
review_headline: With a unique & satisfying savory flavor, Toasted Rice is an unusual green tea that is a must-try for tea lovers
review_body:
Numi's Toasted Rice is a "brown rice tea" that is a mix of brown rice and green tea. This tea has both a savory aroma and flavor, which is slightly different from other Numi green teas I have had. It's such a unique flavor that I think it is a must-try for the avid tea lover.

Numi makes GREAT tea with some of the finest ingredients on planet Earth, utilizing natural & organic ingredients which are GMO-free and sourced from fair trade suppliers. They also utilize recycled materials in their packaging and shipping. Containing everything from the traditional to the unusual, Numi offers a wide variety of teas. When they make a tea, they don't settle for a flavor which is "okay" or "good," but rather pursue a flavor that is "great." Their Toasted Rice is no exception to this rule.

As I have not had other beverages that taste like Toasted Rice, it is difficult for me to describe it. It is a unique flavor in which there is a nutty, earthy, and smokey aspect, which are completely different from other green teas I have had. The rice itself does not make the tea taste like rice, but rather you can taste the green tea, but with a complex array of extra flavors not normally present in other green teas. If you add sugar, you get a flavor that manages to be both sweet AND savory. It's quite satisfying, and it pairs well with a wide variety of meals.

On a brewing note, I have read this type of rice tea tends to have the best flavors when the temp is hotter and the brew shorter. After playing around a bit, I am doing about a 45-60 second brew in water right around 200F. The attached image shows what this tea looks like when brewed that way, which as you can see doesn't look all that different from other green teas.

So for people who like tea, and especially green tea, Numi's Toasted Rice is a must-try. If you have not had brown rice tea before (like I hadn't), this is something that is very different, but likable. It's a nice tea to have to mix up flavors once in a while, and when one has a craving for a tea with savory properties. Like other Numi teas, it's on the more expensive side as far as teas go, but the slightly higher price tag gets a tea of exceptional quality, which to me justifies the price.ikable. product_title: V-fusion V8 + Energy Peach Mango Vegetable & Fruit Beverage Blend 48 OZ (Pack of 12)
review_body:
If you are wanting to get more vegetables in your diet, these fusion drinks which combine fruit juices with vegetable juices are a savvy way to do so. This peach mango mixes the juice of sweet potatoes, yellow tomatoes, and yellow carrots with the juice of white grapes, apples, oranges, peaches and mango puree. You really taste the peach-mango flavor with the other subtle flavors as nuances.

It is 100% juice with no ADDED sugar. However, it does include natural fruit sugar, as all juices do, which is part of the fruit juice - 26g sugar in a one cup serving. What I like to do is use about 1/8 cup - which would be about 3.5g of fruit sugar and 20 calories - and put it in a cup of seltzer with ice to make a refreshing and healthy drink. One cup of this fruit-vegetable fusion drink is 120 calories, but you can dilute it with seltzer to give it fizz and less calories for a refreshing, healthy and tasty beverage. It provides 100% of daily vitamin C and 20% vitamin A in one serving.

It's a great concept to mix fruit and vegetable juices in a healthy fusion drink like this which is naturally delicious. Of all the V8fusion drinks, this is one of my favorites. Mango and peach together are so refreshing and rather tropical tasting.

product_title: Fire Cider - Daily Apple Cider Vinegar and Honey
review_headline: Beware the nay-sayers, this is an INCREDIBLE product!
review_body:
When I first looked up Fire Cider on Amazon, I was shocked to find that it had such a low rating. I've been buying it locally and it is an AMAZING cold prevention. In fact, it's the only thing I've ever encountered that stopped a cold in its tracks after the stage where I was awake coughing all night with a scratchy throat.

I read the one-star reviews out of curiosity. I found that they are not about the actual product as much as they are about a controversy in the herbalist community because Shire City Herbals trademarked a name that herbalists consider generic. Amazon reviews are not the place to play politics. When I read an Amazon review, I want to know about the quality of the product. In that vein, let me tell you more.

When you think of medicine, you don't think "oh, that's going to taste yummy." Likewise, don't expect it here. While some people have said they enjoy the taste of this, I would have to describe the taste as "nasty!" It's hot, as the name indicates, and I can feel a burn as it goes down. However, it seems that "fire" is exactly what defeated the cold germs that were trying to take over my system. I've used Airborne and other cold prevention / immune boosters to try to stay healthy when everyone around me is getting sick. Fire Cider has been the most effective.

One of the complaints I've seen from the one-star reviewers and comments is that Fire Cider is "mass produced" and that you can make your own. Well, I could make my own soap, clothing, paper, etc. but I don't because, like many others, I lead a busy life doing things that I like to do. Why would I want to make a fire cider recipe that takes a month or longer, when Shire City Herbals makes a great product that has served me well? I want to spend my time with family and friends, not making something that I can easily buy from others. I truly don't care how the trademark fight comes out. I will continue to buy this product from Shire City Herbals no matter what it's called.

For the record, I have no connection with herbalists or with Shire City Herbals. My fiancé discovered this product at a local store and I used it out of desperation when I was coming down with a cold at the most inopportune time. The cold was thwarted and I am a true convert to this awesome product. Buy it and try some for yourself.

product_title: Choice Organic Teas, 16-Count Tea Bags (Pack of 6)
review_headline: Thanks Choice Tea for a great cup of tea!!
review_body:
First time I've had this tea and I am in love!!! As one that is typically seen with a cup of PG Tips or Tetley in hand I'm doing what many new tea drinkers do and expanding my knowledge base and taste in my favorite brews. Lapsang Souchong tea is a mellow, but not weak tea that with the smokey attribute is such a distinctive and flavorful tea; if you love your tea strong with an individualistic bend this is one to try! An old tea from centuries ago, one that will stay on my shelf. Since I use a large mug I might brew a strong pot or use two bags in my mug. Next is to switch to bulk leaf as I switch from tea bag to loose leaf anyway. My point is you might be like me and prefer a strong cuppa as opposed to the "lipton" cup of tea so the directions of one tea bag per 8oz for 3 - 5 minutes brew time is correct; a larger mug will require more tea. Well worth it.
Also this is my first time trying the Choice brand and I'm a new convert to this brand. To each their own; I've tried Twinnings and yes it is a great tea company and high quality tea and no I don't like it. I have tried to and I can not help it I do not like Twinnings Tea and never will. Not a bit deal; just not "my cuppa tea" :) I don't like other well know and loved tea brands; that's life! It's my taste I'm interested in pleasing and that's why there's more than one brand. I find Choice Tea a great tea and I like them. They make an honest, pure, well blended teas and I'll be buying more as I'm adding them to my 'first choice' of tea brands.
If you've been wondering about Russian Caravan Tea (Lapsang Souchong Tea) you may find Choice Tea the one you've been looking for! It's my tea now!

Thanks so much to the maker!

I had a really hard time with the skin and the toughness of the fins, and also the crunchiness of the bones. I had a really hard time stomaching sardines.

And then I discovered Crown Prince Skinless & Boneless Sardines in Olive Oil!!! I can't tell you how much better skinless and boneless sardines are! They are delicious and I'm confident with these little gems, I'll be able to work these into my diet. review_headline: At first I hated it. I bought it *before* I read about ...
review_body: At first I hated it. I bought it *before* I read about all the problems you can have but I figured out how to get around them, because I like very strong coffee without sludge and grounds in it. I found out if you put the filter on as directed and make sure it's high, it won't hit the little needle in the bottom of the Keurig brewing basket. product_title: Milkmakers Oatmeal Chocolate Chip Lactation Cookies
review_body:
The first time I ate these was purely for taste. I was not expecting them to affect my supply and quite frankly I didn't care whether they did or not. I thought it was a thoughtful gift and I'm not one to turn down a cookie. A few days later I couldn't figure out why I was pumping so much. And then.....duh. It hit me. Get your storage bags ready. They actually work! Pretty amazing!

Yes, they are 250 calories per cookie. And thank God for that. I usually have one in the mornings (to give my supply a jump start after baby has his big morning feed) with a banana and a glass of milk. Or sometimes a smoothie. And there's breakfast, done. Looking at calories by itself is such a small, very small part of the pie when it comes to nutrition. Be smart. Don't pair them with a donut and you'll be fine.

Yes, you could make your own, and for cheaper. You could also milk your own cow. And make your own bread. And ketchup. And jam, peanut butter, pasta sauce, pizza crust etc....you can make your own anything. I have a 3 yo, 2 yo and an 8 mo baby I'm trying to nurse til 12 months....I'm not exactly trying to be Martha Stewart these days. I'm trying to keep my family fed and healthy. There are foods that I buy instead of making for the sake of convenience - and for as long as I'm breastfeeding, milkmakers is on that list of things. I'll have time to make my own when I no longer need them. If you're not going to make them yourself, these are the very next best thing.

Another reason I buy these is because supporting any mom and her efforts in entrepreneurship is absolutely my jam. I've been trying to be more careful about where my dollars go lately. Knowing your farmer is important, but so is knowing who is behind anything else you buy - especially if it's on any consistent basis. So over the last 4 years, since my first babe was born - I've gotten to know the folks behind milk makers through customer service inquiries and questions on orders etc. Theseare good people who giving breastfeeding some awesome publicity and I'm happy to support that. Know your cookie maker, too!

Two tips for getting the most out of your cookie.....spread nut butter (any kind) on top. And enjoy them straight from the freezer to give them the perfect crunch, if you like crispy cookies. Y.U.M !!

With that said, my jif also has less sodium than pb2 and more protein.  I am not on a mission to lose weight...I need to build/maintain muscle.  This pb2...I have to admit...tends to curb my peanut butter craving...maybe b/c its roasted nut flavor is a bit overwhelming to me...I don't want anything to do with it - lol.  I normally use 1-2tbs of my jif in 2 shakes (each day)...and after it...I'm sometimes still hungry.  With pb2...that is not the case...I only use it in one shake per day...& it seems to curb food cravings...which isn't a bad thing if you're looking to lose weight. product_title: V8 Protein Shake (Pack of 24)
review_headline: Definitely not one that I'd run out for
review_body:
I have had my fair share of protein shakes from powders that I have bought at Costco (some aren't half bad) to pre-prepared shakes like Muscle Milk, etc.

I thought that a chocolate raspberry protein shake sounded intriguingly delicious.

It was decidedly NOT for me. Is it horrific? No, but I can definitely say that it would be more of an acquired taste for me. At first taste, it definitely came across more as a protein shake than as something that was chocolate. The raspberry was there, but almost as a slightly nauseating aftertaste that I got used to as it went down.

After making my way down, I definitely had the impression that this had to be artificially sweetened and was floored when I read 28 grams of sugar on the label. For something that tasted like this, it sure didn't taste like 28 grams of sugar (that's 7 tablespoons of sugar, folks)...certainly made me wonder at what point did the development team keep adding sugar before they held up their hand and shouted, "No, stop! Perfect!" It didn't seem that way.

I let my daughter have a sip and she reported that she liked it (hence the added star), but there is no chance that I'd be handing over a 28g sugar drink for her to consume on a regular basis. She liked it, however, so this might be to SOMEONE'S taste...just not mine.

This is definitely on my "don't recommend" list.

review_body: I'm a nutbar for the heat of capsaicin, having learned a long time ago that it opens the mouth's salivary glands for all flavors  --  sweet, salty, sour, bitter, and umami  --  and long ago having abandoned the chase for heat in favor of the search for flavor.  Tutto Calabria Hot Pepper Sauce was a spectacular find for me, flavorful itself as well as an enhancer for whatever else you think to put it on or in.  My favorites are simple  --  a slather with cheese & deli meats on a good bread, or half a teaspoonful stirred into a cup of soup  --  pretty much any soup.  Afraid of the heat? I prefer the non-instant version like [[ASIN:B0001AVTD6 Non-Instant Non Fat Milk Powder, 1lb.]] for use in yogurt making and bread baking.  If I've run out of non-fat milk for coffee, I can mix it in warm water with a whisk, then use my milk frother to create the foam I want.  If I wanted this for making a glass of milk for drinking, I'd probably go with the instant because it is faster to just give it a shake or stir.  My intent with this package is to use some of it for making hot cacao mix using [[ASIN:B00HES9CMS Viva Labs Organic Cacao Powder: Raw and Non-GMO, 1lb Bag]] and [[ASIN:B009324C0U Nutiva Organic Sugar, Coconut, 1 Pound (Pack of 3)]].  Mix it in hot water, add a little homemade vanilla extract, stick in the milk frother and enjoy the cold weather.  I store my milk powder in a glass jar with the expiration date on the label I attach to the lid.

product_title: Moorland Apiaries Honey in The Rough 16 oz. (Pack of 12)
review_headline: Excellent Virus protection, difficult to use
review_body:
In the past, this honey was absolutely "5 Stars", but then earlier in 2014 it started coming through with a plastic lid rather than a metal lid and at the same time the consistency changed from being spreadable with a knife (like butter) to being so solid that I can scarcely scrap it out of the jar with a spoon. I am so very disappointed because before the change, this honey was the *perfect* virus protection food!
Last October I had 2 sinus infections and just couldn't seem to get completely well, and since I had been hearing how beneficial raw honey can be, when I saw this honey at my local bulk food store I gave it a try! I started taking just 1 teaspoon a day, either in my oatmeal, on a bagel or in my tea- it has been 1 year and I have *not* gotten sick one time since then! Never caught the flu or even a cold all of last winter even when everyone around me was out sick! I keep several jars in my cupboard so that I am sure not to run out, but then the lid-consistency change occurred and now I have to warm the honey to use it which seems to defeat the purpose of using a honey had never been heated so that you get the most benefit from it! As a consumer, the only possible cause of the consistency change I can see is that from metal lid to plastic. I tried to contact the manufacturer directly, but could not find a way to do so other than snail mail, so I decided to try here.
In conclusion, if Moorland Apiaries goes back to using the metal lid so that the consistency goes back to be spreadable, I will absolutely give this 5 Stars because this honey is Awesome!

review_headline: Quality unsmoked Yerba Mate for a good price
review_body:
I read about the benefits of drinking Yerba Mate, so I started researching which brand I wanted to buy. I certainly wanted organic Yerba Mate and unsmoked Yerba Mate. I read that the smoked variety may actually cause some health problems. I found this Ecoteas Yerba Mate and it is inexpensive and unsmoked. I did a little research on the company and it seems to be pretty good. I purchased the product and it has a nice taste. I drink it sweetened with some coconut sugar and it tastes very nice. Sometimes I just drink it plain and it is still nice. I also like that I can steep this while cold and it still infuses nicely into the cold water.

The only issue that I would have with Yerba Mate in general is the caffeine content. The caffeine in this product is natural. However, I have felt jittery several times after drinking it. That is certainly something for me to keep an eye on. There is quite a bit of caffeine in Yerba Mate which may be concerning for some people.

This is a good and inexpensive unsmoked Yerba Mate. I highly recommend it but be careful with the caffeine content.

review_headline: It's supposed to help you by not using any type of sweetener if you are craving something sweet while trying to avoid refined su
review_body: Let's get real. This will arrive to your door heralded as a new diet-miracle. Why? It's supposed to help you by not using any type of sweetener if you are craving something sweet while trying to avoid refined sugars or artificial sweeteners. While this berry's power to sweeten is truly novel, this product is not going to revolutionize the sweetener industry unless they figure out how to make it in mass quantities. Here's how this works: You unpack one precious tablet from the blister package, swirl it about on your tongue until it dissolves and then eat something sour. Hmmmm. OK. I tried sucking on a lime wedge. Not bad, tasted quite sweet, like key lime pie. In the same half hour, I tried some lime infused unsweetened sparkling water. Tasted a bit like a sweet 7-Up. Plain yogurt? Becomes sweet. Sound good? It might be if the effects lasted more than 45 minutes and you did not have to pay more than $1.25 per tablet. That's right... this brand was the cheapest I found online, and I still only got 10 tablets in a box for nearly $15. I think as a party trick it might be fun to pass out lime or lemon wedges with a tablet on the side to your guests, but otherwise, I think I will continue my search for alternative sweeteners.

It bothers me when I have more than 0.2 blood content in my coffee stream, so I've been looking for something for my morning wakeup jolt and a few reinforcers throughout the day.

Frankly, I don't find gagging, coughing, and choking to be a particularly pleasant wakeup call.

This has to be the nastiest thing I've ever put in my mouth, and that includes some old college stories that would make your grandmother faint. It goes beyond the bitterness of a good dark coffee and cloaks itself in the kind of sweaty sour fume normally reserved for highly overtaxed armpits and competitive athletes' jock straps. Lighter fluid and the bitter rot of death, my friends. Lighter fluid and the bitter, cold, clammy rot of a slow and unavoidable death.

I tried making it weaker. I tried making it stronger. I tried more sugar. I tried less. I tried creamer, liquid and powder, flavored and not. I even tried vodka, but no matter what I added or took away, underneath every other flavor came the creeping aftertaste of oily asphalt after a trucker rally. Although to be fair, the vodka made me care a little less.

Long story short? Tastes like the failure of a thousand dreams, and I think I'll stick to Nescafe.
