review_headline: Won't Do What You Think It Will
review_body:
This product is powdered cow skin. Cow skin is made from collagen, and the hydrolysate process just breaks it down to allow your body to digest it. So they call this collagen hydrolysate but its the same as calling a garbage man a sanitation engineer. There's nothing special about it. This is just a waste product that they have figured out how to make digestible, the same way that pink slime turned another beef waste product into something edible. It's not a pharmaceutical, it's just powdered cow skin, a waste product they sell for a premium price because they used some fancy names to describe it. Nothing more special about it.

Collagen, like all protein, is a collection of amino acids. Proteins are like a brick wall and amino acids are the bricks. You can make all sorts of brick walls from all sorts of bricks, and there are lots of types of proteins, but they are all made with the same amino acids, just a different mix of bricks. As soon as you eat collagen, it is broken down into the component amino acids that make up all proteins. Said another way, your body cannot absorb a brick wall without breaking it down into individual bricks. As long as you are eating food with the complete complement of amino acids (which if you're eating meat and eggs, you already are), you're already getting what's in this product, for a much lower price than you are paying for this product. Thus, this product won't do anything more than any egg will, except you'll be paying a lot more.

Your body will certainly use the amino acids it has to rebuild collagen, grow hair, rebuild skin, etc., but those amino acids can come from any source. This one is no better than any other, it's just a lot more expensive.

What this product won't do is deposit itself into your joints, skin or hair intact. It's going to be broken down, and once broken down, it's no better than an egg, for twice the price. It also won't force your body to do anything differently than it already is.

If you like eating powdered cow skin and think it's worth twice the price of an egg, I have a bridge to sell to you. Your body WILL digest this stuff, and will use it like any other protein. A bunch of reviews saying \\"I ate this stuff and my hair got more luxurious in 3 days!\\" are laughable. Your hair is dead dear, it would take months to see any difference and this stuff won't make any difference that an egg isn't already going to do.

In short, if you think eating powdered cow skin is somehow beneficial, I'm sure this powdered cow skin is as good as any other powdered cow skin, but really, unless you are protein deficient, it isn't going to do anything at all. Not for your skin, your nails, your hair or your joints. If this explanation helped you, please indicate using the buttons below before you go buy a carton of eggs. The beans look dark but the ground coffee and flavor is more medium. The flavor out of the Aero Press is mild, with some hints of rich aftertone flavors, not without interest.

Note well however, that in a French press or drip maker, for some reason very little flavor comes through and it's pretty anemic and forgettable, no matter how much grounds you use. I haven't come across too many coffees that have such different results with these different brewing methods.

Thing is, I got it for the French press, whole bean in order to grind it fairly coarse. All the store bought decaf in my area (Southern Cal.) is already ground, just hard to find whole bean decaf. My favorite is Peet's decafs, some of them are quite excellent, but they grind them into practically powder. This doesn't work well in a French Press which needs a coarser grind if you hope to be able to press down without a 100lb weight. (A French press is a bit easier if you are making coffee for two or three people, the Aero Press is really a solo cup maker.)

So in short for the Aero Press I will probably prefer a darker Peet's or Starbucks Cafe Verona. However this is a perfectly good choice for a more medium roast if are using an Aero Press.

review_headline: An excellent cheese substitute in a plant based diet
review_body:
I've become more and more interested in plant based eating, primarily through the books by Dr. Caldwell B. Esselstyn, Jr., and the remarkable results he has documented from patients with heart disease.

[[ASIN:B003TZP350 Prevent & Reverse Heart Disease: The Revolutionary, Scientifically Proven, Nutrition-based Cure -- 2008 publication]]; and

[[ASIN:B00JPR5JE6 The Prevent and Reverse Heart Disease Cookbook: Over 125 Delicious, Life-Changing, Plant-Based Recipes]]

Mrs. Esselstyn gave a fascinating presentation at FoodStock last September near Hudson, New York, and one of her best tips was how mushrooms and nutritional yeast can satisfy your taste for cheese. I tried a bag on popcorn, in soups, and sprinkled over my favorite kale and beans dishes.

Absolutely delicious!

A few thoughts: although not stated on the packaging, the website states: \\"Nutritional yeast is grown on enriched purified cane and beet molasses under carefully controlled conditions. T6635, with the addition of vitamin B12, is an ideal vegetarian support formula and has an appealing cheese flavor.\\"

The added B12 is a good thing for people on a plant based diet; it avoids using supplements containing that vitamin.

There is some evidence that MSG can cause cancer, although both US and European regulatory agencies have found that limited quantities are safe. Nutritional yeast products do not have any added monosodium glutamate; however, all inactive yeast contains a certain amount of free glutamic acid because when the yeast cells are killed, the protein that comprises the cell walls begins to degrade, breaking down into the amino acids that originally formed it.

I have also used [[ASIN:B000173IHE Red Star Nutritional Yeast - VSF Mini Flake -- 5 oz Each]] with great pleasure. Unfortunately, Bob's is much cheaper, especially on Subscribe and Save, so I'll stick with Bob's Red Mill Version.

Robert C. Ross
October 2014October 2014

review_body:
These arrived very quickly and were packed nicely in some shredded paper to keep them from bouncing around. I have a lot of tillandsia and I love these for the soft texture their leaves have. Hinterland never disappoints me in providing nice plants.
Mine are all green as well, and here's why: tillandsia flower once in their life, and it is before and after blooming that you will see the pinkish/red blush on the leaves. Once the blooming is over, don't worry! The tillandsia will have "pups", baby tillys, who will bloom for you in the future!
My t. velutinas were all roughly 2.5 inches (7 cm) tall and 2 inches (5 cm) wide at the widest point. They came with instructions for care, as well. An easy way to care for your tillys is to soak them once a week for 30 minutes to an hour. Be sure that you are not using chlorinated water, though, as from the tap. Use filtered/bottled water, your fish tank (I plop mine in my beta's aquarium, he doesn't seem to mind), rainwater, or tap water that has been left out for 12 hours. The instructions say to mist them but I find the once a week soak is just as good.

product_title: Cocotes
review_headline: Remarkably close to fresh, raw coconut water straight from the fruit
review_body:
No matter which coconut water we're drinking, we always compare it to the coconut water you sip from the actual fruit. That's to what they all aspire, right?

Coconut water - in case you're unfamiliar - is the clear liquid in the center of young, green coconuts. It's very different from coconut milk or coconut cream which is made by soaking the flesh from older coconuts in water. Coconut water is, and should be, virtually unprocessed.

To that end, I try to avoid a couple of things with any coconut water that I choose for my family. First, added sugars. Cocozia passes that test with flying colors. Its ingredient list is a single item; organic coconut water. Nice.

Second, heat-pasteurization. Pasteurization kills bacteria. That's a good thing, right? Yes. However, while heating coconut water to high temperatures may extend its shelf-life, it destroys some of the vitamins, minerals, and phytonutrients. So, my preference is always unpasteurized, raw coconut water. R did find some brands that are high pressure pasteurized, meaning that nutrients were intact but the bacteria were "squeezed out"?!?! I don't know exactly how that works. In any case, Cocozia's package reads: "gently pasteurized." Not quite sure what that means, but I would prefer unpasteurized.

All in all, I was impressed with Cocozia. The flavor of Cocozia is remarkably close to that of fresh, raw coconut water straight from the fruit. I love that the ingredient list is one item. I do like that Cocozia is certified organic by the USDA and verified as non-GMO. Those are all important to me.

review_headline: Organic Matcha Green Tea Powder by Kiss Me Organics is a Great and Healthy Pick Me Up!
review_body:
When I first got this product to review, I was a little hesitant due to the fact I know green tea is good for you,but I wondered about being jittery and not being able to get rid of that uneasy feeling,which I do not like at all,that I have gotten from green tea bags over the counter and drank it that way. This product was something very different from what my past encounters have been like with anything to do with green tea.

This is Culinary Grade Green Tea Powder which is meant to give you: all day energy,metabolism boost,increased focus,improve skin health, AND it has 137X the antioxidants of brewed green tea! It is a 4 oz bag which is a pretty decent size. Also this powder is known for burning calories and used for anti aging. After reading more on this product and what it can be used for, I see it can be used in Lattes,Smoothies,and baking recipes!

I opened the packet,and it does warn you on the attached flyer that the Organic Matcha is VERY fresh,and thus has a naturally strong aroma to it. (which it DEFINITELY does) It says do not be frightened,that is how all antioxidants say hello. It said hello to me alright! lol It had a pretty intense potency to it,but it did not really stink. Just a very strong aroma. I looked down inside,and the color was,a medium green,kind of pale in my eyes,but definitely a noticeable aroma to it no doubt.

Along with getting this product, I did receive a free recipe guide in e-book format that was sent to my email pretty quickly,so I started looking through it to see what I could make when I got my order,and I decided to make a Matcha Orange Cocktail! It was pretty easy to make,and all I did was pray that it tasted good so I would be more encouraged to drink it every day! Recommended dosage is 1/2 a teaspoon to 1 full teaspoon once daily mixed in with whichever recipe you choose.

So I began to make my recipe by mixing together the sugar and Matcha Green Tea Powder in a bowl,and I had my ice set aside in a glass,waiting for my recipe to be mixed together to add to it. After I mixed up the sugar and matcha, I added the hot water and mixed it all together.Then I added the mixture to the ice cubes.Then I added the orange juice on top of that mixture in with the ice cubes.

It left the orange juice sitting on top of the icecubes and mixture so it looked like it had 2 layers the orange layer on top,and green on the bottom which was very pretty to look at! Now comes the tasting of it.

I really did enjoy the flavor of the whole drink! It was absolutely DELICIOUS! I will be fixing this drink frequently! It gave a refreshing,yet healthy taste to the drink,and I did not have to struggle to get it down. I truly enjoyed every last drop of it. I felt the energy and difference within half an hour after drinking the cocktail. I felt a calm,mellow,yet energizing feeling from it. I was not exhausted and I wanted to get up and do things! I have Fibromyalgia,so this is a big deal to me when you deal with pain and exhaustion all of the time! I did feel a LITTLE bit of jittery,more then likely because my body is not use to having anything like this product in it which is super healthy,so I am just going to decrease from the 1 whole teaspoon I used to maybe 3/4 to 1/2 and I am sure that will knock out any small amount of jittery type of feeling I had. Trust me,it was nothing major at all to worry about. I plan on staying with this product and using from here on out to get myself more healthier.

I am 39 years old going on 40,and I do not want to keep waiting to start getting healthy. I have been neglecting my body,and not paying much attention to what it needs,letting one problem lead to another with depression and more,and I firmly believe after taking this product, I am on the right track. I highly recommend anyone wanting to get healthy,to get on this product and stay with it! You will not regret it! I know I don't! :)

product_title: Oatfield Liquorice Toffee Bulk 3kg (105.7oz)
review_body:
What a disappointment.

For years, I've enjoyed the flavor of good licorice-flavored English toffee. First it was C&B; then, after C&B discontinued their licorice toffee, Oatfield and Walkers.

This stuff tastes like none of that. It says "Oatfield" on the bag, but if that's accurate, then something went very wrong at the Oatfield Toffee Works. They must have changed the recipe for the worse, received a shipment of bad ingredients and failed to catch it, or left this candy sitting around in a warehouse for several years until the mildew crept in and the flavor of plastic and cardboard began to compete with the licorice. (The flavor can best be described as "licorice toffee seasoned with musty cardboard with a hint of plastic" - both my wife and I noticed it immediately.)

The texture of the toffee is at least approximately right, but the flavor is off by a mile. Whether it's just this batch or the entire brand that went done the chute, I don't know, but I'm not willing to pay over a buck an ounce for the stuff in the little retail baggies just to get to the bottom of it ($~20 or more per pound for the retail baggies ... now, that's what I call Irish pluck).

If I'm going to pay $50 for a bag of candy - even a 7 pound bag of candy - it had damned well better taste like it's supposed to. This does not, so I'm returning it ... and if you knew how much I like licorice toffee, you'd know how bad it must be for that to happen.

[If Oatfield or Trade Concepts would like to send me a current product sample that tastes as it should, I'll be happy to reorder and modify this review. Until then, buyer beware.]

product_title: Van Houtte Mexican Coffee, K-Cup Portion Pack for Keurig Brewers (24 Count)
review_body:
I love Van Houtte coffee, and Eclipse is my favorite brew. But I've stopped buying their brand because of the poor quality of their pods They aren't sealed well. When the pressure builds up at the end of the brew, the seal breaks and grounds and water go everywhere... in the Keurig, in the coffee, over the counter. And it is NOT easy to clean all the grounds our of the pod receptacle.

I typically get four or five bad pods out of a box of 24. That's about 20% failure rate, and that's a lot of money wasted. I have had this problem with Van Houtte brands since I started buying them, and if anything I'm having more failures per box over time. And I have not had this problem with any other brand of Keurig pod that I've bought.

I wrote to Van Houtte and told them about my experience with their brands and that I thought they needed to look into their quality control. I got a form response back asking me to send them the product number, serial number on the box, the date I bought it and the store I bought it from (which was the Keurig site by the way) and they would replace the product. That's nice, but I'm not going to take the time to report every box of their product that I buy. I want to spend my time drinking my coffee, not cleaning up after it and filing problem reports. It's much easier to buy another brand.

So now I have five partial boxes of Van Houtte pods from my last order. I've used about half of all of them and already had three or four bad pods per box. I recently read that coffee grounds make good fertilizer, so maybe I'll open the pods and mix the grounds into my garden soil so it doesn't go completely to waste.

product_title: Organic Raw Tigernuts
review_headline: An energy-dense, mineral-rich snack that improves your digestion
review_body:
Thousands of years ago, our ancestors pulled these things out of the ground and ate them as their main energy source. They are not nuts, they are tubers, which means they are the part of the plant where all the nutrients are stored. Our ancestors figured this out and according to various research papers ate these tigernuts while ignoring all the other stuff. A bit like how carnivorous animals in the wild typically devour the liver first, because it is the most nutrient dense part of an animal’s body — these tigernuts are the most nutrient dense part of the plant. In fact, tigernuts are more nutrient dense than red meat! They’re a great way for vegans or anyone else to get their nutrients. They’re very high in energy as well.

What makes them even more appealing is that they are very high in resistant starch (not to be mistaken with ‘normal’ starch!), which fuels the cells lining your colon. As a result, eating tigernuts improves the functioning of your gut. A few weeks ago, a guy with stomach problems told me his stomach had gotten much better after he started eating tigernuts. Your mileage may vary, but if you suffer from digestive problems, these are definitely worth a shot.

How do they taste? Rather sweet and delicious — perhaps another reason our ancestors preferred them to other plant parts. People say they taste a bit like coconut, almond, or granola, though really, they have their own unique taste. You’ll probably like their taste; they’re one of the best-tasting ‘super-healthy’ foods. But their texture may throw you. They start off chewy but for the last few chews they will be a bit gritty. Some people mistake this for a defect, but that’s just the way tigernuts are. I don’t mind it at all. At any rate, soaking them overnight in water will soften them and make their texture much more familiar to the American palate. My suggestion is to be adventurous, try them for yourself, and see how you feel about them. You’ll be making your body very happy.happy.

product_title: Huy Fong Sriracha Chili Sauce, 28 Ounce (Pack of 6)
review_headline: Want less sugar?  Try also:  Huy Fong Chili Garlic Sauce
review_body:
The chili garlic sauce is this one: [[ASIN:B0070SGNU6 Huy Fong Chili Garlic Sauce, 18-Ounce (Pack of 3)]]. It's very similar to my beloved Sriracha here, but without all the sugar. As with the equally tasty [[ASIN:B000F865ZQ Huy Fong Sambal Oelek Ground Chili Paste - 8 oz x 2 bottles]], the chiles are a bit less pulverized, giving a bit of chili-flecked texture to your mix. (The Sambal Oelek is very like the Chili Garlic Paste, but without the garlic.)

So you've got three very similar product choices from Huy Fong. American palates love the Sriracha - no surprise - for the sweet/heat pairing. It's been a staple in our household for at least 15 years, and I'm glad to see that so far (knock wood) the greater Sriracha fad hasn't affected the quality of the product.

Go with Sriracha for the tabletop, Sambal Oelek or Chili Garlic in the soup pot or stir fry pan. (Sriracha's brigtness doesn't hold up quite as well to cooking, and the sweetness can throw off the flavor balance in some preparations.)

review_headline: Coming from Franks, may never go back.
review_body:
This hot sauce is the talk of the town, so I figured I'd give it a shot.

Typically, I use Franks Original, but I decided to give this a try and it definitely was a good decision.

Using Franks as a benchmark, this sauce is quite a bit sweeter with very little of the vinegary aftertaste you'd get with Franks as there seems to be much less of a vinegar ratio. Throughout the entire bite, the spice is balanced with sugar and you get a great garlic taste which accents it perfectly to complete the sauce. The spice is fair, but it is in no way overwhelming and the taste of the food always prevails. I personally would rate Tabasco sauce way above this in regards to spice, if that's any help.

The only downside of this is, in my case, these were shipped loosely in a plastic bag as part of a Subscribe and Save delivery. Needless to say, a big box with other items in it did not fare well as these were moving about and their tips acted like knives puncturing the insulation air bag packing causing everything to tumble around freely damaging products in transit. Regardless, Amazon mended the issue swiftly and made another happy customer.

product_title: Pure Bar Organic Variety Pack, Fruit & Nut Bars, 1.7-Ounce Bars (Pack of 12)
review_body:
These are very good, and I would say better than most similar bars out there. I've been trying out different brands lately, and I'd say the only one that actually curves my appetite and gives me a better protein boost - in addition to being tastier overall are the Special K meal bars.

I've tried Kind (too hard), Special K (great), NuGo (taste like whey), Zone Perfect (almost as good as Special K), BelVita (tastes like dog food)

The good part (and maybe bad part) is these bars are just as described, purely organic. It's as if they took all the ingredients labeled and put them in a homemade food processor and mashed it together in the form of a bar. On one side, it's great to have no added junk, and on the other side it just has a very weird texture and taste sometimes. I would suggest refrigeration because they can get very melty in room temperature, and only eat holding the wrapper as it gets on your hands a bit.

It all depends on personal taste, but I was very surprised by the Banana and Blueberry flavored ones. If they made a mix of those two, it'd be worth it.

Overall - worth the buy if you're looking for alternative and healthy meal bars like I am. Could be better, but a better choice than most out there.

Then a friend gave me a pack of these. To me they taste better than any bread or wrap, and really let me feel like I have a normal option for many meals.

They are a daily staple in our house now.

A few uses:
Breakfast burritos with scrambled eggs and sweet potato
Fish "tacos" with grilled mahi mahi, corn + cucumber salsa, sauteed peppers and onions, topped with guac
Lunch wrap with a burger, fried egg, salad greens, and sliced avocado

They are pricey compared to dirt-cheap wheat products, but the difference in health and the way I feel after eating them vs eating gluten is night and day.

Highly recommended!

review_body:
This used to be an excellent product, but the company redesigned it and ruined it. We used to use the bags several times a week, and found them roomy and reliable. Now we find them useless.
What was once a straight-top bag now has 4 long handles carved out of the top. If you manage to keep the handles clean, you use them to tie the bag shut. However, we had no problem tying the top of the old bag, and there was no hassle involved. We'll never buy these again, so I hope we can find another compostable bag of similar size to the old model.
By the way, I don't know why Amazon calls this box of Food Waste Bags a "Kitchen Caddy"—I think that name will confuse most people who are searching for waste bags.

I prefer steel cut oats to the instant packets because those are so highly processed they're bad for anyone who has to manage their blood sugar.

Bring water to a rolling boil in a medium-sized pot. Stir in oats and salt. Boil vigorously for 1 minute. Remove from heat. Cover and let sit overnight (8-12 hours).

review_headline: Complex earthy flavor of ripe pu-erh
review_body:
普洱 or \\"pu-erh\\" is a broad-leaf tea from the mountains of Yunnan that is ripened through oxidation and fermentation until it is dark and fragrant. It is usually sold in compressed forms such as these discs, called 冰茶 or \\"bingcha.\\"

This particular ripened pu-erh from DeChunXian is organic. It has a mild but complex flavor. It makes a beautiful and fragrant brew and is a good way to experience the flavor of this type of tea.

The bingcha weighs 250 g or 8.8 oz. The paper packaging is especially beautiful and it would make a nice gift exactly as-is.

TIP: The traditional method of brewing pu-erh is somewhat complicated, but a delicious cup of tea can be made in a simplified manner:

茶 Use an implement such as an ice pick or oyster knife to break off a few small chunks of the tea and place them in the pot.

茶 With water at a rolling boil, perform two quick rinses to wash away any dust, open the leaves, and warm the pot. Use a strainer to catch the tea and return it to the pot or, as an alternative, use a french press pot.

茶 Pour enough water over the tea to make the amount that will be consumed immediately. The tea is so intense that it will only need to brew a few seconds to obtain a beautiful mahogany color. Subsequent brews can be extended for the intensity desired.

茶 Do not allow it to brew for too long or it will be as dark as coffee. If you intend to add milk and sugar or honey, a somewhat stronger but still translucent brew is suitable, though the earthy flavor and fragrance are best appreciated unadorned.

WeiHeng provided a bingcha for evaluation and review.

Everybody always asks what you dream of when you're a kid. Some people want a puppy, or a pony, or to become an astronaut or a doctor.

Me? I wanted Surge to come back.

It was disturbingly sweet, enough to cause diabetes in an otherwise healthy adult, never mind the awful things it undoubtedly did to our young caffeine-addled bodies. We knew it was bad for us. Even back then, we knew. But we didn't CARE. Surge answered all of our most base needs: It was like drinking a pound of pure white sugar and green food coloring with bubbles in it. It was awful. And we loved it. We LOVED IT.

Then they took it away.

But suddenly.. It has returned. Now I have children of my own (who, thankfully, despise soda or refuse to drink anything caffeinated, depending upon which child you ask), but I still intend on asking them if they want to try a drink.

product_title: Natural Value Coconut Milk, 13.5-Ounce Containers
review_headline: Natural is wonderful, but difficult to use practically for varied diary-free applications
review_body: As a daily user of coconut milk, I had been waiting for the price to come down on this brand as it has zero fillers (YAY for pure products!!).  I paid a fair price and ordered 2 boxes.  When the product arrived I was so excited that I ripped into that first box and immediately opened a can.  SURPRISE, coconut water flew everywhere!  I suppose, being used to the thicker, creamier products that contain guar gum, I was expecting there to be a thick layer of cream near the top and was less than careful in my method, so I learned THAT lesson quickly.  I was disappointed in the texture of this product almost immediately, as there was 3/4 water and probably 1/4 inch of pure coconut oil on the surface of some gritty coconut particles.  It was all busted up, so I whisked it together as well as I could and used it in my usual applications: 1 can was cultured into coconut milk kefir, another can in coconut curry, and another can just as cream in my hot tea.  The kefir did not culture well and instead separated into a fatty layer and a water layer.  The curry tasted phenomenal, but the sauce was watery, not creamy.  The tea was barely drinkable as there was an oily layer floating at the top with coconut particles dispersed throughout the tea -- I am ALL for coconut oil, but when you desire cream and end up with an oily mess, it's just disappointing.  Overall, my experience with the product is it is great for flavor, awful for texture.  I kept one box for cooking, but to use in cold applications this product is worthless to me, so I returned the second box.  Still hopeful that there is a product out there without the fillers, but with that creamy texture I am looking for!  I need to weigh the cost/benefit, but will probably go back to the organic brands which contain less than 1% organic guar gum in order to have a usable product.

product_title: STUR WATER ENHNCR,TEA & LEMON- 6 pack
review_body:
I've been trying for a while to get away from artificial sweeteners, but the truth is, I hate water. People say it has no taste, and maybe that's the problem, but it always 'tastes' horrible to me. And, having brushed up against a diabetes scare that I am controlling by deep and pervasive changes to my eating habits, I found that I really needed a water enhancer that had no carb load (because I actually make myself drink a LOT of water over the course of a day), and wasn't loaded down with artificial sweeteners.

Then I found STUR. My favorite is the Lemon Tea flavor. I love lemon tea, and this is a great enhancer for my water. Now if you're looking for Southern Sweet Tea, this isn't going to be it -- but the flavor is tart, full-bodied, and has just the right amount of flavor to improve water's palatability, without being so overwhelming that you aren't drinking 'water' any more, you're downing a drink mix.

I strongly recommend this to anyone who is following a paleo/primal or LCHF plan, to my friends who are diabetic, or to anyone trying to cut back on their refined sugar and artificial sweetener load, while still being able to enjoy their beverages.

product_title: Akebono industry Microwave Oven Potato Chips Maker with Syakasyaka Shaker Ball (RE-213)
review_body:
This Akebono Potato Chip maker arrives with an instruction booklet (written entirely in Kanji) and comes with 6 pieces: red bowl, white rubber foot ring for bowl, clear bowl top, yellow mandolin-style slicer, white food gripper/pusher and brown silicone/rubber microwave oven chip rack.

What I like about it. The slicer makes perfect thickness slices for potato chips. The slicer is amazingly even. Because thickness is key to making perfect microwave potato chips, this mandolin slicer is hands-down one of the best slicers I've used for this purpose (and I have several mandolin slicers). The look of the whole set works quite well together. The clear top is perfect for use as a small potato chip bowl.

What I dislike about it. The brown silicone is not stiff enough. When you place sliced potatoes into each of the rack holes and then try to pick it up, the rubber doesn't have enough strength to hold them they all fall out. You need to load the slices into the rack in the microwave directly or place the rack onto a plate and then place the plate into the microwave. When you load the rack, the slices sit vertical. But, after about 3 minutes of cooking, the potatoes get floppy and fall over touching each other. The vertical idea just wasn't great. For this reason, the paper-towels-on-a-plate cooking method works better. In fact, it's easier not to use the rack and simply use paper towels on a plate. The paper towels soak up moisture from the potatoes faster than in the rack vertically. So, it takes somewhat longer to make the chips in the rack. Also, because the chips are so close together in the rack, it's hard to see when they are done. Flat on the plate it's easy to see how done they are. Plus, on a plate the chips remain a whole lot flatter.

How to use it.

Clean a russet potato with a vegetable brush. Cut off the ends up to about 1/4 inch and discard. From here, begin slicing with the slicer into the red bowl. The slicer fits perfectly on top of the red bowl. If you choose to use the rack, you'll need about 28 slices. If you use paper towels, slice as many as you want.

With the slices in the bowl, rinse the slices until the water runs mostly clear. You will need to shuffle the slices around to get water between them. After rinsed, use a salad spinner or dry the slices by hand with paper towels. Rinsing off the starch will prevent the chips from sticking together.

Place the slices into the rack or lay them out on paper towels on a large plate. Here's where it gets a little tricky. If you have a 400W microwave, it takes about 20 minutes to complete a batch. A 600W microwave takes about 10 minutes. A 1200W microwave takes about 5 minutes. These instructions assume a 1200W microwave. Place the chips into the microwave and run the microwave on high for about 3 minutes. Lift the chips and move them around either in the rack or on the plate. They might want to stick to the paper towels as the towels dry and chips begin to dry out. If the towels are soaked, you can replace them if you wish. But, the towels will dry out as the cooking progresses. After moving the chips around. Run the microwave for another 2 minutes. If the potatoes are still all white, run it again for another 2 minutes. The chips will shrink in size as the water dries out.

An individual chip is done when it feels mostly hard to the touch and it has a small amount of golden hue in places. It will crisp up more as it cools. Drop them into the clear bowl. Some chips finish faster than others, so remove the done chips and let the others cook longer. If the chips are chewy in parts, place them back into the microwave for 1-2 more minutes. If they get chewy after sitting around, you can also crisp them again this way.

I will caution you the following. Glass plates get very hot in the microwave when using the paper towel method. You will need to handle the plate with an oven mitt.

Note, I prefer them unsalted. But, if you want them salted, add salt to the water for the last soak or sprinkle salt on them on the plate. Enjoy.the water for the last soak or sprinkle salt on them on the plate. Enjoy.

review_headline: Delicious, healthy, will be reordering again and again... plus here's a recipe
review_body:
I live in Hawaii and we have about 20 organic coconut trees on our property. We harvest our own fresh coconuts and I was suspicious that any commercial product would live up to our expectations. We don't harvest our own coconut sugar because the process is too tedious and time consuming, but if we ever do, I will be thrilled if it even comes close to matching this 100% natural, organic, GMO free product.

I had never tried this type of coconut sugar before, so when I wanted some I used this brand because I was so impressed with their other products. I wanted to try some recipes before posting this review. But I have discovered that anything that you can sweeten with regular sugar, you can sweeten with coconut sugar. Just like regular brown sugar adds depth and flavor to recipes that call for it, coconut sugar has somewhat malty, caramel flavor that adds a hint of flavor as well as sweetness. It does not taste "coconutty" at all.

But more importantly than flavor, this sugar is actually good for you. Low Glycemic index and high in vitamins and nutrients. It is especially high in magnesium and potassium, so just like coconut water helps to replace lost electrolytes, this sugar will help keep you balanced when exerting yourself, plus give you a burst of healthy energy. I've actually just taken a spoonful of this stuff when working outside in the tropics and it immediately restores some vitality.

I promised a recipe and here it is. It actually contains two Viva ingredients, the coconut flour and also the coconut sugar. The eggs in the recipe came from our hens, and the bananas came from our yard. Next time, we hope even the vanilla will come from our orchids, but one thing we can't produce ourselves are these quality coconut flour and sugars. Here's the recipe... Enjoy!

Ingredients
* 3 ripe, peeled bananas (300 g, or about 1 1/2 cups mashed)
* 3 large eggs
* 2 tablespoons coconut sugar
* 1 tablespoon vanilla extract
* 3/4 teaspoon baking soda
* 1/2 teaspoon salt
* 1/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons (39 g) coconut flour
Method
1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (180°C, or gas mark 4).
2. Prepare a baking pan with parchment paper, or grease generously.
3. Mash the bananas using a mixer or by hand in a large bowl. Mix until completely mashed and smooth.
4. Add the eggs and vanilla to the mashed bananas and blend well.
5. Add the baking soda, salt, and coconut flour to the wet batter and blend well.
6. Let the batter sit for 5 minutes or so to give the coconut flour time to absorb the liquids.
7. Pour the batter into the baking pan and bake for 50 minutes or until the top begins to brown and a toothpick inserted in the center of the bread comes out clean.
8. Cool fully and slice. This is very moist when first out of the oven but tends to firm up over time. Store covered for a few days at room temperature or in the refrigerator for a few weeks, or seal and freeze for a few months.spoon vanilla extract

I wanted to like this mix so much because I miss pancakes terribly. Unfortunately, the quest for a good pancake continues. I tried multiple times following their instructions precisely, and when that didn't work, I tried tweaking to see if I could make them better. No luck. They tasted bad and had a terrible, eggy texture. Gritty. Mealy. Scrambled egg whites meets sawdust.

These pancakes are very flax-y, and whilst I'm not against flax, I felt like the makers of this product could've done more to make it blend more.

As with all these gluten-free, paleo, low-carb etc products, it's important to remember that your mileage will vary, and what works for someone else won't work for you. Obviously, some people really enjoyed this mix, and their opinion is of course valid. At any rate, I recommend buying the smaller sized package to give it a try before investing in the 14-serving size bag.

product_title: Wild Planet Wild Sardines in Extra Virgin Olive Oil
review_headline: Like a minature vacation to the Pacific Ocean.
review_body:
At first I thought these sardines were too expensive based on my experience with
the cheap sardines found in the grocery stores of the food desert of Albany georgia.
I emailed this company to ask if the cost of these sardines was more in the logo design
than the sardines.The founder of the company emailed me and explained that the sardines
used in his brand where actually sardines or sardinops sagax. The fish in most cheap
cans of sardines are immature herring. The brand I have the most experience with
Chicken of the sea uses this variety, I usually get the smoked variety and they taste fine.
The King Oscar brand uses brislings and while they are better than the Chicken of the sea
they are tiny and it seems like you are eating goldfish or bait.

These Sardines are a completely different experience. They are as big as the immature
herring sold by Chicken of the sea, but they are as plump as the brislings sold by King Oscar.
The meat inside of these is like biting into a tiny tuna loin, it is beige with a purple streak
going through it, the skin is so firm and it does not rip apart when you pull it out of the can.
Biting into this fish is like a minature vacation to the pacific ocean, you can really smell it
and taste it.

I know now these sardines are very inexpensive based on their value. King Oscar sardines
cost more than these and they are cheap in comparison to these sardines. The only way
those immature herrings taste good is if they are smoked and then you have to worry about
the bpa in the cans they are packed in.

review_headline: Muisjes sound like some kind of superfluous breakfast treat
review_body:
My step-father's family is Dutch and Dutch/Indo, so I was privileged to try some very delicious and obscure foods that I otherwise would've been completely oblivious to otherwise. Muisjes sound like some kind of superfluous breakfast treat; I mean, sprinkles on toast? What's next, cake icing? But, try it once, and you'll instantly love it.

Every flavor I've had I end up loving, they're all quite good. That being said, the milk chocolate muisjes are my favorite. Kids, loving sweet overkill, will probably put a mountain of this stuff on toast, but I find a light to moderate dousing works best for the flavor of salty butter and sweet muisjes to blend together at just the right ratio.

Seriously, I can't recommend this stuff enough. It might not be an everyday thing, but when you get that hankering, it turns regular old toast into a morning desert!

product_title: Truvia Natural Sweetener 3g (300-Count Packages)
review_body:
Truvia sweetener is made from about 99.5% erythritol (a sugar alcohol), and 0.5% rebiana, an extract from the stevia plant (but not at all the same thing as stevia).

Erythritol made from yeast fed genetically modified corn derivatives. Cargill was forced to settle a class action lawsuit last year (2) for labeling Truvia "natural" when it's actually made from a fermentation process whereby yeast are fed GM corn maltodextrin. "The more you get [fruit flies] to consume erythritol, the faster they die," Sean O'Donnell, a professor of biology at Drexel University in Philadelphia, told CBS News.

Cargill plays word games with this process, insisting erroneously that "erythritol is not derived from corn or dextrose feedstock; it is derived from the yeast organism."

They also tested Purevia and found it was safe for fruit flies. Only erythritol, the main component of Truvia, replicated the toxic effects on fruit flies. Pyure Brands offers alternative sweeteners for the health-conscious marketplace, and their product is USDA Organic certified and Non-GMO Project Verified.

Learn more: http://www.naturalnews.com/045450_Truvia_erythritol_natural_pesticide.html#ixzz3A3TGSBJX

product_title: Viva Labs Organic Chia Seeds: Raw and Non-GMO
review_body:

The packaging is excellent - seals easily and tightly, stands up well for easy portioning and opens nice and wide. I've been using the chia seeds in many different ways. My favorite ways are on salad, in vinaigrette or in a drink. I added about 1 tsp of chia seeds for every 16 oz of water/juice. They absorb water very quickly, so be careful how much you add, but do not absorb other liquids as fast. The days I added chia seeds to my diet, I could feel a difference. I'm prone to migraines. The chia seeds helped significantly with my migraines because of the added raw vitamins. I don't like taking medication too often for my migraines as they make me too tired, but the chia seeds really helped reduce how much medication I needed.

The only reason I'm giving these seeds 4 out of 5 stars is for use. Although they can be added easily to just about anything, you do have to be careful for the gelatinous texture they create when bloated. I've definitely enjoyed adding these little seeds to my diet and plan to keep using them!

product_title: DREAMFIELDS PASTA MACARONI LINGUINE 13.25 OZ
review_headline: NOT LOW CARB!!  GOOGLE THIS:  "DREAMFIELDS PASTA FRAUD"
review_body:
I added this to my Atkins diet choices and loved it. However, today I decided to try the linguine that I'd just purchased via Subscribe & Save (10 boxes for $29.02). While it was cooking, I thought I'd better make sure that the linguine only had 5g of digestible carbs too, since I had only had the rotini and the lasagna in the past. So I looked at the box, and where previously it used to say something like, "41g carbohydrates, less 36g indigestible carbohydrates, 5g net carbs," there was absolutely nothing. Simply 41g carbs in the nutrition info box. So I asked the internet, and it turns out that the claims related to indigestible carbs were a bunch of hooey. Dreamfields settled a class action lawsuit on the matter earlier this year.

It's unsettling that this happened months ago and I was entirely unaware of it. Somehow the news story missed my radar entirely. Or it was "underreported," as those savvy marketing folks would say.

Don't eat this is if you're trying to do Atkins. One serving is 2 days’ worth of carbs (at least in Phase I.)

review_body: Buying Pyure Organic Stevia packets in bulk makes sense and saves money. I've tried several brands of Stevia and I like Pyure the best. review_headline: How could they melt in December?
review_body: Bought these truffles as a three pack. One for my own family and two as part of my children's godparents gifts for Christmas. I live in MN so I thought I would be okay to order them in early December when our temps are below freezing. (Other reviewers claimed that they received melted candy, but I thought I would be safe.) Unfortunately that was not the case. I could tell that something was wrong right away. When I opened the box that I purchased for my family I was disappointed to find a large lump of melted truffles. Because they are not individually wrapped, they all just melted together. I didn't want to give these away as gifts so I opened up the second box, which actually sounded like perhaps they might be okay, it at least sounded like it hadn't all melted together when I shook the box. The second box, oddly enough was not melted. (This was a three pack, so you would have thought that if one was melted then they all would be) However, all the cocoa powder that should have been coating the truffles had fallen off and settled in the bag. What was left was small uneven chocolate rounds that resembled presents that my dog leaves on my sidewalk when he is mad at us. Not fit for gifting, not even appetizing enough to put out of the counter at my house. Because I HATE wasting I ended up grinding up the "lump" that came in the first box to use for baking. I rolled the naked truffles in baking cocoa to try and vamp up their appearance in hopes that they would get eaten.  The third box is sitting in the bottom of my pantry unopened. Very disappointed. The ones that I vamped up, we finished off about 1/3 before we got sick of eating them. They are okay, but not really something that anyone got to excited about. I would never purchase these again.

We tried it for the first time yesterday for dinner and were happy with the results. It didn't get all mushy quickly like another type of gf pasta we tried. GF pasta seems more delicate than regular wheat pasta. It held the sauce well and didn't swell up after being in the pasta bowl with spaghetti sauce for awhile. Some pastas get too soft after soaking in the sauce for awhile, but this one seemed aldente still. Would have given it 5 stars but for the smaller size of the boxes-only 12 oz each, but plenty for the two of us. We are trying to reduce gluten in our diet for health reasons...to eat less refined white flour. This is corn and rice, the box doesn't say if it was whole grain so it is probably refined, no preservatives listed. It would be nice if we could get whole grain gf pasta. review_body:
Tejava (12x33.8OZ ), by Tejava.
This tea is excellent, with nothing added, no sweeteners, no preservatives. This is Java tea. The Amazon product description, and the Tejava web site, also list it as a black tea. It is nice to find bottled tea without flavorings, preservatives, sugar, fructose, or artificial sweeteners. This is great for people like me who are pre-diabetic, and have to avoid sugar. The only complaint I have, is that it was sold in 1 liter glass bottles that are heavy, smooth sided, and hard to hold onto. I would prefer plastic bottles with some kind of shape to hold onto. I made the mistake of putting a bottle of this tea into a very cold (32-34 degrees) beer, wine and soda refrigerator, where the tea froze and caused the bottle to break apart. I will have to find room in the food refrigerator (36-40 degrees) for these glass bottles. They should only use plastic bottles that will flex without breaking. This tea is very strong, and would be best served either over ice or in half a glass of cold water to thin it out a bit. The amount of acidity could cause a stomach ache in anyone prone to acid stomach problems (it happened to me). I only gave this product four stars, and that was because of the container, not the tea itself, which was excellent. The label mentioned some awards: "NORTH AMERICAN TEA CHAMPION 2011, 2012, 2013, FIRST PLACE 3 YEARS IN A ROW", but did not mention what organization did the judging. The tejava.com website said:

The annual Championship is made up of two classes: Hot Tea and Iced Tea. The Iced Tea Class was evaluated in May. Nearly 250 premium iced teas were entered into this year's Iced Tea class, which featured 20 categories. Each submission is evaluated through blind organoleptic analysis of the following characteristics: flavor, mouthfeel, color, clarity, and balance. An overall numerical value is then calculated based on the ratings of each characteristic above, and winners are determined by rank.

The Tejava Difference.
Tejava is the world's only 100% all natural, microbrewed and ready-to-drink iced tea made entirely from select, handpicked tea leaves from the island of Java. For the best tasting tea, only the top few leaves from each branch are picked - and only from May through October, the optimum harvesting months.

Tejava's unique microbrewing process eliminates bitterness and yields a rich, distinctive, full-bodied taste. Unsweetened and calorie free, Tejava is made with no added tea flavors, sweeteners, preservatives, or artificial ingredients. Tejava is simply pure and refreshing black tea."

product_title: Barilla Pasta
review_headline: Can't go wrong with Barilla! Yummy Pasta! (and my favorite recipe to use these noodles in!)
review_body:
I love Barilla pasta; it cooks up better and doesn't fall apart like some of the cheaper brands of pasta. And I love these mini farfalle for pasta salads and such. Here is my favorite recipe to use with them. I just made it and everyone was asking for the recipe (which I found a long time ago) so I'll post it here too!

Chicken Sesame Salad
Ingredients:
1 (16 ounce) package bow tie pasta
¼ cup sesame seeds
½ cup vegetable oil
1/3 cup rice vinegar
1/3 cup soy sauce
1 teaspoon sesame oil (I have left this out and it still is yummy!)
3 tablespoons sugar
½ teaspoon ground ginger
¼ teaspoon black pepper
3 cups cooked chicken (shredded or cut into small chunks)
1/3 cup cilantro (chopped)
1/3 cup green onions (sliced)
1 15 oz. can of mandarin oranges (drained)

Cooking Instructions:

Step 1: Heat a skillet over medium high heat. Add sesame seeds and cook while stirring until they are lightly browned. Remove from heat and set aside. Bring a large pot of water to a boil and cook according to package direction until Al Dente. Drain pasta and cool. Transfer to a large serving bowl.
Step 2: In a jar with a tight fitting lid combine vegetable oil, rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, ginger, black pepper and sesame seeds. Shake well. (Or just whisk it in a box)
Step 3: Pour the dressing over the noodles. Add chicken and mix well. Add green onions and cilantro and serve.

The reason is simply that this foil bag that it comes in reseals very easily and thus keeps the product safer for a longer period of time and that's a huge plus unless you know you need an entire pound of cocoa powder for some event. The Superfoods raw cacao powder has 9 more calories per serving than the previous raw cacao powder I reviewed suggesting that there is a difference in processing but what that difference is I'm unsure of.

Otherwise the two raw cacao powders are basically the same -- good cocoa scent but slightly less flavor in the recipes, slightly better nutritional values compared to traditionally process cocoa powder. You can use them in regular recipes or use the eCookbook that you should get if you order this one. Note that that recipe booklet has some problems that I'll report on in depth on The Chocolate Cult. The bag is easy to get into to get the product though it doesn't stand up as well as the previous brand did it did stand up on its own.

The bag coupled with the recipes make this a very easy way for you to try out raw cacao powder to see if it is something you'd like to use regularly in your diet.

But then I saw reviews for this San Francisco Bay French Roast--I like a bold cuppa--and decided to try it. Its cheaper price was also a motivator as was the packaging. Truth be told, Keurigs are horrible for the environment, and my experience using those reusable cups has been pretty dismal--even the boldest coffee seems to come out weak.

The SFB coffee comes in the more environmentally friendly meshy cup, meaning less plastic. Plus it's organic too.

My big box came today, and mid-afternoon, I decided to try a cup. Bold, smooth, not bitter. Just right.

I will be drinking this from now on. Love you Newman's, but between the lower cost and the more environmentally-friendly packaging, San Francisco Bay is my new morning jolt.

review_headline: Terrific ~ Tastes just like real lemonaid, although a bit on the tart side
review_body:
If you enjoy the taste of fresh lemonade, you'll be delighted with the taste of these. The only issue that some people might have is that the flavor changes slightly as you're sucking on it. Initially, the sweetness level is the same as fresh sweetened lemonade, but after about a minute, there's a stage where it becomes very tart, too much so for my taste. The last third of the candy returns to the original sweetness level, maybe even more so.

The bottom line for me is that I enjoy the first minute of sucking on this candy the best, as it tastes exactly like real sweetened fresh lemonade. The second stage is too sour for me, but thankfully it doesn't last long. The final stage returns to the taste you get when you first start sucking on these, but than becomes a little too sweet for me. All in all a nice candy, but not perfect for all.

product_title: Melitta Java Jig, Reusable K-Cups for Keurig K-Cup Brewers, Uses Melitta Paper Coffee Filters,2 cups and 30 filters
review_body:
I'm giving this 2 stars because when it works, It's decent at best.

I rarely leave reviews, but my frustrations from this thing caused me to seek out amazon to leave this review.

First off, as others have said it's cheaply made. I personally got a Keurig so I didn't have to put together filters and parts and all that jazz, but k-cups get expensive (especially when i drink 2-3 cups of coffee a day) so I decided to try this instead of going with Keurig Approved My K-Cup (which i still haven't used).

First off assembly. When I wakeup, i really don't feel like putting together ANYTHING. I'm the person who accidentally forgets a coffee cup under the coffee spout and spills coffee everywhere, putting stuff together is no good for me. But this has a 3 step process (assuming it's been washed, and you didn't leave it in the coffee pot).

Second, if the filter gets wet, might as well toss it. Because it's going to tear or be punctured and spill coffee grinds into your cofee, and honestly what is worse than that?

Third: I have ALWAYS used the 2nd option for coffee strength, and quantity. When I use the Javajig, it fills my cup up maybe 1/4th of the way, which I assume is because the spout is blocked with coffee grinds. So ontop of having little to no coffee, when I open the lid, coffee grinds & hot water fly all over the place.

Fourth, I'll just say Clean up sucks. I hate the feeling of coffee grinds, and even when this thing works, your hands are going to be covered in them while trying to clean the piece.

I have been using and attempting to use this thing, at least once a day for the last 2 weeks, and it has worked twice.

If you are like me, moody in the morning before you have your coffee, steer clear, because this thing will only make it worse.

product_title: Organic Raw Maca Powder, 2 LB Grade AAA+
review_body:
Literally just received this and tried it. I was a bit skeptical because I don't usually receive large packages of brown powder. Whomever put my package together though seemed to take great care ensuring that it was probably sealed and dated correctly. After opening the package I noticed that there was a small package of Chlorella samples, a Natural Calm magnesium supplement sample, and a copy of a handwritten thank you letter (in cursive). Overall, the packaging was neat and well sealed. A+

After opening everything, I took a whiff of the Maca Powder and was surprised that it didn't smell that bad. To me, it kind of smelled kind of nutty but not bad at all. I mixed 1 tablespoon with a few ounces of warm water, it shook it up, and down the hatch no problem. I wouldn't say it was tasted good but something I think I'll be able to take it everyday. I also mix wheat grass powder the similar way so I'm hoping that my body responds well to these.

I gave this 4/5 because literally just received it and wanted to review my intial reaction to it (having no previous experience with maca). After a few weeks I'll come back and post an update. My verdict so far is that this product seems worth the buy to me because my body agrees with it and the seller did a great job on packaging and the free samples. Those were awesome.

20 AUG 14 EDIT: Been taking this for about a month now. I take it with powder wheat grass and it goes down pretty easy. My energy levels have been much better and I feel like healthier since taking this. Will definitely buy again seeing how good of experience the first buy was. I take two servings a day of this stuff and still have maybe 1 - 2 weeks worth left. Worth 5 stars IMO.

product_title: Raw Almonds from California - 10 (1 Lb) Resealable Packages
review_body:
I have been a customer of CAlmonds for 3 years. (I never wrote a review for them before because usually I am too busy, and also there is enough reviews extolling their almonds already. But I am writing today, because of my most recent--superb--experience with their customer service.)

First, about almonds: I compared CAlmonds to Whole Foods market's bulk almonds and Azur Standard almonds (also from California, and also raw). CAlmonds are fresher (softer, less dry, and more flavourful) than WF's almonds; and they are very similar to Azur almonds in quality, but at a much better pricepoint. Also, as CAlmonds only processes nuts, I feel safe about my gluten sensitivities. Regarding sprouting: in my experience, it varies by the batch. I was unable to sprout almonds in my very first batch, but almonds in some of the subsequent batches did sprout. (The most recent batch that I have been able to sprout was ordered on May 2, 2014.) Regarding storing: I suggest freezer, especially if bought in bulk.

The highlights about the Customer Service: they respond within 24 hours, they are very clear and respectful in their communication, and if there is a problem, as I had recently, they resolve it to the highest of the customer's satisfaction. In my shopping experience, this is a rare and precious thing.

So by now, my husband and I tried their regular almonds and their walnuts, switched from buying individually packed bags to buying 10lb bags, and are now buying directly from their website (and I find it very convenient that it is linked to my amazon card). I hope they stay in and grow as a business for a long time, and I anticipate eating through many more bags of their wonderful nuts. Thank you, CAlmonds!

review_headline: A little more progresso and it'll be perfetto!
review_body:
I'm a tomato fanatic. It's my favorite fruit. Love all the ways the tom can be used in cooking.
And I enjoy a good tomato soup.
Obviously homemade is best but who has the time to prepare it, or the energy?

Campbell's tomato? Eh! It's almost orangey-red and is loaded with corn syrup.
Besides, soup from concentrate is one step away from dessicated powder in a packet.

Now PROGRESSO HEARTY TOMATO soup is near perfect!
Love that dark red color, and its blend of spices is wonderful.
My only problem is the lumps of tomato sour the experience for me.
I almost want to fish them out beforehand, or maybe puree the can's contents, then heat.

My ideal Progresso soup would have the same ingredients but no lumps,
just tiny bits of tomato for some texture, also a sprinkling of rice.

Recipe for Death Chowder:
Make a can of this in a crock pot.
Mince up ~1 cup of shallots and throw them in.
Throw in a few pounds of shrimp and/or crawfish/crayfish (if you are rich you could go lobster/crab)
Cube up ~2 lbs of potatoes, blanch and air dry them to bring out some starch (if you want to cheat toss them in cornstarch and let them sit and dry a bit). Deep fry these to golden brown and either sit them in a bowl beside and let people add them to their own bowl or stir them in right before you serve.
VERY OPTIONAL: Old Bay or Cajun seasoning to taste.

If you want to make Death Pies just cut out the potatoes, double the meat, and bake in a flaky pie crust. If you use a mini pie maker they will look harmless and not like 1000+ calorie food bombs.

Everyone who eats these should be dead of cardiac arrest within the hour. If there are any survivors, add a 2 lbs of diced fried bacon to the next batch.

review_headline: This makes the world's healthiest and easiest lunch - packed with protein and fiber
review_body:
How much do I love these lentils? I use them in an Ethiopian stew that I bring for lunch every day of my life. It is filling, cheap, and tasty. And good for your waistline. Here's the recipe:

1 cup lentils...boiled in 4 cups water (bring to boil, then turn to simmer)
Add:
One half onion and 3-4 cloves garlic, sautéed (makes a big difference if you sautée them before adding!)
One 6oz can tomato paste
1 tsp cayenne pepper -- leave this out if you are a spice wimp
1 tsp garam masala
1 tsp salt
2 packets truvia (or sugar, or whatever you like)
1 tsp ginger
1 tbsp paprika

Then just let it all simmer for up to 35 min. Cool it a bit before you taste it. Add what you think is necessary (sometimes I add more sugar/truvia to balance out the spicy and the acidity from the tomato)

product_title: Come With Me Kitty Harness and Bungee Leash
review_headline: A Little Snug in Some Areas and Loose in Others
review_body:
I like the idea of this. However, I think the problem may be that like humans, some cats have odd bodies. Though you can adjust this harness, there are limits. My cat seemed like he should fit this. He seems small...but even when fully adjusted, this harness is too snug around his stomach. Meanwhile, the other part of the harness slips off of him. I bought the larger size for my cat, and it fit better around his stomach...but it seemed tighter in other areas. Also be advised that if you have an animal that has arthritis or has suffered some past injuries, the harness may be uncomfortable for them. My cat is funny about the area behind his front legs. Also notice if your animal is frightened of certain colors. When I got the larger size, I chose a red leash. It turns out that my cat freaks out whenever he sees something red.

Ask yourself several questions before you purchase this:
1) Has your animal been declawed and/or neutered? (Declawing (and neutering a young animal) can stunt growth, which might make your cat's body odd--this happened to my cat).
2) Is your animal a mix? (Also can cause strange proportions if you mix a large breed with a smaller one)
3) Is your animal a rescue pet? (Mine is...and the problem with rescue pets is they come with emotional baggage. My cat seems to associate anything red with a fear that he is going to be hit. This isn't something he learned from me)

The leash and harness are sturdy, and if fit on a well proportioned cat, it will probably work very nicely. The instructions and information provided were very thorough. However, if you have a rescue pet...be very patient and watch them carefully.

product_title: Reeds Crystallized Ginger in Tin, 10-Ounces  (Pack of 4)
review_body:
When the label says “Net Wt. 10 Oz.,” you might think you’re buying a fairly small product. Not so. It’s actually bigger than my palm, too big to put in a suit coat pocket, full of dozens of pieces of baby ginger root. The pieces are fairly large, but because the crystallizing process removes the water, the large pieces are lightweight. Because the pieces have less mass, but full flavor, you get way more taste than the light weight suggests.

This product has only two ingredients: “Diced baby ginger root, raw cane sugar.” The sugar makes the fibrous dried ginger go down easily, but isn’t so sweet that it tastes like mere candy. The uncomplicated recipe makes me feel good after having to swear off mass-packaged snacks for my health. Real ginger, not processed ginger extract or expeller-pressed ginger oil, doesn’t just taste good; its natural properties help fire the blood.

I like to pop a cube in my mouth and just hold it, as the sugar and ginger oil dissolve on my tongue; this lets the ginger burn coat my mouth. Doing that, one or two pieces can last over ten minutes, and the ginger flavor lingers long after the pieces dissolve away. This light, natural snack has the luxurious qualities of a rich dessert, without the heavy calories and fat; you can enjoy this snack without feeling weighed down and heavy.

Admittedly, this stuff isn’t cheap. Being made with real food ingredients, not synthesized pseudo-food, it’s pricier to produce and transport, and doesn’t store forever. However, if you like flavorful snacks that satisfy your appetite without leaving you feel bloated, or just something you can enjoy without worrying about tooth decay, here’s your snack. I’ve become quite the ginger lover recently, and this stuff just proves me right.

review_headline: Not as awesome as I'd hoped
review_body:
I was excited to try these flavorings because I love popcorn and I love topping my popcorn with tasty things. And what an incredible variety! Unfortunately, I got my hopes up too high.

These flavorings fall down in a couple of areas:
- They don't stick to your popcorn unless you use a generous amount of butter. I was trying to "dip" oil-popped popcorn in a small amount of each flavor for my taste test and had to press hard to get any to stick to the popcorn. The kettle corn was particularly difficult to get to stick.

- Most of the flavors are just not to my taste. If you like actual parmesan cheese on your popcorn, you will be incredibly disappointed by the flavors. The powdering and preservation pretty much kills the cheddar. The butter had a chemical after-taste. Caramel was just odd. Bacon cheddar tasted like imitation bacon bits. I liked the cheesy jalapeno the best, but it still was very artificial tasting. The ranch was probably the closest to what I expected.

These would be fun for rainy summer days when you're trapped inside with a movie as a fun experiment. However, if you really enjoy your popcorn and dislike chemical flavors, these flavorings probably aren't for you.

product_title: Jolly Time KettleMania Microwave Popcorn Sweet and Salty Gourmet Kettle Corn
review_body:
I was buying the Heuermann's brand for years, until they went out of business. Purchased a case at that point and finally ran out. This one is the closest to that for me.

What I look for in a kettle corn is a fairly even combination of sweet, salty, and buttery tasting. This one does have that.

You have to really watch it, however, as all the caramelized stuff is on one side of the bag and it can burn easily. I watch, toward the end, and as soon as it goes one second without popping, I pull it out. It's usually fine until the last 4-8 seconds, but sometimes it is fine to the end.

I use the 'popcorn' button on my Sharp microwave, for reference.

Of course, every single kernel doesn't have all the flavors. That's just the way it is. But it's enough that I enjoy it.

As for percentage that pops vs percentage of kernels that are dead - I find that I've had anywhere from six to eighteen dead ones. That's a pretty decent average, IMO. It's usually between six and twelve.

One more thing - about the 'Insta-bowl' deal that shows on the picture here - I don't know what that's about. The ones I received are in the regular microwave popcorn bags. I would have poured it out into a regular bowl anyway, but it's worth mention.
