product_title: Palmetto Farms White Stone Ground Grits 2 LB - Non-GMO - Just All Natural Corn, No Additives - Naturally Gluten Free, Produced in a Wheat Free Facility - Grinding Grits Since 1934
review_body:
These are the best grits we have found since leaving South Carolina many years ago. We have purchased stone ground grits from several different mills over the years but these are the only ones that have been ground ready to cook. If the grits are too coarse you will be cooking them until lunchtime or they will require regrinding in a coffee mill. If they are ground too fine they will be like supermarket grits and may be used for hanging wallpaper. Palmetto Farms Stone Ground Grits have the correct grind.
Now to prepare the grits. You may find this recipe better than the instructions on the bag. My wife (Southern Lady) has been preparing grits for many years. Each grind requires changes to the preparation. For Palmetto Farms Stone Ground Grits, here is her recipe for four servings.
½ Cup Grits
½ Cup Milk
1 3/4 Cups Water
¾ Teaspoon salt
¼ Teaspoon freshly ground pepper
Bring Milk, Water, Salt, and Pepper to a boil in medium saucepan.
Sprinkle ½ Cups grits into center of pan while stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat to low and cover.
Set timer for 20 minutes and stir every 5 minutes while cooking.
If not tender enough after 20 minutes continue cooking another 10 minutes, stirring after 5 minutes.
Burners vary so you may need to raise the heat from low to medium low to maintain a slow bubble.
Serve with patty of butter on each serving.
Good for Breakfast or as a Side for Seafood or Meats.

Spread leftover grits about an inch thick in a pan and chill. When firm, cut and sprinkle one side with salt and pepper, then dust both sides with flour and fry in a combo of oil and butter turning once when lightly browned. The flour will prevent the grits from popping like popcorn all over your cooktop.
I recommend these grits for anyone who appreciates genuine southern grits.

product_title: Nongshim Shin Noodle Black Cup
review_headline: Awesome Flavor, A Bit Overpriced - Blame Nong Shim's Marketing
review_body:
Coming from a 1st generation Korean family (meaning my parents emigrated from Korea), I grew up as one would expect in a Korean household. That includes culture, beliefs, and food. For a good portion of my life (almost 2 decades), I grew up on eating instant Korean noodles. This ranges from the Neoguri, to Jin Ramyun, to Chappaghetti, to Kimchi Ramyun, etc. If it was a Korean brand of instant noodle, I've probably eaten it. It wasn't until recently I was getting tired of the same old noodles and wanted to try something new. I drove to my local Korean supermarket and bought several \\"new brands\\" of instant Korean noodles, with Shin Ramyun Black being one of them.

For those of you familiar with the original Shin Ramyun, I can tell you that Shin Ramyun Black is quite a bit more flavorful. The Black version comes with 3 packets of seasoning/mix vs the regular version's two packets. These packets consist of the soup base, the vegetable mix, and the \\"sul-long tang\\" soup base. For those of you that don't know what that is, \\"sul-long-tang\\" is a Korean soup made typically of beef bones and sometimes beef slices. Traditionally this soup is white/cream colored because of the long (several hours) simmering effect of boiling beef bones. The marrow eventually gets cooked into the water, creating a beefy creamy/milky flavor. In my opinion, this is what makes the Black version taste so much different than the original. Aside from that, the vegetable mix contains chunkier vegetables with a small bits of dehydrated beef. Personally I think the flavor of this soup is superior to the original... but it comes at a cost....

For those of you that are curious about this product, know that it is nearly double the price of the original Shin Ramyun. I guess Nong Shim considers them \\"premium\\" noodles (as the packaging states), but is it worth it? You have to ask yourself, is one single packet worth the double price? Not really despite the tasty flavor. However, I ended up getting these on an Amazon Lightning deal for 50% off, so they ended up being the same price as the regular cup noodle version, that's why I took a stab at it. So if you really want to try these, you can give it a go either on Amazon or your local Asian grocery.wever, I ended up getting these on an Amazon Lightning deal for 50% off, so they ended up being the same price as the regular cup noodle version, that's why I took a stab at it. So if you really want to try these, you can give it a go either on Amazon or your local Asian grocery.

review_body:

Once you do, however, you'll have a perfectly good noodle substitute with no fishy aftertaste. They do have a slightly different consistency than wheat noodles, but it's not hard to get used to.

I'm gluten intolerant (I get major acid reflux within minutes of eating any wheat product), so it's nice to have a gluten free alternative. We've also been trying to eat lower carb to loose weight, so these are perfect for our family.

While you can use these for a spaghetti style Italian dish, I think they are best suited for Asian recipes. Think of them more as a replacement for rice noodles than a replacement for wheat noodles and you're sure to be happy. The simplest way to enjoy them is to simply boil them as instructed (rinse first!) and then toss with toasted sesame oil, soy sauce, lime juice, maybe some cilantro. Yum! They would probably make a great pad thai, though I haven't tried it with these yet.

product_title: Ceylon Tea Sri Lanka Tea Black Tea By Yes!sir
review_body:
If you are new to tea whole leaf tea and steeping tea, Black Ceylon is basically a nice, plain foundation. Variations of it are found in most teabags. It's also the basis for most black tea blends- most flavored teas, if they aren't herbal, are created with a Ceylon as the base, and then flavor is added to it.

This is a nice, whole body Ceylon. Nice crisp taste with no bitterness or "chalky" feeling in the mouth. I use a heaping teaspoon in 12 ounces of boiling water, and I only steep for 3 minutes, stirring once during the steeping. It's very easy for Ceylons to get bitter if you use too much or you let it steep too long.

The tea came beautifully packaged in a tall tin, with a sealed bag inside. Honestly, I prefer my tea tins squat and wide so they fit into a drawer, and I can scoop the last leaves out when I am running low, but these tins look beautiful on the counter near my kettle.

Fresh and crisp. This is a nice basic tea, and a good ceylon to add to your collection.

review_headline: High Quality, Great Color, Subtle Flavor
review_body:
If you're shopping here you have probably used saffron before. But a few interesting points about saffron: it is a spice derived from the saffron crocus flower. There are only three red stigmas on each flower. These stigmas are where the saffron comes from. Saffron crocus are native to Greece and southwest Asia and it is one of the world's most costly spices by weight. Knowing this helps to understand the cost associated with it and to appreciate that Mehr saffron is thoroughly dried, not only for longevity, but a lower weight.

Additionally, powdered saffron will not last as long as threads but the rule of thumb is that you should use half the amount of powdered saffron than threads. So 1/2 teaspoon of saffron threads = 1/4 teaspoon of saffron powder.

These are small and nice little corked jars with nice, bright red powdered saffron, filled with flavor and aroma. I have enjoyed the beauty of cooking with this saffron, in rice and other dishes. It adds a wonderful deep yellow color while infusing a subtle but exquisite flavor. You don't need a lot to make a difference, which is good because one jar doesn't last long. It is worth investing in better quality powdered saffron since lower grade versions can have additional powders added in and will take more product to reach the same flavor.

Mehr Saffron is top notch with saffron bright in color and fresh and the packaging makes it like opening a little gift each time you use it.

I was provided a jar for trial and an honest review.

product_title: MTR Mixed VegetablePickle, 10.58-Ounce Plastic Bottles (Pack of 8)
review_headline: Chemical odor and taste, soupy, not satisfactory
review_body:
This pickle tastes and looks nothing like what you'd get in a restaurant, and nothing like what you typically get in glass jar at the store. Let me preface: I love pickle. I don't care if it's mixed, mango, lime... I'm hooked on it and have been eating it for years.

I ordered this 8-pack, and I'm unsatisfied enough that I am strongly considering returning the whole lot.

On opening the first of eight containers, I took a big whiff and it smells like chemicals to me. Thought it may just be a fluke, tasted it, and it tastes like chemicals. Compared that to a jar of Vimal brand mixed pickle and a jar of Khazana mixed pickle... neither one smell or taste like this.

The product is overly liquid and runny. Very similar to a can of vegetable soup. It's got great heat, perfect for me, but I can't get beyond the taste.

When opening the first one, there was a great deal of vacuum on the plastic container it arrived in. I wanted to be sure I didn't get a bad jar before posting a review, so I opened a second container from the pack - same thing.

Final test, I shared it today with coworkers natively from Pakistan and India that I eat lunch with daily at my office, and they thought it tasted strange as well. That's when I decided someone needed to post a lengthy review to describe the product.

Personally, if you're reading this and the previous reviews made you think it could be worthwhile (like I did), I'm here to say: It's ain't so. I would go with another brand. This stuff is cheap and low quality, certainly reflected by the price.

If you want something closer to authentic, I'd recommend you buy something from Patak's, Vimal, Mother's or Sanjeev Kapoor Khazana instead. It's going to be closer to what you're going to get at a local restaurant if they're not making their own in-house.

If you're looking for a great, nutritious yogurt type product, you might like to try this blueberry lowfat kefir which you can drink or eat from a cup with a spoon. I learned about kefir in the book The 17 Day Diet: A Doctor's Plan Designed for Rapid Results. A nutritionist recommended having protein for breakfast and combining protein with fruit such as berries. I love to make fruit smoothies with this kefir: one banana, one cup frozen berries, 1/2 cup kefir and 1/2 cup berry juice or 1/2 cup seltzer for fewer calories and grams of sugar. Protein keeps you from getting hungry said the nutritionist.

This kefir is great to drink for breakfast or when you don't have time to make a smoothie in the morning. This kefir is probiotic and great for digestion with 12 different kinds of bacteria, and is naturally cultured. Kefir provides 25% of Vitamin D, 30% Calcium and 11g of Protein. The plain low-fat yogurt I buy has 15g of sugar per cup and this kefir has 20g of sugar in a cup -- which is less than most juices. It's a great breakfast, lunch or snack option. A cup is about 140 calories.

If you are looking for a healthy and tasty probiotic food that is high in protein and other nutritious ingredients, while being low in calories, you might want to try this tasty product. It tastes as good as most desserts, and when I don't have time to make a smoothie in the morning, I just have this kefir instead. It's also a tasty and healthy snack.

review_body:
They taste really good, but it's nothing magical. Just some good crackers. I don't think they are particularly healthy, like any other crackers. Overall I am very happy with them, but would not lose any sleep over it if costco took them off the shelf.

However, everyone saying these are like eating crackers with sand are just huge babies. There are some small crispy seeds, but I like them. They do kind of *sound* like sand when you eat them, but without the discomfort of biting into sand. They're about like poppy seeds, maybe a bit crispier than that. It's the kind of thing a reasonable person expects when they get exotic grain crackers.

As always, make sure you read the actual reviews (not just the ratings) because anyone can write reviews, and clueless crybabies like writing them more than most people do.

Purchased here, these are about double the in-store price.

It does work for that, but I still think that tea leaves need to sit in hot water for a longer period of time, but it does work.  After much experimentation I've found that if you put your loose leaf tea in a Magic Bullet and blend it to a fine powder, then it works great in the Brew and Save. product_title: Zhena's Gypsy Tea Chocolate Chai Organic Loose Tea, 16-Ounce Bag
review_body:
I love this tea. The flavor is great, not too peppery but you can definitely taste the spices. For those thinking of buying this, keep in mind that it has a rooibos base rather than a black tea base as most chai tea does. This definitely gives it a different flavor than other chai mixes. But the rooibos adds another flavor dimension, and makes it caffeine-free, as well.

My favorite way to make this is 1/3rd water, 1/3rd vanilla almond milk and 1/3rd chocolate milk. I add everything to a sauce pot (including 1/8th cup of chai mix), slowly bring it to 180 degrees, then shut off the heat and let it steep for 10 minutes. Another benefit of rooibos is that you can't over-steep it, like you can with regular black tea leaves. Add a little sweetener (I use Splenda) and it's a perfect cup on a cold winter's day.

product_title: Tea Fete de Versailles
review_body:

Breathe in deeply, and you will know what this tea smells like and tastes like. There is also a candy-like sweetness to the scent from the floral aspect. The orange is so natural, without a hint of anything artificial.

Don't think of this as just a Christmas tea. The snowy white tin with starry gold filigree is beautiful. The absence of cinnamon and clove make it more multiseasonal to me. I will be serving it for my New Year's Day tea time. The black tea base is strong enough to stand as a breakfast tea, fancy enough to be an afternoon blend. review_headline: Great formula with the least harmful additives
review_body:
I have been on a search for a organic formula that does not contain soy or other processed by-products or additives and this is the only one on the market that I have found that is the most straight forward, least contaminated formula product out there. Aside from making my own formula, I realistically don't have time to do that, but this is an excellent product in it's place. I am a firm believer of giving my children the best products that have the least likely hood of having adverse effects on their development, and this one seemed to be the best option.

I exclusively breast-fed my little guy until he was about 9-10 months old, and began to supplement with this formula even though this is technically a toddler formula. (My little guy has been plagued with ear infections and side lying to nurse was not comfortable for him at all, which is why he began to self wean. I was able to give him this formula in addition to the pumped breast milk and feedings that I could coax him into in addition to giving him coconut oil and mashed avocado to maintain a higher nutrient and fat content that this formula lacks that a infant formula would otherwise have.)

In comparison to other organic and non-organic formulas, this one is an excellent source of absorbable iron, which at his one year appointment he checked out in normal range for, as opposed to my first born whom I used other brands of formula exclusively from 9 months on and he ended up being low on iron and needing supplementation. I don't know if I can credit it specifically to the formula alone since the circumstances were not identical, nor are my children; but from what I understand and have already mentioned, the iron in this product is of higher absorbancy.

My only complaint-which isn't really a complaint; a direct result of this product not containing additives/products, is that it does not need are that it does not contain emulsifiers and shaking a bottle of this formula justcreates a large amount of bubbles, just as shaking a glass of milk. Stirring this formula into the water is my personal recommendation to avoid the bubbles. You also must swirl the bottle around to reconstitute the formula as it does tend to separate quickly, again due to the fact that it does not contain garbage ingredients that are not good for your baby.

There usually wasn't a whole lot in the cup, which leads me to to believe that a lot of brands have the same quality for their non-coffee K-Cups.  The packaging was fine. it came in a bag within a box. There was no way for damage & I received all 30 cups.  The only thing I would've improved on, was the number of regular coffee cups in the selection. It doesn't seem like it's quite as much variety if you've got 9 kinds of regular coffee... Of course, I'm a fru-fru coffee drinker and  love flavored coffee.  I realize this is just a personal preference.  In the future, I'd add more varieties of beverages, as well. But for someone who just purchases a Keurig & doesn't know their favorites, yet, this is a good way to go & more for your money than wasting $6 on a pack at the grocery store in which you may be uncertain.

product_title: A Taste of Thai Noodles Quick Meal (Pack of 6)
review_headline: Delicious, easy,  and lots of variation...
review_body:
I love these Thai meals. I love Thai food in general. These quick meals taste remarkably good and are done in just a few minutes. I also like that you can use these and mix them with other stuff to provide a lot of variation.

For the Thai Red Curry noodles, for instance, you can add a few pieces of fish, shrimp, chicken, pork, or beansprouts. You can also cook the noodles separate from the sauce and serve them both. Nobody has to know it came from a simple box. :)

A tip: break the noodles first, or else they will not be completely immersed in the water and cook unevenly. Stir well before you place it in the microwave, then microwave on high for 3 minutes and stir again, then 1 more minute in the microwave. If you add ingredients adjust the time as needed. After taking them out let it sit for a minute to allow the noodles to finish. (beware of hot steam coming from the box)

Note that this item on Amazon is actually cheaper then buying them in the grocery store. Even including shipping!

Also try the Peanut and Coconut Ginger flavors, they are just as great. The Pad Thai flavor is perhaps my least favorite, but still very good.

Recommended!!

review_headline: Even better than the real thing!

Obviously dough has to rise.  DUH!  I would've thought any adult human would realize this, but I suppose that isn't so.  I might also add that I am by no means a cook, or baker!  Anyway, I can honestly admit that I will never purchase another $2+ pretzel from the Auntie Anne store ever again, because these FAR surpassed theirs! Every time I go to an Auntie Anne's, the pretzels are thin, and in most cases, they appear burnt.  This is not the thick and delicious Auntie Anne's pretzels they started the company with; but with the economy, I realize things change and go downhill.  I am extremely thrilled they offer this option though!  When we bake these, we don't make \\"pretzel\\" shaped pretzels.  We take two balls of dough, roll them, and then twist them together to make a HUGE FLUFFY stick!  It is absolutely to die for!  We obviously can't finish them all at once because we are only a family of 3, but we stick them in the fridge, and they stay good for a few days.  Just pop them in the microwave for a few seconds, and voila!  Super deliciousness!

product_title: Let's Do Organic Creamed Coconut, 7-Ounce Boxes
review_headline: great creamed coconut -- more versitle than coconut milk
review_body: I've found many uses for this product in my cooking. It is great in soups and curries.  I like it much better than coconut milk. product_title: Raw Almonds from California - 10 (1 Lb) Resealable Packages
review_headline: Reasonable quality almonds, but nothing to write home about.
review_body:
Well-packaged, shipped quickly.

How good are these almonds?

Depends on what you want them for. For baking or slivering into large amounts of other food (say, salads,) these will do just fine. For snacking out of hand, plain, to me they're not all that great.

My comparison & reference point to date is organic plain almonds purchased in the bulk bin at Whole Foods.

Cosmetics: Uniform, healthy brown color, smaller size than most supermarket almonds. All whole almonds in the bag, almost no pieces or dust. No off odors in the bag or flavors in the almond.

Texture: Reasonably OK, neither super-crunchy & dry nor overly soft / damp.

Flavor: Average, nothing objectionable, but nothing all that tasty either.

Sprouting: Haven't tested them, but would not be surprised if they do not sprout, due to CA and/or US regulations on pasteurizing, etc.

----
Nota bene: I just got these today & so far I've opened 2 of the 10 individual 1-pound bags, and eaten a total of about 1 cup of almonds. I think it's a fair chance that the other 8 bags are like these 2, but if they're significantly different in any way I'll edit & update this review.

product_title: Knorr Rice Sides
review_body:
i loooove the knorr sides!
i like to \\"play\\" with them a bit and make them even better.
what i do with this flavor is that i saute garlic and some chopped chili peppers(dry coarse ground would be fine too) in some oil(dont use olive oil in this flavor) and then add the rice mix with 2 1\4 cup water and then i let it boil.
when it does boil i cover it(with a pot cover and a small kitchen towel under the cover) and cook it on the LOWEST heat on my stove top for 10 mins........then open and stir the rice and quickly seal the pot again and cock for another 10 mins(total of 20 mins).
shut off the heat of the stove top and let it stand for 10 mins.
open the cover and stir the rice and enjoy! :-))
i love this one soo much! :-)

TIP: the only small problem i have with this flavor of the knorr sides is that it dosent have enough of a \\"cheese\\" flavor to it. so what i do is add two tablespoons of shredded cheddar cheese to the rice after the 20 min cooking time of the rice is over.
so i just open up the pan lid and stir in the cheese and close the lid and let stand for 10 min and thats it :-)

review_headline: Nuts for PB2 Powdered Peanut Butter!
review_body:
Nuts for PB2 Powdered Peanut Butter!

When I first came across this product I was in a small boutique and was told 'everyone who's bought this has been back for more - it's so popular the manufacturer can't keep up with demand for the smaller containers of chocolate peanut butter'. They must've ramped up production because I'm starting to be able to find the jars of powder locally. I was thrilled to be able to find this product on Amazon where I can take advantage of Prime shipping-- as my local stores aren't carrying the larger value packages yet.

Originally we only ate the PB2 by dipping freshly cut fruits (bananas!!!) in the powder, now we've begun turning it into 'peanut butter'. When mixing the product with water it offers a rich peanut taste, and a peanut-butterish consistency (thick though obviously not as oily as oils have been extracted from the product and so a little less dense). I absolutely adore adding a tiny squeeze of syrup or honey to add back in some of the sweetness (though it's great without it). I love eating it on crackers or apples.

With less oil and none of the sugar of normal peanut butter this product has less than half the normal calories of an equivalent amount of peanut butter!!!! But with 99.9% of the taste! (Dance). Any peanut butter lover I've given this to so far has adored it and is faced with a challenge ---> If it has less than half the calories should I eat twice as much? Or eat the same amount I usually do -- and benefit from a lower calorie snack? <---

The chocolate flavored powder tastes very much like peanut butter to me - and I prefer purchasing the traditional peanut butter flavored powder (I'd eventually like to try some of the widely varying and plentiful recipes available on the BellPlantation PB2 website and I felt the original flavor would be more versatile.).

product_title: Luwak Star Gourmet Coffee, 100% Arabica Sumatra Gayo Luwak Coffee from Indonesia (or Kopi Luwak) Whole Beans, Medium Roast, 150 Gram (0.33 Lb) Bag, Roasted in the U.S
review_body:
Kopi luwak is made from the beans of coffee berries that have been eaten and excreted--yes, you read that right!--by the Asian palm civet. To make this coffee, the civets are typically snatched from their homes and life in the wild to be imprisoned alone in tiny, barren cages. They're deprived of everything that is natural and important to them, including freedom, exercise, space--even real food. They bite at the cage bars, turn in circles, and go insane from being imprisoned with no escape. Deprived of adequate nutrition, they begin to lose their fur. All of this cruelty is just for a novelty coffee sold by companies such as Amazon.com. We're asking the company, as a leader in global online retail sales, to learn the ugly truth behind this coffee from this recent investigation and end the sale of kopi luwak.

[...]

Animal cruelty during the production of one of the world's priciest coffees has been exposed by a BBC investigation.

Kopi luwak is made from coffee beans excreted by Indonesian palm civets - small, mongoose-like creatures.

But undercover reporters in Indonesia witnessed civets held in battery-cage conditions to produce the coffee.

And experts say they are \\"totally convinced\\" kopi luwak from caged animals ends up on the London market.

review_headline: Tasty non-refrigerated add-in for instant coffee at the office

Also, it's hard to keep milk in an office. Other people will drink it, and even at best I'd have to keep it freshly stocked. My memory being as poor as it is, I'd end up having uselessly soured milk most of the time.

Enter these International Delight creamers. They don't require refrigeration, so they can stay safe and sound under my desk. I use 2 creamers in each cup of coffee, and at 1 cup per day this is a 144 workday supply (over 7 months!)

Unfortunately, the case I received had an expiration date a mere 5 months after delivery so I'm going to have to throw a bunch out.(Actually, they've just expired and I put in another order today for a case).

Despite not using almost a third of the creamers, the pricing on this case is still a great deal! Check it out for yourself; I've found 50 counts on Amazon selling for the same price as this 288-count! Combined with fee Prime shipping, it's a fantastic deal.

They're tasty, too! They're also not very healthy, but I figure a couple per day won't be the end of me.

All in all, I'd highly recommend this item (assuming you like this sort of artificially flavored milk substitute as I do).

product_title: Whole Wheat Bread Mix
review_headline: Like the bread, but stars reduced due to price DOUBLING
review_body:
Good grief. When I ordered this product, it was $11.15 for a pack of 4. That's $2.78 a loat -- very reasonable. Now I look at it, and it's ~*23.99*~?!? GOOD NIGHT IRENE! That's $6 a loaf! There is no way on God's green earth that I am paying $6 a loaf for ANY bread. That's just absurd. It's delicious, but price has to be a consideration. I can't consider this product any longer.

I'm committed to whole wheat bread, but live where the selections at the grocery store are 1) limited, and 2) not very tasty.

This mix bakes up beautifully in my machine. I use the Whole Wheat setting; this MAKES A DIFFERENCE in your final product. If your machine doesn't HAVE a WW setting, look at the MANUAL and see what the manufacturer suggests with regard to WW. Email them and ask, if you have to.

But on WW setting, Medium crust, this 1.5-lb loaf comes out crispy on the outside and chewy on the inside. When it cools, the crispiness does soften, leaving you with a lovely, sliceable loaf.

This makes lovely toast, and can be sliced thin enough for sandwiches, and still hold up, and not crumble. I like the seeds that are mixed in; my son doesn't like them.

The loaf is ...bread machine shaped... of course, so it's kind of different from a bagged loaf from the store. One hearty slice of this is probably equivalent to two sissy slices of grocery WW. But much more tasty and satisfying.

This keeps well in a [[ASIN:B001BB2LMM Bread Keeper]] for 2-3 days. Refrigerates well for several days longer. Freezes well -- slice a loaf in advance, freeze, and pull out slices for toast.

If this mix turns out \\"dark\\" or \\"heavy\\" for you -- it's probably operator error, or a machine setting. This makes a lovely, beige, springy, tasty loaf! (Done correctly.)

review_body:
I purchased Amazing Grass Chocolate three months ago. I have pretty poor eating habits that consist of a lot of fast food and little healthy, home cooked meals. Vegetables really aren't high on the list priorities (do French Fries count?). So I bought this product to supplement a poor diet with something healthier. I mix a scoop of Amazing Grass with a scoop of chocolate protein and some milk. I've noticed that vigorous shaking for about a minute smooths the product out quite nicely. Otherwise it is slightly lumpy (and it isn't due to the protein powder). It took a week or two to adjust to the slightly grassy, gritty taste of the product. Now I don't even notice any flavor nuances the product has.

The first week or so of taking the product it turned the bowels a lovely shade of green. Nowadays I have to admit that I do feel much more energetic and I swear the hair on my arms and hands are growing thicker (Maybe that is just from getting older). My skin feels less oily as well. Too bad the hair up top keeps falling out. Oh well, It it can't do everything I suppose. I do plan on continuing to use this product into the foreseeable future due the improvements in energy levels, and I think I'm going to keep a second serving with me for those especially long days that never seem to end. Great product.

product_title: Anis De Flavigny Original Anise French Mints 1.75 Ounce (Pack of 8)
review_body: I just love the taste of Anise, and these mints are just the ticket.  The mints provide a cool refreshing flavor, and are truly long lasting if you can manage not to bite down on them.  In fact, the package tells you, "Hard Mints, Do Not Bite."  The tins are just darling and would be perfect for any collector.  I discovered them, like other reviewers, at Epcot for 4.95 per case. product_title: Turbana Plantain Chips, 3 Ounce Bags (Pack of 24)
review_headline: Great flavor and plenty of chips
review_body: I was able to get the plain / lightly-salted flavor of these chips at my office until recently, and it seems that flavor is difficult to come by but these chips are just as good -- maybe a little better!  I'm a fan of lime flavor, and this has a nice amount of that (more than the just-a-hint-of-lime tortilla chips, but not so much that the taste is sour).  There are plenty of chips in each bag (three servings according to the packaging) and with 24 bags I'll have enough for a little while, but I'm probably going to purchase more when these run out.

product_title: Huy Fong Chili Garlic Sauce, 18-Ounce (Pack of 3)
review_headline: The sauce is delish and fantabulous- find some, get some, buy some! The shipping is a damn joke.
review_body:
This arrived BROKEN because it was poorly packaged. It then leaked all over everything else in the box, which was also poorly packaged, rendering most of my Amazon Mom delivery an expensive yet worthless disaster. Hey, I feel like maybe someone should inform you that a balled up sheet of paper isn't going to stop anything from moving around, isn't going to protect anything when it's moving around, and isn't going to make it any easier to clean up the mess from your incompetence.
*I've changed my rating from 1 to 3 stars- the PRODUCT itself is fantabulous! It tastes great, has a good heat, a little goes a long way, it's good in anything and everything and everything's great-grandchildren. Great stuff, seriously.
The shipping and packaging, however, are horrid. Mine was shipped with part of my Amazon Mom order. 3 plastic jars of this, in a sealed thin plastic bag, that was just tossed in the box with stuff for my 9 month old daughter. The only protective packing they even attempted was a long piece of brown paper, because they apparently believed the story of paper beating rock. Well, the box was then abused, probably because there was not a single warning on it that it contained something that could easily break and cause a mess. So, of course, the thin plastic jars busted and leaked to their little hearts' content all inside the thin plastic bag they were sealed in. It was like a little chili garlic sauce goldfish sack. Then, being the level of worthless thin plastic bags will be in situations such as this, my chili garlic sauce goldfish sack leaked all over the rest of the stuff shoved in the box- because washing super spicy sauce off of all the items and food meant for my 9 month old child is my favorite weekend activity.
Amazon has been kind enough to replace the chili garlic sauce portion of my order- we will see if they arrive in a more acceptable and usable manner- and apparently duck-all to my annoyance and less than stellar experience, as well as the rest of my now violated order.as the rest of my now violated order.

review_headline: The classiest tonic you'll ever imbibe.
review_body:
This tonic won't just change the way you feel about tonic, it might highlight all the less classy parts of your life.

After one G&T with this stuff, my mustache grew in like Tom Selleck and my voice dropped three octaves. I put a shot of it in some mediocre apple cider and discovered I was suddenly wearing a bowler and a monocle. I brought a bottle to a dinner party a few nights later, and within two hours we realized the living room we were sitting in had become a well-appointed parlour, and we were being served delicious highballs by a gentleman butler named Bradley. His tuxedo would have put us all to shame, but of course we were dressed to the nines.

Do you want to attend such a fancy party? Perhaps Bradley's Kinda Tonic is for you! Drink responsibly, it's hard to tie a cravat if you've had one too many. Perhaps Bradley will assist.

product_title: HiPP Organic 6-Month Organic Follow On Milk, 800g
review_body:
I waited a while after receipt to review to make sure I gave it some time to see how my baby liked Hipp. I was concerned about some of the ingredients in domestic organic formulas, and am just beginning to introduce formula at 7 months, since my supply has gone down some. I was in a pinch a few months back and gave her Similac and it was a nightmare - she screamed all night. I was concerned I would encounter the same reaction, but this stuff is...well...amazing.

Like other reviewers, I noticed that this formula does not smell like formula. It dissolves easily with a few swirls in a warm bottle and my baby didn't even blink at the taste! She seems to enjoy it! The best thing of all is that there have been no tummy issues...no gas, constipation, fussiness, or strange BM. I am so thrilled with this product and wish the ready-to-feed was also available on amazon.

It does take a while to arrive after purchase, so order a few if you can, and if I were to be really nitpicky, I'd ask they reevaluate the packaging, since it isn't really resealable...but none of that outweighs this fabulous product. After researching it and narrowing it down to Baby's Only or Hipp, I feel like I made the best choice for my baby.

review_body: This mix makes excellent waffles!  They are crispy on the outside and light and fluffy on the inside! It took a few tries to get them perfect, but the \\"secret\\" is to mix 1 cup cold water and 1 cup cold soda (my husband and I like Orange soda while my son loves Root Beer) then add 3 cups mix and stir only until large lumps disappear. We have the Presto Flip that was purchased on Amazon. Your Sunday breakfast just got better!  Enjoy, and play around with different soda favors, the possibilities are endless!

review_headline: Ahmad Blend of Ceylon loose tea with Earl Grey flavour
review_body:
A blend of tea that I was accustomed to drink and not easy to get. When I finally ordered it through Amazon, the tea came before the date it was supposed to arrive, very well packaged. At the same time I did not believe them because they publish all the ratings together with the offer and I read most of them before buying both tins. At the present time I have two tins that I bought more expensive than the ones I used to buy and Amazon denied me the opportunity of return only one tin.
My advice to future buyers: Believe me, I know a little about teas. This is not a good purchase at all. And last but not least, I stopped buying from Amazon because I feel deceive from them. product_title: Pampers Sensitive Baby Wipes - Unscented - 168 ct (3 - 56ct Travel Pack)
review_body:
These wipes come in a very convenient size and packaging. The individual packs have plastic snap close lids that ensure that the wipes will not dry out. The packs are a nice size for travel, yet you won't have to worry about running out too quickly.

They are soft and somewhat stretchy, with just a wavy line or two on each wipe for a pattern. They are otherwise smooth and soft, and therefore smooth and gentle on the skin.

There is no stickiness, no tackiness, no residue left on baby's skin. The skin just dries smooth, clean and soft. They are strong enough that your fingers wont poke through and they will not rip, but yet they are really soft.

The only scent on these is very faint. You will only smell it if you put them right up against your nose and to me they almost smell like elmers glue. That is not exactly a bad thing though since the scent is so very faint. Your baby definitely will not smell like glue :)
I even use these on my face every now and then throughout the day. some baby wipes I can use like that, while other ones seem to make my face feel a little sticky. These just make the skin feel clean. I also use them on the baby's face and body of course as needed and there is never any irritation.

product_title: Great Northern Popcorn Organic All Natural Yellow Gourmet Popcorn
review_body:
This tastes great! Glad to be able to find a reasonably priced organic popcorn.

For movie theater taste I like to put a layer of organic coconut oil in the bottom of a saucepan (enough to where the kernels are just barely submerged) , turn the stove on to medium heat, add 3-4 kernels and put a lid on the saucepan. When you hear the initial kernels pop add 1/4 to 1/2 cup of the popcorn kernels, depending on the size of your pan. Shake briefly to coat the kernels with oil. The recipe on the package says to shake throughout cooking but that is not necessary. Cover again and pop. When the popping slows and seems to be coming to a stop, remove from heat and dump into a large bowl immediately so that the popcorn on the bottom of the pan does not burn. Season with sea salt. The flavor is very similar to the movie theater due to the buttery taste of coconut oil.

review_headline: A good balance of nose, palate, and heat
review_body:
A good balance of nose, palate, and heat. 3 to 3.5 tablespoons per one head of nappa cabbage makes for a warm, medium heat baechu kimchi. I have a feeling my 16oz pack will disappear quickly at the present rate of consumption.

A note for those new to Korean cuisine: the recipe provided on the back label, although called a form of kimchi, is for an instant spicy salad. I have no doubt that it's tasty, and perhaps a good fit for the \\"instant gratification\\" modern American psyche, but it is not the heavenly fermented goodness known as baechu kimchi. The latter takes a bit of patience, but is so very worth it.

In furtherance of your Quest for the Holy (baechu kimchi) Grail, I would also recommend [[ASIN:B00B617XK2 Red Boat Fish Sauce, 500 ml (17 oz.)]] from Vietnam. It's a cut above a random fish sauce from an Asian market, and is in my humble opinion worth the premium price.

product_title: Keebler Simply Made Cookies, 10 Ounce
review_headline: Light, crispy shortbread cookies with a good butter flavor
review_body:
I love classic butter shortbread cookies. They are my favorite type of cookie.

These are affordable and of decent quality. The shortbread is leavened with baking powder and eggs so instead of a dense cookie, it's light and crisp. A good balance of ingredients keeps them from being too sweet. They have enough salt and vanilla to really bring out the buttery flavor. The vanilla flavor is barely noticeable, these are a lot more butter than vanilla.

They aren't as good as my favorite Scottish shortbread cookies, but they are easier to find and more affordable. A good cookie to dip in coffee or cocoa.

I will be getting these again. Not for entertaining- for that I'd still prefer Dean's of Scotland, Walker's or if I have the time, homemade. But for a good, consistent, store bought cookie as an occasional treat? These will do nicely and I won't mind sharing them with my family.

review_body:
I grew up drinking this coffee. I'm not one of those coffee snobs who order "grande mocha latte with double espresso..." at starbucks. I really don't know what all that means. I want a cup of strong coffee that's not bitter, and I din't want to pay through the nose for it. Luzianne coffee with chicory makes that cup, and very inexpensively. But it appears I'm a rare individual, because this stuff is hard to find. I grew up in Mobile, Alabama, where we could find it in most supermarkets. Now we live in louisianna, where for some reason it is virtually imposible to find. We were reduced to stocking up whenever we went hom to Mobile to visit. Now the store in Mobile close to my mother has changed owners and they don't aappear to be stocking it.
I am finding Amazon to be the go to place for just about everything, but hadn't really thought about it for food items, so on a lark decided to look. Not only did they have it, but I was able to set up a subscription for recurring delivery! Amazon comes through again!
Oh, yeah, this stuff is strong. I use seven coffee scoops, which I think are equivalent to tablespoons, for a ten cup automatic drip machine. Experiment to taste. But the chicory really does cut the bitterness.

All that to say I feel that, over at least 20 years and many kinds of cups of Darjeeling, my palate knows what a good Darjeeling tea will taste like.

This tea looks fine, and has somewhat of a Darjeeling smell, but when I drank it I was very disappointed. It was as if someone sucked all the flavor out of the leaf!

product_title: Kicking Horse Coffee, Whole Bean Coffee, 2.2 Pound Pouch
review_headline: Regarding Kicking Horse coffee  I have to say...
review_body:
I have been searching for the ultimate cup of coffee for many years. In my opinion, for what it is worth-judging coffee is like judging the quality of steak. If you have a marginal steak you will need to smother it in steak sauce to eat it but if you have a really good cut of meat, you can eat it with no steak sauce. This allows you to taste the true flavor of the meat.

Coffee is no different. I used to enjoy making my coffee very strong then creamer it down to be drinkable. I gave this Kicking horse dark roast a try and was pleasantly surprised. It is strong but smooth and has enough bite it is fairly easy to balance the ratio of coffee with water to get just the right taste with no need for creamer. I drink it straight with nothing added. Does this make me a bad person? You can really taste the flavor of this coffee by not adding creamer or just a tiny bit. I recently traveled to Canada so when I saw this coffee is produced in Canada I thought why not give it a try? I am glad I did. Thank You Kicking Horse...I am a fan ~:- )

product_title: Luwak Star Gourmet Coffee, 100% Arabica Sumatra Gayo Luwak Coffee from Indonesia (or Kopi Luwak) Whole Beans, Medium Roast, Roasted in the U.S
review_headline: If you want to pay for animal cruelty, this is just the thing!
review_body: These coffee beans have been eaten and excreted (defecated) by Asian palm civets. These small, harmless animals are snatched from the wild and locked into small barren cages where they are kept for years. (Think of a prisoner in solitary confinement for several years.) They are isolated from their normal contact with other civets and lose their minds from stress, so they constantly walk in circles. They lose the fur from their backs due to malnutrition as they eat the coffee beans that are later retrieved from their feces. I have found a far better alternative that costs a fraction of this price. Coffee Primero in Gainesville, FL uses a process developed at the University of Florida that does not involve animals, but produces coffee with the same flavor characteristics. It's rather nice to know that the beans for my coffee is not only much less expensive than this, but was not part of a pile of poop.

Add 3/4 cup of organic plain Almond Milk (Pacific brand)
Add 3/4 cup of organic unsweetened apple sauce
2 eggs (you can remove the yolks if you want fat free)

I promise you these are delicious. Are they the same as regular brownies? Of course not!

product_title: SweetLeaf Stevia Powder, 4-Ounce Shaker Jars
review_body: I have tried other brands like Trader Joes and a few others and they all had a horrible bitter aftertaste.  This brand, though, does not.  However, when you first begin to use Stevia, it does take a few weeks to adjust to it.  You also have to start with very little and move upwards as you adjust to the taste.  There is an "alternative sugar" aftertaste, but it is minimal and not bitter in this brand.  After a few weeks of consistent use, I never taste it now and actually enjoy the flavor even when I end up with a tiny clump of it undissolved on my tongue.  A few times we have received a bottle that did not dissolve as easily as the others in cold liquids.  I am not sure what causes one bottle to work this way as opposed to others, but that has only occurred a few times with dozens of bottles of usage. They do make a liquid drop variety that is very good (has flavors like chocolate, etc), and it obviously has no problems at all with dissolving. However, I like the powder since I can put a container of it in my larger-sized purse for when we go out to eat.  Unfortunately, the liquid has to be kept refrigerated.  I wouldn't hesitate to try this variety of Stevia if you are trying it for the first time.  My suggestion would be to give yourself the time to "like" it and eventually you won't miss sugar (and all it's detrimental health effects!) at all.

You can tell it's honey and not sugar, but it has none of the lovely subtle flavours I was expecting from a a jar that says 'We have searched the world and traveled thousands of miles to find the perfect isolated, untouched areas where nature is abundant with wildflowers that flourish in the undisturbed frontier wilderness.' etc ect.

I used to get big 5kg tubs of raw honey from a local beekeeper, it was oh so much more flavorful than this stuff, their clover honey was like nibbling on clover blossoms and their wildflower was as unpredictable as wildflowers are, but always something fresh and fruity and floral and wonderful, but I've since moved away... I thought this would be a good replacement, but alas, I will have to go searching and see if I can find a farmer's market nearby.

If you're coming from the perspective of using the honey flavoured corn syrup often sold as honey in supermarkets, you'll find this delightful. Just know that there is much, much better out there.

review_body: I am trying this with a melitta cup which is a ceramic cup with a hole in it that you can put a paper filter into and then the coffee and hot water.  I am using 2 tablespoons as I like it strong typically for a 12 oz mug.  I am experimenting with it as suggested by various people who wrote reviews.  I find it absolutely delicious.  I don't tolerate the sugar and from what I've read about Turkish coffee it can be done in a variety of ways as per the taste buds of the individual. Some people like the sugar and some find the strong black coffee taste just fine.  It has an amazing taste.  I checked the mouth ph after drinking the coffee and it registers a dark green (alkaline).  I don't find a heavy caffeine response to it so drinking it later in the evening without it impacting sleep is a nice treat.  I do my Italian coffee in the morning and then the Turkish coffee in the afternoon or early evening typically. Both types help my asthma and open my lungs for me which is why I started using black coffee.  Putting sugar or any other coffee creamer neutralizes the theophylline/caffeine impacts for opening the lungs.  I also found in doing some reading that some people find using the melitta cup and the paper filter method neutralizes the issues of the cholesterol question as it relates to Turkish coffee.  I don't have cholesterol issues but it was the only negative issue that I found related to Turkish coffee.  I don't know if that is an issue with this kind of Turkish coffee.  I was really curious about it especially after doing a mouth ph strip test after drinking a cup of it.  It has such an amazing impact and doesn't raise the heart rate or cause sleep disturbances that I truly wondered what was in it and how it was made or processed or if some special type of coffee bean was used or developed for it.  Everything I found out, just said it was regular coffee beans.  It has the magic touch though I'd say.  Very delicious.  Highly recommended.

product_title: Runa Amazon Guayusa, 1 Pound
review_headline: Great on it's own and blends fantastically as well.
review_body:
I typically recommend this to everyone and especially those who are new to tea because it's so great and so hard to mess up. Some teas require a chemists perfection but with this anyone can throw it in any hot water and it will turn out great. Really the perfect alternative to coffee and has all the things you want from a green tea.

Although, I typically don't have it by itself. It's great on it's own, but I find this stuff to be perfect for blending teas together. My favorite to blend it with is a spicy chai tea, which is also another one of my favorites. Chai also contains caffeine so it's typically the perfect morning beverage or even late night energy boost. If you're looking to add a little green flavor or some caffeine into a beverage without it overpowering it - this is perfect.

There are just so many great things about green teas and I would recommend any one to try any of them, but I have to say this is always my first recommendation. It's easy to brew, easy to blend and I'd say you'd have a difficult time finding something else that's organic, pesticide-free, non-gmo and of such a high quality leaf. review_headline: Amazing Taste, But Not Cost Effective
review_body:
Hamburger Helper, Bacon Cheeseburger

Item: Bacon Cheeseburger
Brand: Hamburger Helper
Purchase Offline, In Store

The quality of the product itself was very good. The cost per amount really wasn't.

The cooking process of the meal is easy and efficient. It comes with quick steps and it a fast meal that tastes good. Hamburger Helper is very well known for that. As a tip, if you keep the grease from the meat and add it to the mix during the noodle stage it tastes even better, IMPO, because the package doesn't have as much spice and kick as it could.

The finish texture, if cooked for the correct time, it very good. The noodles do get a bit soft and larger than planned, if you stop too early they get hard and stiff and don't cook all the way, but that is a price you pay for swift meal and quick boil noodles.

The taste is always amazing. It is a favorite flavor at my house, my man goes wild over it.

The only real problem I have with product, which is what kicks it down to a 4 out of 5, is that there isn't enough product in it. On TV they always show a family of 3 to 5 enjoying it as a meal and having good portions but honestly it doesn't make enough for two to eat fully. At almost two dollars a box it really isn't an affordable meal. I only get them when they are on sale in multipacks, or are discounted at the Grocery Outlet because they are a few days past their sale date; since they are a dry food they are still good for a while after their sale date. (I don't feel this way about all food though; I honor the Milk sale buy dates like they are federal laws.)

I would suggest it to a friend, but not to a friend who has a large family, or even a family of more than two. I also wouldn't suggest it to a male friend because my male friends, mostly all in their 20's, could eat two boxes in one sitting and that isn't cost effective.

product_title: Organic Red Heirloom Quinoa, 12 oz”.
review_body:
Alter Eco is quinoa with one huge difference from all other quinoa brands... They are lots of organic, pre-washed quinoa in the market but none is Fair Trade. Alter Eco is the real deal. An important part of my healthy diet, Alter Eco is a blessing since it's in organic form and a Fair Trade product where other quinoas never come in Fair Trade form regardless of the color of quinoa. Fair Trade is more expensive than none Fair Trade product. Prices of red quinoa has been going up to $10 a pound, which is the most expensive quinoa, than black, rainbow and yellow. Bravo, bravo, bravo.

KEEN-Waah... A complete protein source, a seed related to other healthy cousins like spinach and beets. In a pot I place quinoa, frozen peas, carrots, corn, add water and tomato paste. Spinach is added at the end the last minute. Stewing tomatoes for a half hour increases the cancer fighting lycopene content by 35 percent. Cooking also unlocks another nutrient, beta-carotene, in corn and carrots since heat breaks down the fibrous cell walls, releasing more of these antioxidants. The same goes for spinach but then you need to get your vitamin C from something else since that is the first vitamin which is depleted with heat. I saute lots of onion separately then in ten minutes I add paprika, cumin, dillweed, gram marsala, crushed red pepper, turmeric and lots of garlic [[ASIN:B00E382P44 2 x 2 Pound Fresh Garlic USA California Heirloom Monviso Gilroy Finest (4 Pounds Total)]], mix it well and add the mix to the pot and let it sit without heat for five minutes. This is what vegans consume instead of beef since it is a complete protein. Greens, vegetables, nuts, seeds, etc. may have protein but the fact is that only quinoa has a complete protein and all others do not since all others are missing few amino acids here and there but not quinoa. I rarely ever consume beef, chicken, etc. so fish and quinoa are the only source of complete protein with all amino acids for me. Organic, whole grain, very fulfilling due to some starch with host of vitamins, minerals that no beef or chicken can even come close to. Cooks in ten minutes with some water, no fat, no salt, no sugar... I consume it with eggplant, onions, okra, smoked hearings, curry type dishes with lots of spices and delicious juices. product_title: MW Polar Herring Sauce
review_body:
Polar is the distributor, the producer Rügen Fisch AG engages in processing, packaging, and supplying fish in Germany and internationally. The company offers canned fish including herring, mackerel, sardines, salmon, and many more. The company was founded in 1949 and is based in Sassnitz, Germany. Rugen is such a giant in herring business that they sell all their herrings through different wholesalers which all you need to do is look at the packaging with only different seller. Rügen Fisch deserves recognition for these cans since they are one of the only producers with MSC Certification, others are not so Rügen Fisch costs more than others.

PRICE= 2.0, Polar sells these herrings in few different sauces and priced for Kipper .48, hot tomato .32, tomato .27, mustard .26, paprika .17 an oz on Amazon
SIZE= 6.0oz, majority of fish sold in cans vary in size between 3.5, 6.7, 7.2, 14, 17 ounce
TASTE= Not smoked and fillets are big but the mix taste is not the best
MEAT= 170g
MIX= Can separate fillets from the mix

Fish is my main diet. I try and consume only small fish from reputable sources. No fish from China or Asia, only from Canada, US, Germany and cold Baltic Seas except sardines from Morocco. I am not worried about the added ingredients of tomato sauce, oil, water, etc. since I never consume that part of the can where sodium lingers around plus all additives, I only consume the fish and dump the rest of the mix. I always prefer smoked since the producer has to sell the fish in one piece instead of pieces of fish floating around in juice regardless of the juice type. Fillets are usually sold in some type of tomato juice, water, oil, etc. I never get the chance to taste the real fish which I am after so experience has proven to me to trust smoked more than filet. Filet is always soft and hardly tastes like fish and for that reason always sells less than smoked as well.

My goal is to get the most PROTEIN, CALCIUM and VITAMIN D and B-12 without sacrificing TASTE. No farm raised fish for me, only wild fish. I do not trust what is printed on the Nutrition Facts of the labeling in majority of times since after consuming thousands cans from hundreds of different producers, I have noticed a considerable manipulation of numbers in the NUTRITION FACTS when comparing all those cans time after time. It is obvious to me that there is much misrepresentation especially when it comes to protein on these cans. Canned fish are sold everywhere so prices vary much and Amazon does not have the best prices at all on all since there are many great stores that offer canned fish for unbelievable prices so shoppers need to do their search accordingly. Majority of the canned fish in a flat form shipped by Amazon were shipped to me somehow damaged, bent, cracked open regardless since those cans were not protected properly during shipping due to its weight so remember to have your camera ready.

Smoked sprats from Baltic Seas are the smallest of all only one inch long and I get some 18 sprats in a 4oz cans. Here is the scoop for salmon, herrings and sardines. Sardines, sprat and Alaska salmons offer more calcium since those are complete fish with bones and skin unlike herrings. Herring fillets in mix offer less taste and more additive unlike the smoked herrings which are whole fish with great taste so the extra charge is for the sauce not the fish where I dump anyway so fillets have never made any sense to me. Salmon and sardines offer more protein per calorie but sardines have the most saturated fat per calorie not per serving size. For higher Omega 3 to 6 ratio and vitamin B, I consume Herrings but for high vitamin D and calcium I consume sardines, sprats and Alaskan salmon with bones, skin and all. Check out the comment section of my review for links to other fish with great taste. It is so stupid to purchase farm raised fish which pollute the environment with added carpet dyefor coloring before selling it to consumers without any knowledge about farm raised fish practices.

product_title: Luwak Star Gourmet Coffee, 100% Arabica Sumatra Gayo Luwak Coffee from Indonesia (or Kopi Luwak) Whole Beans, Medium Roast, Roasted in the U.S
review_body:
Kopi luwak is made from the beans of coffee berries that have been eaten and excreted--by the Asian palm civet. To make this coffee, the civets are typically snatched from their homes and life in the wild to be imprisoned alone in tiny, barren cages. They're deprived of everything that is natural and important to them, including freedom, exercise, space--even real food. They bite at the cage bars, turn in circles, and go insane from being imprisoned with no escape. Deprived of adequate nutrition, they begin to lose their fur. All of this cruelty is just for a novelty coffee sold by companies such as Amazon.com. We're asking the company, as a leader in global online retail sales, to learn the ugly truth behind this coffee from this recent investigation and end the sale of kopi luwak.
A PETA Asia investigator visited civet coffee farms in Indonesia and the Philippines, two of the world's top producers of kopi luwak. Undercover footage from these farms--some of which falsely advertise their coffee as \\"wild-sourced\\"--shows sick, depressed civets suffering from infections and exhibiting signs of zoochosis, a stress-induced neurotic condition that causes captive animals to spin, pace, and bob their heads in constant frantic displays of frustration

(1) It is created in a lab by chemical extraction from corn stalks. As such, it is absolutely not a \\"natural\\" food product. It has been difficult for investigators to discover exactly what chemicals are used in creating HFCS because manufacturers call the process \\"proprietary\\" in order to hide that information from consumers. If it were a healthy process, you can be assured they'd be proclaiming how it is done as a selling point. In addition, in some cases, particularly in foods imported from outside the US, there have been documented instances of mercury contamination in HFCS.
(2) While HFCS and sucrose (white sugar) both contain fructose, their chemical structure is different. Sucrose is composed of a molecule of glucose and one of fructose which are in 50:50 proportion and are tightly bound together. Enzymes in the digestive tract must break apart these two bound molecules before they can be absorbed into the body. In contrast, HFCS contains glucose and fructose in an uneven ratio of 45:55, and the fructose is not bound to the glucose, meaning that HFCS does not have to be digested. This triggers an immune reaction that results in systemic inflammation across the entire body. It has been known for decades now that [[ASIN:0071438718 inflammation]] is either the direct cause or a contributing factor in virtually every known disease.

product_title: Pacific Natural Foods Organic Minestrone With Chicken Meatballs Soup, 17.6-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 12)
review_body:
I bought this particular soup for work lunches during the fall and winter.
What I like:
The packaging. I'm not a fan of the tinny smell of foods that are normally canned.
Flavor. Can't echo the sentiment of previous reviewer of authentic Italian granny, but it tastes better than your average prepared soup.
Quality. The beans are whole, the veggies identifiable and the appropriate color (green beans are green and not grayish-brownish, carrots are orange, etc.) and nothing is mushy-yucky.
Convenience. I like that I can subscribe and have cases delivered 2x a year - in my area, it's hit or miss on what flavors of Pacific soup my local stores stock, and most of the time it's the more basic varieties.

The things other buyers might consider before purchase:
The sodium content is high. If you're not on a low-sodium diet, it's not any different than other prepared foods.
They use garlic powder, not fresh garlic. If you're like me, garlic powder tends to linger on the palate.

My kid refused to try them...don't really blame her after the first attempt went so bad...so I wiped all sense of \\"eww\\" off of my face and walked in to the room to ask my significant other to try it. They took one look and said \\"that doesn't look good, why is is brown? Are you sure it's just bananas?\\" I asked them to try it anyways...they did and immediately joined my daughter in the bathroom :/

All three of us still feel a little nauseous...I'm working on getting a Vegan friend to try these..maybe it's just us?

product_title: Community Coffee Private Reserve Whole Bean Coffee, Sumatra, (Pack of 3)
review_headline: good whole bean coffee -- now HOW MUCH DOES IT COST?
review_body:
I think this is Community Sumatra is a pretty good coffee, and definitely one that could make it onto someone's permanent everyday menu. Let me tell you what I like about it:

* First, of course, is that it's whole bean, which preserves the freshness until it's time to grind and brew. Nothing compares with the smell and taste once you're accustomed to it.

* This Sumatra has a nice medium roast flavor. There is *tiny* bit of acid film, more common in dark roasts, and a slight nutty flavor, more common in light roasts, so I've concluded that it truly does fall right in the middle. Obviously each individual drinker will need to determine if it's to their taste, but I personally like the strong, even, earthy taste.

* Partly for the reasons described above, it makes great iced coffee. During the hot Texas summers, I brew a pot like usual, put it in the refrigerator, and next morning put the coffee in a big drinking container along with milk and sugar. The only difference between hot and iced coffee when does this way is that really acidic coffees, like dark roasts, tend to taste terrible when they're cold, but this Sumatra is quite good.

Unfortunately Community Coffee has left me in the awkward position of not knowing how much this product costs. If this 3-pack was selling for $15, that would be a pretty great deal, and I would give it five stars. On the other hand, if it comes out selling for $35, I would point you to a different coffee that offers more bang for the buck. product_title: Yogi Rejuvenation Green Tea, 16 Tea Bags (Pack of 6)
review_headline: Great tea, excellent value for what you're getting
review_body:
So first, I'm not really a tea fan, but the Yogi Green Tea Rejuvenation has a pretty decent flavor in my opinion, and my wife who actually likes tea really liked this flavor. In comparison, we had originally ordered [[ASIN:B002YJCAKI Lipton Green Tea Bags, Superfruit Purple Acai with Blueberry, 20-Count, Boxes (Pack of 6)]] since it had a 20% coupon, and even at the reduced price there's no way I would recommend it. I was shocked at how little tea was actually in each packet for starters, two bags couldn't even flavor an 8ounce cup!

So, I looked around, and liked Yogi's response to a critic's claims, they have organic tea leaves and that's a big deal to me; I like to purchse organic produce when possible, but didn't even make the connection that they might be spraying down their originating plants (Camellia sinensis). After receiving my order, I really think we made the right choice.

The tea bags where stuffed pretty full, having almost 3x as many tea leaves in each bag as the Lipton bags, so that alone makes the slightly higher price justified. Each bag is plenty for a small cup. The flavor is pretty good, like I said I'm not a tea person, it's almost like it needs a squirt of orange or something, but still a little dab of honey I'm certainly OK with it. The tea is fairly mild and smooth, but not in a watery/unflavored sort of way like the Lipton tea.

So, I strongly recommend this brand, I look forward to trying out other flavors but as for now this will certainly be my mid-afternoon tea; the caffeine amount is perfect so I can go work out, but not so much that it keeps me up at night.

product_title: Orville Redenbacher's Ready to Eat Popcorn
review_headline: Orville's.White and Sharp Cheddar Mix Pop Crunch
review_body:
Normally I like Orville Redenbacher's products -- they are usually high quality and tasty, but this Cheddar Pop Crunch is unspeakably bad.

I was given a free full-sized bag at my local grocery store, and even though I paid nothing, the price was still too steep. What an unpleasant experience. The popcorn does not have the flavor of a mix of white and sharp cheddar cheese, as advertised, rather it tastes like what I would imagine dust would taste like if I were to sample some. After eating, it left a strange after-taste and somehow seemed to absorb every bit of moisture in my mouth. I was left in what I would consider to be an arid mummy-like state -- well at least in my mouth.

This popcorn product has an unusually long shelf-life, obtained by coating the kernels in what I believe to be the embodiment of Clark Griswald's (Christmas Vacation movie) fictional non-nutritive food varnish that, in the movie, was used to keep cereal crisp in milk.

Snack food usually is not particularly healthy and is generally full of chemicals and other bad things, but it at least tastes good. This product pushes the boundaries of my definition of food and actually seems more closely aligned to something plastic. Seriously bad. Unbelievably bad.

review_headline: Good food for the baby, best price with auto-ship from Amazon

We spend more on this formula than on the cheaper formula, 'tis true... and we believe it's worth it for the munchkins (or anklebiters, or rugrats, whatever you prefer to call them).

review_body:

product_title: Side Mates Pearl Couscous, Roasted Garlic & Parsley, 6 Ounce (Pack of 8)
review_body:
We regularly eat couscous but I usually make homemade. I figured I'd give this a try and the whole family didn't like it. We felt it was really salty. At 510 mg per serving, which is just about 1/4 teaspoon per serving, that's too much for our tastebuds. We use salt every day on nearly every food and use salt at the table but this is over the top.

It had a different taste of the spices and garlic that is not at all like when I made couscous from scratch using fresh garlic and dried parsley (two ingredients in this). The ingredient list is: pearl couscous (wheat), rosemary extract, onion, alt, corn starch, sugar, corn syrup powder, garlic, yeast extracts, vegetable oils, spices, celery, parsley. At home I do not use sugar of any kind in my couscous. This has 1 gram of sugar per serving.

As a healthier alternative consider making homemade couscous. Put some olive oil in the pan, sautee in a bit of celery, onion and garlic, then add the couscous and either chicken or vegetable stock at a 1:2 ratio of couscous to 2 parts liquid. Add a pinch of dried or fresh parsley and let cook as per general instructions you can find free on the internet.

I rate this product 2 stars = I Don't Like It.

review_headline: Very refreshing 'n ultra-sweet fruit flavored tea for the on-the-go person ...
review_body:
I've tried a few of Lipton's Tea & Honey to Go drinks and really enjoy the taste. They are totally refreshing and, admittedly, much better than the soda I like to drink. Try guzzle. The \\"to go\\" packages are all over the place now and if you've been in a convenience store recently, you'll find them right near the water. Most of these I'll shy away from because of the high acid content. I do like them, but it's simply trading one problem for another.

I can taste the honey in these drinks, but not the tea. Honey granules are a very popular sweetener, but so is Splenda. In essence the reason these drinks are so sweet is because of the sucralose which is marketed under several names. If you have problems with this, you can simply take a pass. All of the information is not hidden, but here on the pictures for everyone to take a look at.

Personally, I do love the taste of these \\"teas,\\" which taste more like fruit drinks than they do tea. The real tea drinker in my house actually liked the taste, but does prefer his real tea with his cookies. If you like the \\"to go\\" factor and like your teas ultra-sweet, you may just like these teas. One additional plus is that these are now Amazon Add-on Items, something that makes ordering them really easy.

product_title: Powdered Purple Yam Ube
review_headline: Huge Disappointment--Can't Stand it At All
review_body:
I must preface this by saying I've never cooked with powdered ube before, so maybe there's some secret I am unaware of. I chose this product because I LOVE LOVE LOVE baked purple sweet potatoes. They are so sweet, almost cake-like, and delicious. I thought this powder would be a condensed form of that wonderful sweet flavor, which I could mix into things like oatmeal, frozen yogurt, or soy milk for ube-flavored delight. To my extreme disappointment, it tastes AWFUL. It does not taste sweet whatsoever; rather, it tastes like how I'd imagine an ashtray to taste. I thought maybe you can't simply mix the powder into oatmeal, as I did the first time; maybe I should rehydrate it before eating. So I tried rehydrating it with water, simmering on the stove, and achieved a nice purple paste. Perhaps the heat of cooking would draw out the natural flavors I expect of a purple sweet potato? Nope. It tasted the same as it did when mixed into the oatmeal--burnt, ashy, gross.

There is a recipe on the back of the packet to make a sweet ube filling, but it is loaded with sugar, butter, etc. I love simply baked purple sweet potatoes because they taste like dessert and are healthy--no need to add sugar and butter. So why buy the powder if it doesn't taste like the original healthy form without unhealthy crap? The packet also recommends adding it to cakes and ice cream; perhaps the sugar of those desserts would finally get the ube powder to taste as I'd expect, but the ashtray flavor is so strong to me that I'd be shocked if it magically tasted like normal sweet potatoes.

I don't know what to do with the rest of my powder. I can't stand it. I will always buy fresh purple sweet potatoes from now on. :-(

product_title: Baron Blazing Hot Pepper Sauce
review_headline: Not exactly blazing hot, but packed with flavor
review_body:
'Hot' is a subjective term, and blazing hot even more so. This sauce does pack some heat, but the main reason I love it (and awarded five stars) is the flavor. The ingredients are somewhat simple and straightforward: peppers, water, vinegar, salt and some spices.)

What sets this apart from other Scotch-Bonnet sauces is the peppers themselves impart a touch of sweetness. Also, instead of giving this sauce a sour quality the vinegar actually makes it tangy. It has the obligatory saltiness to round out the basic flavor profile for a hot sauce, but at a scant 39mg of sodium per serving this is practically guilt free for me. I have sodium restrictions and have to watch my intake.

The heat has almost no bite and is the typical slow build, spread and burn type that is characteristic of Scotch bonnet peppers. It's certainly much hotter than Tabasco sauce, but not as hot as, say, [[ASIN:B0000GHNTK El Yucateco Green Chile Habanero Sauce]]. Not very precise, but that is the best I can describe the piquant qualities of this sauce.

If you love maximum flavor with respectable heat you will probably enjoy this sauce. I'll confess that I do not purchase it often, but when I do a bottle does not last me long. So many hot sauces and so little time.

review_headline: Excellent, but the Cost is  Too High.
review_body:
San Diego tap water smells a bit and leaves a lot of white crud in the glass if evaporated dry. It's mostly from the Colorado River. But, what the hey? Why should I buy supplemental minerals if Colorado River water already contains a good variety? In any case, the city says it's safe and I'm unaware of any major problems. Well, there's the taste. My wife feels differently about such matters. She's from Europe and nobody there supposedly drinks tap water. It's considered disgusting. Proper drinking water must come in a bottle and be collected from some important and well-known springs. Besides, she seems to have elevated perceptions in taste, smell, sight, hearing and all other senses. In any case, to keep peace in the household, I agreed that we would drink bottled water. We gradually settled in on Kirkland Signature bottled water. The price was right! Well, now even that isn't good enough. My wife seems to have discovered Fiji Natural Artesian Water which comes in attractive rectangular bottles and is imported all the way from the South Pacific. It costs several times as much as regular brands, but that's part of the appeal. It's the best, she claims. It's so smooth and goes down so easy, she says. Now other bottled waters, although OK, are not nearly as good. No, Fiji Natural Artesian Water is the water for her. I must admit that it's excellent, but the cost is way too high.

Gary Peterson

product_title: La Victoria Diced Jalapeno Peppers, Hot, 4-Ounce Units (Pack of 24)
review_body:
Note: I purchase these locally so my review will address the peppers and sidestep variable factors such as price and shipping costs.

What I love about these jalapenos is they have a flavor that is actually as good or better than when I fire-roast peppers I buy fresh. I always keep a dozen or so cans in my pantry for times when I do not have fresh jalapenos on hand and want a quick omelet or to spice up some beans or make a fresh salsa.

They are hot. Not terribly so, but they have a nice bite and will balance out the piquant part of a flavor profile for most dishes.

An advantage of these over fresh is the piquant quality is consistent. What I mean is I can sound on the peppers in one can being identical in heat to any other can. With fresh peppers it's hit or miss - sometimes they are milder than I want and others much hotter than I expected.

There is a disadvantage to these as well. They are very high in sodium at 150mg per serving (there are about four servings per can). For most uses I simply drain them and quickly rinse to remove most of the sodium without affecting the basic flavor.

These are convenient, relatively inexpensive when compared to other brands, and have a flavor that no other canned peppers I purchase come close to having. Plus, as I mentioned above, they are as good as my home made fire-roasted jalapenos (minus the sodium.)
