product_title: Cornucopia Fruit Wine Making Kit, 16.4 Pound Box
review_body:
I have had really good luck with these kits. I've made a couple of the other Cornucopia kits and they have been perfect.

I had a little trouble with this kit, and in case anyone else has a similar problem, I will list how I overcame the issue.

When I pitched the yeast into the must in the primary, after 48 hours I still did not see any signs of fermentation (by this time, you should at the very least see a layer of yeast "scum" on top of the must and should really see vigorous bubbling on the surface). So I pitched a second packet of yeast that I had on hand of a similar strain (Lalvin 1118; these kits come with Lalvin 1114). This still did not work. So I used a method that I had found for starting skeeter pee:

First, I poured a new packet of yeast into a mason jar containing warm water (~70 degrees) and sugar (1 cup of each). I let this sit for 2 hours with the lid loosely placed on top and by then there was a large amount of foaming on the surface of the starter. I then added 8 oz of the juice from the primary fermentation bucket and let this sit for 4 hours. At this time, there was vigorous fermentation and lots of bubbling on the surface. I added 8 oz more of the juice from the primary bucket and waited for 4 hours again. At this point, I dumped half of the starter out into the bucket, stirred up the bucket, and filled the starter mason jar with juice from the bucket. I left this sitting overnight with the lid sitting loosely on the top. The next morning, I dumped the whole starter into the bucket. By that evening, there was vigorous fermentation in my bucket.

I can't comment on the flavor of the wine yet but the juice tastes really good. I think it will turn out to be a really nice sweet red wine. I will try to remember to post an update when I've tasted the wine.

My favorite thing about these Cornucopia fruit wines is that they are ready to drink in < 2 months. Can't beat that!

product_title: Sweet Heat Caribbean Pepper Sauce by Tortuga (5 ounce)
review_body:
I love Caribbean sauces, and particularly love the diversity among them - especially between the northern Caribbean and the southern islands. This one has all of the hallmarks of a great southern sauce: more fruity and sweet, but with a respectable amount of heat.

While not among the hottest sauces from the region the flavor profile is almost evenly split between sweet and pungent. There is a bit of tang, and very little saltiness. In many respects it is one of the most unique Caribbean sauces I have tried. Part of the reason for that is the choice of fruit - the star fruit - which is enigmatic in itself. It has a subtle hint of citrus, but also is similar to fleshy fruits like apples, although not quite that either.

The tang mainly comes from the citric acid and mustard, while the turmeric both colors the sauce and gives it a slightly bitter aftertaste. What I love is the Scotch bonnets which add both flavor and heat. The heat is the slow burn type typical of those peppers, without the bite of habaneros that are often used in the southern Caribbean sauces.

Since I am on a sodium-restricted diet I especially love the low sodium levels, which come in at 60mg per serving. That is less than many other Caribbean sauces and significantly less than Mexican and Mesoamerican ones.

The sauce is thick and can be spread almost like mayonnaise. I've used it on just about every conceivable dish, including fish, eggs and even as a condiment for soups and stews. Do note that you have to refrigerate this sauce after opening it.

product_title: Cafe Najjar Classic Turkish-style ground coffee 450g (1 lbs) (Lebanon)
review_headline: Top quality for Turkish, Arabic and Greek coffees
review_body:
I found this locally. Actually I found the companion product, [[ASIN:B002ABW7GW Cafe Najjar Classic with Cardamom Turkish-style ground coffee]], first and was so impressed that I immediately went back and purchased this one.

This is the real thing, from the fresh, aromatic coffee to the extra fine, powdery grind. It is ground especially for brewing in an ibrik (also called a cezve). I prefer to hand grind my cardamom with a mortar and pestle and do my own blending. To that end this is the perfect coffee for that. I will admit that the brand's pre-blended coffee is almost as good, but there is nothing like fresh ground cardamom in my opinion so I now have the best of both worlds. For the record I have found that [[ASIN:B002SWJQSK Rani Green Cardamom Pods]] are the best I have come across in the US, so if you use that spice in your coffee give that brand a try.

In order to obtain the best results from this coffee it must be brewed in an ibrik. Using one requires a very specific technique: First, use good water. Filtered or bottled. Most tap water will ruin the flavor of the brewed coffee. Second, DO NOT fill the maker more than half way. And when heating do not use any heat source or setting above medium low. As soon as it boils immediately remove it from the heat and let it settle down. Trust me, it can get quickly out of control, so pay close attention. You can do a second boil to increase the strength of the brew.

If properly brewed this coffee will win you over. It has already become my favorite brand and I am not likely to switch. I value both freshness and quality beans in my coffees, and this one has both.

review_headline: Not Gerbs - may not really be allergy free
review_body:
When I ordered these, it said they were Gerbs brand. Gerbs is known for their allergy friendly products. When it arrived, it came with a receipt from East Empire, and had no label on it. It looked like they substituted generic. We specifically wanted Gerbs due to a nut allergy in the family.

FOR THOSE WHO HAVE NUT ALLERGIES, BEWARE, THESE MAY NOT REALLY BE GERBS BRAND, AS ADVERTISED, SO THEY MAY NOT BE NUT FREE!! It appears they are substituting for a generic product from East Empire. They also do not taste as good.

It appears they might have changed the description to say they come from East Empire some of the time, but it is deceptive because it still says Gerbs (which it is not) and nut free (which it may not be - the seller had no idea when I called them). Also, it seems when I reload the page, sometimes it says it is fulfilled by Gerbs and sometimes it says East Empire, but it is East Empire.

I'd give them zero stars if I could, as they not only did a bait and switch and sent a different product than I ordered, but also, then they made me pay to return it -- which cost as much as the product itself!! And it's dangerous to advertise as nut free when the product is not.

review_headline: Bob's Red Mill is turning from a good company to an unscrupulous one
review_body: I have been buying Bob's Red Mill Organic products for years, but since last year I found that the company is implementing some strategy to make more money by producing inferior products. For example, the  flax seed meal is no longer made out of the whole grain; the company extracted most of the real meaty part of the seeds to produce oil and what's left is just the shell and bran. I couldn't believe it at first after seeing someone's comments about the product made out of shells. But My last purchase of 8x16 oz organic flax seed meal all came with straws some as long as 1 inch long. I had to sift through each bag to get rid of the straws. As I was sifting through, I further confirmed the meal is NOT from the whole grain, but only shells after the meat and oil have been extracted. It's a cheating marketing strategy. The straws pricked my gum and sometimes almost choked me. I'm extremely disappointed. I should have written this review earlier, but I couldn't believe each bag is just as bad as the other. product_title: Yogi Teas Woman's Mother To Be, 16 Count (Pack of 6)
review_body:
I have stage 3 endometriosis, and I bought this product in a fit of desperation, looking for anything that might ease my pain. I read the reviews on here promising miracles to women who've suffered lifelong menstrual pain. I have suffered severe cramps for over a decade and within the past few years have developed endometriosis, so I know all about menstrual pain. Unsurprisingly and unfortunately, this tea didn't work. I used it as advised for over a month (1-2 cups per day, 3 during my period, steeped 10 min with boiled water), but it didn't help my pain at all.

The taste is a bit odd. I thought it was pretty gross at first, but I forced myself to drink it. Eventually I got used to it and it became tolerable. The smell reminds me of vegetable stock. On the other hand, my boyfriend thinks it tastes fine, although he has no need to avail himself of the purported benefits. So obviously the taste is, well, personal taste.

After I found that this tea did not help me at all, I extensively researched the components in scholarly journals and I cannot find any evidence that they reduce menstrual pain. I find conflicting reports on the use of raspberry leaf for various uterine conditions, which some midwives actually use to INDUCE uterine contractions (unclear how successfully) -- exactly the opposite of what you want when you want to reduce cramps caused by uterine contractions. I should have researched this beforehand but I literally purchased this item while my judgment was impaired due to extreme pain.

product_title: Spitz Seasoned Sunflower Seed, 6-Ounce (Pack of 12)
review_body:
I've tried 4 brands of seeds: Frito Lay, David, Dakota, and Spitz. Frito Lay was the first brand I tried when I was a kid, and for 50¢ (or 59¢ now) they are alright for a snack. Then I moved to David seeds when I started working and could buy my own. They are good, but VERY salty. Then I saw Dakota seeds in a local grocery store a few years ago. They are also good, and big, and not as salty as David seeds but still quite salty. Then I saw Spitz brand in Wal-Mart last year and saw the lower sodium content and they also had olive oil on the ingredients list so I bought a back and immediately loved them, just the right amount of salt and the hint of olive oil to give it a mellow flavor. But, sadly, Wal-Mart doesn't carry Spitz brand anymore, so I hit Amazon hoping to find some. And I did (the original flavor) and ordered some.

Then I came across the Seasoned flavor. The ingredients list looked great, with brown sugar and other spices, so I bought a carton of these. All I can say is they are just amazing. They are very well seasoned, enough so you can taste the seasonings, but not so much that it is obnoxious (in other words, it is well balanced). I would recommend these as well as the original (salt and olive oil) flavor over any other brand.

product_title: Numi Organic Pu'erh Tea, Tea Bags
review_body:
Ginger fans- very mellow ginger
Pu'erh fans - very mellow pu'erh
General fans of black tea - a nice warm, balanced blend,

I love tea.
I am, generally, not a fan of Pu'erh and I usually choose fairly basic black teas and I love a cup of matcha in the afternoon. Pu'erh, as I have tasted before this particular blend, is rather \\"earthy\\", and by earthy I mean that it tastes, to me, like moss and cigar in garden runoff. It's just not the kind of thing I would choose to drink again... EVER. No way.

I am, though, a ginger fan. I love ginger. I buy pounds of the knobbly root and use it in many different foods, every day. Tasty stuff and I like the benefits.

So, when faced with Numi's Ginger Pu'erh, I had hopes that perhaps the warm and snappy root would overpower and mute that stale, cologne overdose of Pu'erh.

It didn't. The ginger BALANCED the Pu'erh. The Pu'erh mellows the ginger! Numi Ginger Pu'erh is actually tasty!
I would certainly buy this and drink this again. It has replaced my usual black tea and ginger blend when I crave a cup just after lunch (any later and Pu'erh monkeys with my sleep way more than my plain back Irish or English Breakfast or Earl Grey).

review_body: I bought this starter directly from Gold Mine Natural Foods about ten years ago but didn't get around to using it until this past winter.  It did great even after all that time sitting in a cabinet in my kitchen!  If you enjoy natto, you can make lots (and I mean lots) of it cheaply and reliably with this starter.  A gas oven (turned way, way down) and a digital thermometer with a remote probe make the process easy, but there are multiple methods for holding the correct temp if you don't have a gas oven.  Online instructions for making natto are all similar, but I have been using instructions by Kazuo Shiroki (search for \\"Methods for Making Natto in North America\\"). Just read the instructions carefully all the way through before you start the process.  Shiroki has good tips and valid precautions, not all of which are mentioned by other instruction writers.

product_title: Bell Plantation PB2 with Premium Chocolate
review_body:
Let me start by saying that I never write reviews. PB2 sparked a desire to do so. I am a self-admitted peanut butter addict. I can easily house an entire jar in a single sitting. This being said, I am also paleo, and peanut butter doesn't fit in with that based on the omega 3 to 6 ratio and being a legume. I also tend to *really* regret eating peanut butter the next day, as my stomach doesn't really appreciate it.

Enter PB2. I was highly skeptical. Opening the package is a little tricky, as it's vacuum-packed without a resealable container. You just have to carefully use a knife or whatever. I just put the rest into empty peanut butter jars. Easy fix.

First, I tasted the powder straight up. Highly promising. Tasted exactly like delicious, roasted peanuts. I mixed two spoons of the powder with just enough water to imitate thick peanut butter. My first taste was...a revelation. Amazing. Mind-blowing. I couldn't comprehend it. IT. TASTED. LIKE. PEANUT. BUTTER.

Holy crap, this stuff is amazing (both the regular and chocolate), and has limitless applications. I stirred it into mashed bananas with a dash of milk. I put it into my post-workout protein smoothie. Oh. God. I'm going to spend so much money on this.

One caveat is that the texture is not like true peanut butter. It doesn't have the viscous, thick, stick-to-the-roof-of-your-mouth feel. It's more like a light, peanut butter \\"mousse\\" if you will.

The real litmus test was how my stomach would handle it. No problem at all.

PB2. I love thee, and will create a shrine in my kitchen to thee.

product_title: Campbell's Go Soup Microwavable Pouch
review_headline: Good packaging. "Interesting" flavor. Very high sodium.
review_body:
Well, first of all I gave it a couple of stars because I do think the microwavable packaging is a very good idea and better than some plastic cup and lid arrangement in my humble opinion. I received this Campbell's Go Soup Coconut Curry with Chicken and Shitake Mushrooms as a free sample with another order. I just finished eating it as I write this review and I decided to review it for a few reasons. Firstly, it does indeed have what I consider an odd smell and taste probably due to some of the spices. I'm the type of person who tastes things like saffron as a plastic type of smell and taste. Although the ingredients on this soup don't include saffron, it has something of a similar effect.

Secondly I was a bit surprised at how much sodium is in each serving, 830mg, and then to realize that this single bowl of soup is actually considered 2 servings.. Well I really hate how labeling laws allow for such things. This is ONE bowl of soup people.. but 2 servings? I don't think so. So 99% of people are eating the whole bowl in one sitting and therefore receiving 1660mg of sodium in one small bowl of soup! The entire daily allowance in a 2000 calorie diet is 2400mg. This is why your hospital tells you to never eat \\"canned\\" soup after you've had a heart attack, like I have. For goodness sakes, add flavor without salt OK? Please? Anyone?

Third, I didn't recognize a single piece of shitake mushroom in my entire bowl of soup. There were nice big chunks of carrot, pepper and water chestnut, but the chicken was kind of small and again I couldn't positively identify a mushroom.

Well, as a free sample it was fine. After looking over the ingredients list I still can't identify where the \\"weird\\" smell and flavor comes from, but I suspect spices. It has too much sodium like nearly everything else in American grocery aisles and considering it 2 servings is like calling 1 candy bar 2 servings. Should be disallowed by law when it's quite clearly designedas a single serving container. I won't buy this again. I would consider another flavor if it came in a truly single serving without making me do math in the store aisle.

review_body:
From my wife Sarah: Although cinnamon Altoids are my favorite flavor, I eat these too. If I eat too many of the cinnamon Altoids, they're so strong that they irritate my tongue, mouth and stomach, but the wintergreen Altoids don't do that. So I use these in addition to the cinnamon to help me stick to my low calorie, low sugar diet. Here's why:

- They've got just a touch of sweetness that satisfies my cravings. They taste decent to me.

- They're extremely low calorie - 3 pieces is 10 calories - so that's just over 3 calories a piece.

- They've only got 2 grams of sugar and 2 carbs for 3 pieces. That's low enough for me to enjoy a few without messing up my sugar or weight loss.

- They're also great as a breath mint.

- They're gluten free also.

So I find them good to munch on without blowing my diet.

product_title: BUSH'S BEST Pinto Beans, 111 oz
review_headline: Heart healthy alternative to other brands
review_body:
Note: I purchase this locally so my review will address the product itself and not the pricing or shipping.

I discovered these when my then-favorite brand was out of stock. While these are not as flavorful they more than make up for it in nutritional values. Each one half cup serving of these pinto beans contains only 80 calories and zero for fat and cholesterol.

My comment about flavor compared to the other brand I buy is mainly based on what is left out. These contains beans, water, salt and an additive to aid in color retention. Nothing more. That alone is a good trade-off for a little additional flavor. More importantly, the beans are plump and firm. Some brands have beans that must have been over processed, so this one gets yet another point for that.

While these have a better nutrition profile that some other brands, the sodium is still a little high at 450mg per half cup serving. Also, if you are counting carbs this has 18 grams per serving. Potassium is 310mg per half cup, which is impressive considering a medium banana contains about 420mg. So this is a good way to get that into your daily diet, and equally impressive is the 6 grams or protein per serving.

I get around the sodium issue by rinsing these before I cook them. That eliminates a lot of the salt, but I compensate by using various spices depending on my mood. Look up products by eeny Tiny Spice Co. of Vermont for ideas. One of my favorites to use with these beans is [[ASIN:B0063J1L1Y Teeny Tiny Spice Co. of Vermont Organic Chocolate Chili]] followed closely by [[ASIN:B0063J1OIY Teeny Tiny Spice Co. of Vermont Organic Ethiopian Bereberé]].

Unfortunately, I am not wild about the flavor of this sauce. I much prefer Dave's Total Insanity Sauce which has a garlicky hint to it. Though it's slightly less spicy the flavor is much, much better. This original sauce I think has a weird sort of sweetness to it which seems out of place and I found unpleasant. Bottom line if you want something very spicy I would recommend this. If you want something slightly less spicy but with a better flavor, I'd recommend Dave's total Insanity Sauce.

product_title: Alessi Caponata, Egglpant, 10.50-Ounce
review_headline: Not bad for something from a jar
review_body:
Note: I purchase this locally, so this review will only address the product and not pricing or shipping costs.

All of the key flavors are there: you can taste the blend of eggplant and tomato, the tang of vinegar and the saltiness of the capers. This also has a good base of other flavors from celery, olives and seasonings. In other words, it may not be close to home made, but it is tasty and definitely convenient. It has that distinctive Sicilian flavor that makes it perfect for last minute entertaining when you need to put out antipasti or meze.

There are approximately three servings per can, with each serving coming in at about 140 calories. Not bad for something so delicious.

What I truly love, though, is the reasonable levels of sodium, which is a fraction of the fried eggplant I mentioned above, and other nutritional values. Sodium is 310mg, which is less than half of the same serving of the fried eggplant, although the carbs and fat are still a tad high at 7 grams each. If you are watching cholesterol there is zero in this product. Do be aware that the sugar content is 8 grams.

As an antipasti or meze - hot or cold - this is an excellent choice to accompany breads for dipping and scooping, and it goes well with other servings that are Mediterranean (olives, pickled peppers, cheeses, dolmas, etc.) Of course it's great to make this delicious dish yourself, but these jars are convenient for putting something together on short notice.

Package came fairly quickly (considering it went from West Coast to East Coast). Package was small and well packed. Plants were wrapped in wet moss along with a wet paper towel. Even in the 85+ degree heat and high humidity that the package was shipped in the plants came alive and the cloth/moss was still wet.

I planted them in the provided pot and moss and placed the pot in a small disposable plastic container (store brand that you can get like the Gladware, $2 for 3) and surrounded the pot with the left over moss and filled it about a 1/3 of the way with distilled water. This was on Saturday 6/1. As of Tuesday 6/4 everything appears to be going well. Nothing has died and the traps are starting to open up.

One thing to note is that these are very small plants when they arrive, even the biggest of the heads was the side of a half dime or so.

product_title: Sugar Beet Syrup 16oz
review_headline: Like it and you'll love it.
review_body:
To me the "golden syrup" is something special because I grew up with it. Even though it may look like molasses, tastewise it is not the same. It lacks the harshness and bitter of the taste of molasses. I even tried cane sugar syrup and was disappointed because it had some of that bitter, burned after-taste. I believe it is the way the syrup is made. The water needs to be evaporated to be left with the syrup. But when you heat the juice to make the syrup and the heat at the bottom of the pot becomes too hot, the sugar starts to burn to yield the burned, bitter taste. This Goldsaft has a hearty, but not bitter taste. I enjoy it as a special treat.

Why a four star and not a five star? Only because it came in a jar and not in a squeeze bottle. I was able to refill a squeeze bottle from the jar. I had to sacrifice a little of the sticky syrup and that cost one star. Now I can lay ribbons of this syrup in fancy design patterns on my toasted open face roll and enjoy it without having a sticky spoon or knife.

product_title: Mainstay Emergency Food Rations - 3600 Calorie Bars
review_headline: The perfect grab and go box for bug-out food
review_body:
This is THE perfect grab and go box of emergency rations for bugging-out. The ten pouches can be rationed out to provide 1200 calories of subsistence level food for 30 days, for a single individual. Ideally, you would supplement this with other food to give you more energy and variety. The taste is palatable, but be sure to have sufficient water on hand. Even my dogs will eat it.

When you receive the box, do not open it. Instead, make a duct tape handle for it. I like to use a small loop on the end, sticky side out, and then a large loop around the whole box and small loop, sticky side in. Label the box with the month and year it expires, in bold black marker. Stash it in a cold dark closet, near your most likely exit, so you can grab it and go.

Realistically, 1 box could serve 6 people for 5 days. Ideally, you should have 1 box per person.

Simple Peanut Butter Protein Shake

One Cup Soy Milk
One 1\\" slice of Firm Tofu
Two tablespoons of this peanut butter

Add soy milk and tofu to blender and blend until liquid.
Add peanut butter and blend again just to mix.

Protein is 21g. Calories 245.

Note: do not substitute some other type of vegetarian milk as it won't give enough protein. Also, use firm or extra firm tofu because softer tofu makes the shake too runny and also because it has less protein.

This can be made in bigger batches and stored for up two 48 hours.

product_title: V8 100% Vegetable Juice, Original Low Sodium
review_headline: Great product- but Amazon ships it POORLY.
review_body:
As many other reviewers have said, this is a good product, reasonably priced. It tastes good; it has lower sodium (and increased potassium), and it's about as 'healthy' as you can get with a commercial juice. The cans are too big for one person, but work well for one serving each for the two of us. The original packaging by Campbell (in the 24 pack) is pretty good as well- the shrink wrap holds all the cans together, and isn't too bad to remove and store.

However...

Amazon put two of these 24 packs into a much larger shipping box (which was not only oversized, but flimsy). The two heavy cases of 24 slid around inside, damaging the outer box, which was already marginal at best. Result: One completely crushed can went all over the inside of the shipping box, making an incredible mess, and melting through a corner of the shipping box and causing the tape to let go as well; 12 other cans (all on one side of the top case) were wrinkled or dented. We came home to discover that we had a big mess on our front porch- and since the large box was tossed on top of another Subscribe/Save box (crushing part of it), we had V8 ALL over everything. Gee, thanks Amazon...

To top that off, Amazon's return policy requires that I ship the damaged items back- so although I briefly considered just putting all of this mess into yet another even larger box, I decided I could live with the other 12 dented/wrinkled cans- especially after thinking about the cost and hassle of getting together the shipping materials to contain the mess.

I don't recommend buying this from Amazon unless / until they figure out how to have a pick/pack/ship process for subscribe/save items that works effectively for the customer!

What I've found is that instead of mixing the packet with an entire quart of water, I used 1 and 3/4 quarts. Still, there is no bold flavor! There is, in fact, just very little flavor at all. I bought a watermelon Kool-Aid at my grocer's, and that was so incredible! Strawberry just doesn't compare. I did save a dollar by buying this product online, but given how much I don't love it, that's not much of a consolation.

p.s. to those of you who want to cut down on your sugar, use only 1/4 cup of sugar, and then mix to taste with liquid stevia. It is just as sweet as sugar without the health concerns! I hope you will try it. Enjoy : )

product_title: Betty Crocker Brownie Mix, 20.5-Ounce Boxes
review_headline: Good Revision of a Classic Product
review_body:
A number of years ago, I created a dessert called \\"Brownie Tuesdays\\", which involve brownies topped with pudding and a homemade sauce, often vanilla or butterscotch, topped with whipped cream. I was distraught when Amazon discontinued the regular brownie mix, but decided to try these. My sons agreed to try this new formulation made with a number of different recipes (based upon earlier Betty Crocker product instructions)- a batch each day for a week. I'm sure you can all imagine what a sacrifice this was for them - eating brownies every day ;-)

The nomenclature \\"low fat\\" appears to refer to the fact that this mix uses only one egg instead of 2, and has reduced by about 85% the amount of oil used. The recipe on the box makes very sticky, fudgy brownies. Using the recipe from the previous mix (2 eggs, 1/2 cup oil, 1/4 cup water) makes a cake-like recipe. Using the recipe I remember from 30+ years ago (1 egg, 1/4 cup water, 1/4 cup oil) makes a fudgy, but less sticky, brownie.

Also, it's worth noting that I was given a stoneware pan a couple of years back, and I use it to make my brownies now. They cook much more evenly.

It's a real shame that too many Americans today won't even consider kippered herring.
They are a tasty, good for you, portable, temperature stable lunch with some bread or crackers and a piece of fruit.

product_title: Tropical Blossom Tropical Wild Honey, 48-Ounce Bottle
review_body:
I had hoped to be able to send feedback directly to the company, but this option was not available. I wanted to give the company a chance, because maybe I got a bad batch?

I understand that a honey's taste, color, and smell will vary greatly, depending on the source. I had never had \\"tropical\\" honey before, but from the seemingly massive positive testimonials I thought I was safe. I am disappointed.

The honey is dark and has a strong molasses-like flavor to it - no problem for me, really, but just reporting for others' sakes. When tasting the honey alone I notice a strong bitter after-taste - terrible! Easier to ignore when using the honey in something else, but I like to eat honey by itself at times. I don't consider myself as having a delicate or sensitive palate, so this was especially strange to me. As strange are the consistently positive reviews by everyone else so far, compounding my feelings of disappointment.

As for testimonials regarding how it tastes like it is fresh from the comb, I have to say I emphatically disagree. I do not detect much of a floral scent, which for me, is indicative of a fresh, raw honey. It may be fresh and raw, but in any case, not for me. So disappointed.

product_title: Ekobrew Coffee Reusable Filter, Small, Violet
review_headline: Works well, but beware of fine ground coffee
review_body:
I have had the Ekobrew for 2 months now and average about 2 cups per day on my Keurig. This works well, I find that you have to keep the size of the brew to 12 oz as 16oz just gets too watered down (even with the disposable k-cups). Clean up just takes a quick rinse in the sink.

HOWEVER, do not use a fine ground coffee in here (like Gevalia), because it turns to mud and does not allow the water to go thru the filter, which creates a huge mess opening the filter tops due to the water not being able to drain thru the bottom. A medium grind coffee will quickly resolve this issue and avoid you making a mess.

If you want a stronger brew, brew twice, but do not use a finer grind. Remember that most coffees require 2 rounded tablespoons per 6oz. The Ekobew probably fits just over 3 tablespoons (but I have not properly measured, so it might even take 4 tablespoons).

Overall I suggest this product.

review_body:
I am reviewing several instant coffees at the same time, and the same review will be found for all of them.

My reviews are based on two criteria: How it tastes, and how well I wake up with it.

Quick disclaimer, I am generally a health nut, with one exception, coffee. I am aware that instant coffee is not exactly in the healthy food category, but this is a choice that I make because I just don't have time to brew an actual pot of coffee.

I'm starting with my worst, and will work my way down to my favorite, also note, I drink my coffee black.

6th Place: Davidoff Cafe Rich Aroma Instant Coffee

This coffee has a great aroma, but tastes like Folgers (dirty dishwater). I was actually very disappointed as I had high expectations. I can deal with Folgers flavor, but this coffee made me feel awful; the same sick feeling that I get from Folgers instant coffee. (I swear Folgers must have some sort of contaminant in it.) I gave it a second chance, and felt just as bad. In the recycling it went. I tried to save the glass container, but the design is so ridiculous, that I couldn't even find a use for it.
Flavor Rank: #6
Stimulant Rank: #6

Stimulant Rank: #5

product_title: Lars' Own Rice (For Porridge), 12-Ounce Packages (Pack of 12)
review_body:
Love this rice pudding! The rice is the perfect texture and really has some substance to it. Perfect for rice pudding.

FIrst you make the rice porridge, and then when it's been refrigerated and is cold, you make the rice pudding. I make the porridge following their directions, except that I cut the salt in half. It was way too salty for me, and I like salt.

I tried both recipes for the rice pudding that you make from the porridge, and wasn't actually that pleased with either of them. The recipe that called for eggs had kind of an odd texture, and the recipe that called for whipped cream called for so much whipped cream that it was too much, even for a whipped cream lover.

So I experimented, and came up with the perfect recipe. I use 8 ounces of whipped cream for the entire batch of rice porridge (instead of just 2 cups of the porridge). I used 3 tablespoons of vanilla and 1/3 - 1/2 cup of sugar. It was truly the best rice pudding ever.

If you love rice pudding, you have to try this.

review_headline: Decent robust coffee, but not at boutique prices
review_body:
Seattle's Best Level 5 (or the coffee previously known as French Roast) passes all the criteria for a very good, robust cup of coffee. It has a dark flavor that does not taste quite as burnt or toasted as some French Roasts, including its Starbuck's cousin, and it mixes well with Level 4 or 3 to make a less intense but still hearty brew for early mornings when the jolt is perhaps a bit more important than the lingering flavor. But on a rainy morning when time meanders and there is no where one has to be, this is a fine brew to accompany time spent reading a novel, dabbling in poetry, or constructing a diatribe against the perceived ills of modern society.

The new packaging for this line of coffees (well, it is not that new now) however, remains off-putting and garish and the best to be said is that ii is hard to miss in the coffee-tea aisles. Still, despite all the packaging tricks, the one visual element that guides my purchases is the cost. Right now I could go to my local grocery and buy a bags of Level 5 and get enough change for a quart of half and half for the price listed here. It's good coffee but not a a deal at these boutique prices.

product_title: Manitoba Harvest Hemp Pro 50 Protein Supplement, 16 Ounce
review_headline: Great for you, not so great consistency
review_body:
Unlike milk, hemp is high in both protein and fiber and Manitoba processes it to get the right balance. This specific powder is more of a nutritional supplement than protein powder because it keeps a large amount of both, and has a much lower concentration of protein to powder than a pure protein mix. The whey mix I use has 18g of protein in 23g of mix, this hemp has 15g of protein in 30g of mix (most of the rest - 7g - is fiber and 3.5g is good unsaturated fat). If you're looking for more protein, then check out Manitoba's 70% protein, which has more protein per amount of powder (but still a decent amount of fiber). None of the hemp products will give the protein punch that you get with whey or soy, so you have to consume more of the powder to get the same amount of protein. Manitoba also makes a powder that is focused on fiber but also has a decent amount of protein. Hemp also has a good load of omega3 fatty acids.

The downside of this powder is consistency. I add it to shakes, and it's like adding flour - it makes the shake thick and gummy, not at all like adding frozen fruit. If the shake sits for a little while, it gets to be much thicker, almost like thick pancake batter. I have trouble using a full serving. I think it's best in a small shake without a lot else in it that adds thickness (not a lot of pureed fruit, for example), just enough to flavor the drink. I don't really notice the taste.

review_body:
Yeah, it's good popcorn but hold the trumpets and fanfare.

I use my hot air popper nearly every day, and this corn pops well. Some days there are a few unpopped kernels and some days not. There is seldom an exploding kernel once an unpopped one hits the bowl (you know what I mean). That's a sign of good popcorn. As it should be, the corn is generally lighter and crisper than the more dense yellow variety.

So while this is a good product, I'm not so sure it's better than any other decent brand out there. Just before ordering this 4-pack, I picked up some Lieutenant Kernel brand at Von's (West Coast supermarket) and it turned out to be at least as good as Bob's for about the same price. product_title: La Chinata Sweet Spanish Smoked Paprika by Latienda
review_body:
I'm Hungarian and paprika is a national pastime in Hungary. While this isn't a Hungarian paprika, it is an excellent addition to any spice cabinet. The taste is bold, rich, and smokey (obviously), but with very little bitterness compared to most other paprikas. The smokiness overpowers the sweet, so it's not as sweet as an unsmoked sweet paprika. This isn't a spicy paprika. It has excellent dark red color and great aroma. It blends well into liquids.

It can be used alone as a more subtle seasoning, or if you want to really up the effect, mix it with just a little liquid smoke and/or toasted sesame oil to enhance the smokiness and add more complexity of flavor.

The canister is a bit difficult to open. You'll need to use a knife to pry it off, and if goes back on tightly so you will have to do that every time, not just on the first opening. I'd be happy to see a packaging redesign for an easier to open canister. The canister itself is attractive enough to display with other containers on an open shelf--it doesn't look like a typical cheap mass market spice jar.

review_body:

With Xanthan gum a gluten free product has the sought after texture of gluten laced products. Xanthan gum does not add any flavor to your favorite baking, but does give the much needed "glue" that holds the flour together.

The Xanthan gum 1lb bag when I purchased it was the lowest priced item of its type on Amazon. The thick plastic bag is re-sealable making it easy to store, and keep the gum from getting moister in it. The product itself is a fine slightly off white powder, and has performed excellently in breads, cake, cookies, and all manner of baking products.

product_title: Nutiva Organic Virgin Coconut Oil, 15 Ounce
review_headline: Where have you been all my life?
review_body:
I use it in place of butter in ALL my baking recipes. it all started because my lil guy can't have dairy. You have to learn how to bake a little differently: I find that if I melt over the stove the butter, and put it in my baking mixes as a LAST ingredient, it mixes best. If I put it in with the eggs in most recipes, since the oil is warm, I didn't want to semi cook the eggs. In soft butter recipes, I soften the oil just a bit so it has a similar "soft" consistency that softened butter would have. It takes getting used to, but was well worth the trial and error on my part.

My kids and I LOVE the taste of this oil with our popcorn. I put enough of the oil in the bottom of a saucepan to just cover the kernels, cover and cook on high. I hold the pan off of the stove so as not to burn the kernels. It gives it a buttery kind of taste. At first we felt like we tasted a bit of the coconut, but it could have been our noses. Now, we prefer it this way and LOVE it.

I've used it in stir fries but it clumps up too fast after the food cools. Don't like the taste of it in the stir fries.

review_headline: The ONLY legit Key Lime juice!
review_body:
Many lime pies are fobbed off as \\"key lime,\\" but only pies made with real key lime juice qualify. If you've never tasted a key lime, you have no idea how different is the flavor of key lime vs. regular lime. Many recipes allow the substitution of regular lime juice, but you will disappoint anyone who knows the actual flavor of a key lime if you try to fob it off on them as the real thing.

Nellie and Joe's Key West Lime Juice is the only product I know that is commercially available outside of Florida that is made entirely from actual key limes. There is nothing else that imparts the true flavor of the key lime.

Don't settle for less: Nellie and Joe's is the ONLY choice for those wishing to present true key-lime flavor!

product_title: Campbell's Go Soup Microwavable Pouch
review_headline: Thick, spicy & a nice change of pace for lunch but feeds only 1 without a salad or small sandwich
review_body:
The serving size for these microwave pouch said 2 per pouch but if I hadn't had a salad to go with it I could have easily eaten the entire pouch. Even so, it was a nice change of pace for Campbell's. Way better than their Chunky soups too. I liked that it had a healthy, high protein whole grain in there - the Quinoa. My wife puts that in her chicken soup now in place of pasta. There were noticeable chunks of chicken, black beans, corn, tomatoes and peppers among other items. The sodium rate seems high only if you count it as 1 serving then it would be about 395 mgs of sodium which is par for the course when it comes to prepared soups. I don't salt my food so whatever is in there is all I get. I tend to add pepper.

The packages was easy enough to set up in the microwave at work and nuke. No spills to speak of and I did share with a colleague. This is a decent alternative to a quick lunch out where I'd likely consume three times the calories. Therefore even considering the sodium count, I WOULD keep this in the kitchen at the office and maybe even eat the entire package. There's more sodium in most of the lunch meats I would get at Subway. If they sold them in multipacks via Subscribe & Save I would ask my wife to figure some into the budget. As singles, they don't seem that great a value unless you figure they saved you from going out to eat and kept you from spending $8 on lunch.

review_body: I am a huge fish lover and have tried almost every tuna brand on the market. My husband has always wanted to like fish but was on-again, off-again with tuna. We couldn't find a brand that he really loved, and I was spending five dollars a can because the Star-Kist, Bumblebee, and Chicken of the Sea brands are almost unedible. They inject them with vegetable broth to make them taste better, and that practice really turns me off. So, after seeing the reviews for Polar, thought I'd give it a try. Amazing! This is what tuna should taste like. It comes in big solid chunks, with just a bit of water and light salt. Now, my husband has me re-ordering regularly because he loves it so much. I also gave my parents a couple of cans to try, and they enjoyed it so much they ordered their own. You will not be disappointed!

product_title: ALOE GLOE Natural Aloe Water, 15.2 Ounce (Pack of 12)
review_body:
I had first heard about aloe water from a friend who had problems with acid reflux and recommended that I try it, as it had gotten him off otc meds. Having not gotten around to trying aloe yet, I was eager to try this product.

The taste is light and maybe a little reminiscent of apple, but not overpowering. The consistency was just like water, and very easy to drink when chilled... I downed it pretty quickly in enjoyment. Of course, for me, the main point was helping with acid reflux and I can say I definitely noticed a difference after drinking it. My tummy felt soothed and coated in a way that pepto just doesn't deliver. The acid was almost non existent all day long, which is very rare for me. I plan on trying the other flavors in this product while drinking one a day for good feeling reflux control.

product_title: Leila Bay Trading Company Himalayan Pink Finishing Salt (Fine) 4 Pack [Misc.]
review_body:
I'm talking about the Himalayan Pink Mineral Salt - Fine, 7 oz (198g) Product of the Himalayas, by the Leila Bay Trading Company est. 1997. We got our package from Home Goods for $5.99, I'm not sure how long ago (maybe in 2011 or 2012); I think it was a special purchase meaning they might not have it in stock at any particular time.

Taste. Ok, it's salt. It has a nice taste, but so does other salts.

Look. The crystals are about the same size as your table salt, but these are a light salmon color that they call pink.

Packaging. It is a jar that holds the salt in bulk. If you're going to use it on the table, then you'll need a spoon or you'll be taking pinches of this, or maybe you have a salt shaker you can put the salt into.

Note that this salt does not state that it contains iodine, an necessary nutrient.

Opinion. What makes this salt special is its color. What is lacking is a listing of the minerals that make up the salt. Take a look at another product that Amazon sells, "Redmond Real Salt" and you'll see a listing of the mineral makeup on the label; and it comes in a shaker.

My bottom line: I'll go for the "Real Salt" over this.

Biggest problem is that they may be too good - it's hard to stop at one or two but it's a good test of your self-discipline :) Treat yourself and buy these cookies! I heartily recommend them.

Kudos to the late Paul Newman for establishing a practical and wonderful way to support charitable causes. review_body:
I had a trip to Florida coming up and I thought an Irish accent would help me get the girls. So I'm in a hotel bar and I see some real hotties. I go into the mens room, take out a piece of gum and start chewing away. I head over to the table with the girls, tell them I've just arrived and ask them if they know of any local Irish pubs (I tell them I hate the taste of American beer). Well, the accent is awesome. In fact, I even say that American beer tastes like \\"s***e.\\" I've never used that word in my life!

So they think I'm \\"charming\\" and offer to walk me over to McSomething's Pub down the street. I'm really getting a good vibe from one of them and everything is great. We get to the Pub and I go to order a round and the words come out with NO ACCENT AT ALL! It wore off after only about 15 minutes. WTF? What am I going to do now, pull out my Irish Accent gum in front of everyone? It's too late by now. The girls give me a really awful \\"you're an a-hole\\" look, say they're going back to [whatever bar we came from], tell me they'll call the police if I follow them and walk out.

All I can say is that, for the price, I expected more than 15 minutes off one piece. Never again.

product_title: Milkmakers Oatmeal Chocolate Chip Lactation Cookies
review_headline: A cookie a day keeps the milk, um, flowing
review_body:
I've been exclusively breastfeeding my little girl since she was born in November 2012. Around three weeks post partum, I had a bout of mastitis, and because of that I had to pump from the affected breast and nurse on the unaffected one. This caused my supply to go down. I tried taking fenugreek pills but they irritated my baby and caused her horrid green slimy poo (sorry for the TMI).

A friend told me about lactation cookies... made with oatmeal. \\"Ewww, no no no, not oatmeal, ewww I can't stand the stuff,\\" I exclaimed (or something to that extent). But desperate to keep my supply up, I bought a bag of the chocolate chip oatmeal cookies. Upon first bite, and much to my surprise, I was hooked. They were yummy, delicious, tasty, and did not at all have the consistency of a bowl of oatmeal. Since that point, I've eaten a Milkmakers cookie every single day in the morning. I prefer to freeze mine and eat them right from the freezer, as I am not a fan of warm chewy cookies. If I'm feeling adventurous, I'll have one with some frozen yogurt. I know that one way to help increase your milk supply is to reduce stress, relax and be happy, and there is something about knowing you get to eat a big chocolate chip cookie every day that reduces stress, relaxes you and makes you happy. I will definitely keep eating these bundles of yummy goodness.

May 20: I wrote to Nature's Path to complain. They explained that they had a new plant manufacturing the cereal and that the new plant had failed to meet their expectations. product_title: Terre Exotique Espelette Chili Pepper (Basque), 1.4-Ounce Units (Pack of 2)
review_headline: Great subsitute for black pepper, Piment D'Espelette
review_body:
I have an adverse reaction to peppercorns (Malabar pepper and Tellicherry pepper). I was looking a substitute and saw this chili pepper being used to season fish on a cooking program. So, I did some research and found that this particular chili pepper is grown in France and used by the Basques of the Espellette region in place of pepper.

Espelette pepper is mild; in fact it only rates as 4 on the 'Scoville' pepper strength scale. It may lack in heat but the chili pepper has depth of flavor. Espelette has a unique and delicate flavor, with a hint of smokiness that compliments many different foods. It can be used to season fish, shellfish, poultry, beef, lamb, vegetables, soup, and eggs. I use Espelette pepper, in place of regular peppercorns.

product_title: OKONATUR 100% Extra Virgin Red Palm Oil - 16 Fl Oz
review_body:
I bought this product for its health benefits. Specifically palm oil contains tocotrienols that current research suggests might inhibit, oppose, or remove excess glutamate in the brain, a substance which is neurologically toxic and found in high amounts in the brains of those who suffer from severe OCD. My OCD is crippling, as in CRIPPLING, and I figured this was worth a try. I am also taking NAC & GABA for OCD - no really improvement in my OCD, but the GABA does have a calming effect, and both are well-tolerated.

Anyway, I decided to start with a tablespoon, opened the jar to give it a good smell - what a mistake - the odor & texture could be described as a thick, waxy, rancid parmesan cheese. I decided to give it a go in spite of this, gagged instantly, and almost puked right there in the kitchen. I'm not exaggerating.

So I thought well maybe if I didn't smell it prior to taking it I'd do okay with it. So the next time I made sure to avoid smelling it. This was NOT effective in avoiding the gag effect, and to make matters worse it left a waxy cheesy aftertaste for hours afterwards, even after brushing my teeth. Haven't tried it since - too scared!

I gave it a generous 2 stars because I imagine if I could handle the taste, it might actually provide some health benefits. It's also possible that when masked by other flavors in cooking, it might prove valuable there.

product_title: OliveNation Dried Cranberries - Superb for Snacking, Baking, Tossing with Salads Size of 8 oz
review_body:
I recently received these and I love 'em. I use them in my oatmeal as well as in dishes with wild rice and/or quinoa. It also makes a nice addition to dessert or meat dishes, especially pork or turkey... or of course as a snack :)

At any rate, I find these delicious.. not too dry, but also not any noticeable \\"wetness\\". I have read of other selections that reviewer's complain juice or water is in the package. That isn't true for these. They do not have to be soaked for most uses as they do retain a certain moisture content. They do not have that \\"bite\\" which you expect from fresh cranberries. I expect that is why growing/marketing groups add the sugar to promote them as a snack. In my own mind, I'd love to find \\"just cranberries\\" dried, but I have never seen them offered.

I received them promptly and reasonably packaged. (They were part of a multi-item order). Shipping is expensive, but if you can find several items to pack together, it makes for a more reasonable deal. JR Mushroom has a large list of items it sells if you go to their page. I like my experience from JR Mushroom, but most items received seems to be packed by OliveNation. I'm not sure of the connection.

I will say that in my experience with J R Mushroom's products they have been great. Its kind of a pain to be sure you're getting them from JR.. you have to go to the \\"xxx new\\" link and scan down the vendors until you find JR Mushroom, then click \\"add to cart\\" for each item until you're done. It's particularly important that you're buying all from the same vendor if you're grouping a purchase for shipping-cost savings.

The pricing is reasonable.. certainly you're not restricted here as MANY stores now carry \\"dried cranberries\\". I put that in quotes because you have to be careful what you're buying. Almost all have added sugar (as these do) and added vegetable-based oil (which I'm pretty sure these do.. isn't on the package nor the description, but I think I detect something).

If you have dried cranberries at your local stores (most \\"supermarkets\\" now carry them) you'd have to price it to see which is the better deal. I find the products to be similar to these. But if you don't have them available, you can order these with confidence.tect something).

If you have dried cranberries at your local stores (most \\"supermarkets\\" now carry them) you'd have to price it to see which is the better deal. I find the products to be similar to these. But if you don't have them available, you can order these with confidence.

product_title: Saf Instant Yeast
review_body:
Great quality yeast at a really cheap price.

Who am I to judge, but I'm a bit suspicious of reviews that state that the yeast didn't work (It worked fine for 50 other reviewers, but not for them? Go figure...)

If you buy this from Amazon you get 16 oz. of yeast for about the same price as 4 oz of yeast in those strips you buy at the supermarket. I just tossed the whole one-pound package into a zip-lock bag and keep it in my refrigerator.

Make SURE you understand the difference between the different types of yeast (which can be confusing!) This product is INSTANT YEAST. Here's some great info from the amazing folks at Cooks Illustrated:

Instant Yeasts: Also called \\"Instant,\\" \\"Rapid Rise,\\" or \\"Bread\\" instant yeasts are also processed to 95 percent dry matter, but are subjected to a gentler drying process than active dry. As a result, every dried particle is living, or active. This means the yeast can be mixed directly with recipe ingredients without first being dissolved in water or proofed. It is in this context that the yeast is characterized as \\"instant.\\" We prefer instant yeast in the test kitchen. It combines the potency of fresh yeast with the convenience of active dry, and it is considered by some to have a cleaner flavor than active dry because it contains no dead cells. (In our months of testing, we found this to be true when we made a lean baguette dough but could detect no difference in flavor when using the two yeasts in doughs made with milk, sugar, and butter.)

To substitute active dry for instant (or rapid rise) yeast: Use 25 percent more active dry. For example, if the recipe calls for 1 teaspoon of instant yeast, use 1 1/4 teaspoons of active dry. And don't forget to \\"prove\\" the yeast, i.e. dissolving it in a portion of the water from the recipe, heated to 105 degrees.

To substitute instant (or rapid rise) yeast for active dry: Use about 25 percent less. For example if the recipe calls for 1 packet or 2 1/4 teaspoons of active dry yeast, use 1 3/4 teaspoons of instant yeast. And you do not need to prove the yeast, just add it to the dry ingredients.

To substitute fresh yeast for active dry yeast, use a ratio of roughly 2:1, i.e. use one small cake (0.6 ounce) of compressed fresh yeast in lieu of 1 packet (.25 ounces) of active dry yeast.

Note a packet of active dry or instant yeast contains about 2 1/4 teaspoons (.25 ounces) of yeast.

product_title: Vegemite (220 gram)
review_body:
I was thrilled to find I could buy vegemite on Amazon. I'm an Aussie, been in the USA many years now and had the 'craving' for a lot of that time. Alas it's very hard to get here so I was amazed I could get it through Amazon. I bought 3x 220g jars for around $32 with free super saver shipping. Still very expensive compared to buying it off the shelves in Oz but it's worth it to me! My craving been sated finally.

Malty and salty, just the way I like it! It's primarily a breakfast spread that's great on toast but it can also be used as bullion cubes for cooking. It has consistency a little bit firmer than peanut butter but it's quite smooth to spread. I certainly love the stuff but it's an acquired taste, definitely. Keep it in the cupboard and not the fridge.

A US colleague of mine loves the stuff, because it reminds him of the tasty pan residue/drippings after cooking meat. Others I have let try it make such a screwed-up face you'd think I had given them sour warheads! Each to their own I guess.

Anyhoo... I will be buying it here from now on. Im a happy little vegemite =)

*UPDATE* I am on my last jar in the cupboard. The expiry date was some time in 2013, some 2 years out-of-date, but it's still just as good as the day I bought it. This stuff lasts a heck of a long time! If you're wondering why I stopped eating it to let it expire like that, well... sometimes you just gotta be in the mood for Vegemite. My mood has returned... haha! I need to stock up on some more now.

Ingredients: YEAST EXTRACT, SALT, POTASSIUM CHLORIDE, MALT EXTRACT(FROM BARLEY), COLOUR(E150d), CONTAINS PRESERVATIVE(SULPHUR DIOXIDE), VEGETABLE EXTRACT,(CONTAINS ONION, CELERY), NIACIN, THIAMINE, RIBOFLAVIN, FOLIC ACID.

product_title: EZ-Sweetz (1.05oz - Liquid Sweetener 400 Servings/Bottle)
review_headline: Not as concentrated as some of the other size bottles, but better for folks who like LESS sweet
review_body:
I've bought both concentrations--the one you'd find in the .5 oz bottle and in the 2 oz bottle. Because I like my mug coffee REALLY sweet, it's more convenient for me to have the .5 oz strenth concentration handy. I use 4 to 5 drops per mug, depending on how strong the brew/roast is and which mug I use. VERY SWEET.

However, I also buy the less concentrated type for when I want to be able to more finely control the sweetness level and I buy it for my relatives. The guys in the family don't need the supersweet drop for their espresso. So, they get the more diluted version. Easier to control sweetness level.

I say all this because THIS IS THE DILUTED VERSION in a smaller size (and different bottle type). If you don't mind using more drops per cup or recipe or whatever, then no problem. Just know this is not as concentrated as some other EZ SWEETZ sizes

If you normally get the 2 oz 800 serving size--the longer bottle with the yellow cap-- then know this is the same concentration, but the bottle is smaller and it's half the servings per bottle. That means the price is the same per serving: 800 servings for 12.99. The size may be more convenient for you to carry around is all. Some folks want a handier bottle for purses, for example.

If you use and enjoy the blue-capped/more concentrated version, this will disappoint.

I use both concentrations at home. I take a superconcentrated one in my purse to save space.

But this is a very convenient (if not necessarily healthful) product. It's got additives and there is concern for how this affects the intestinal flora. But unsweetened iced tea and coffee have no allure for me, and I used to be prediabetic. I can't indulge in sugar or lots of honey. So, I compromise with sucralose. And this has been my favorite Sucralose product. (Yes, I tried Sweetzfree without the additives and it was a disaster from the way it came out of the bottle--unmanageable--to how it clotted/clogged up the hole for dispensing. If they fixed those issues, I'd rebuy.) I stick mostly to sucralose cause I don't trust Equal or Sweet n Low, and can't stand the taste of Stevia. Until a more perfect sweetener arrives, EZ Sweetz is convenient for me.

review_headline: Wow - Brings Back Memories of Growing Up in the Islands.
review_body:
I grew up in the beautiful islands of American Samoa. And this product was a stable in our daily lives. We eat Arnotts Sao crackers mostly everyday after school as a snack before dinner is ready. I have not eaten these since I left the island in 1976 and here, in 2013 - I found them on Amazon and ordered them and they were AWESOME.

Aussie Products beat expectations by delivering my Arnotts Sao Biscuits on 1/28/2013 - when it was supposed to arrive by 2/05/2013 - AWESOME service.

Quality: Crackers are FRESH - I opened and ate them immediately upon arrival. Please note that these crackers, as I recalled back in the island, will TASTE STALE if they are stale - no hiding it but these arrived and tasted AWESOME - deliciously awesome with butter and peanut butter mixed together.

I would recommend these to anyone that grew up in the South Pacific and were used to eating Arnotts Sao Biscuits - these are JUST like what we grew up with - and there is a gap of 37 years for me since I've had these are they are still pretty tasty - brings back so many good memories of the easy life of growing up in the islands.

Thank you Amazon and Aussie Products - top shelf service all the way.

review_headline: This Sweetener Goes a LONNNGGG Way!
review_body:
My reason for switching from Honey to Agave Nectar is based on what I have learned about IF Ratings (inflammation factor) ~ Honey has an IF Rating of -1262 (HIGHLY inflammatory) versus Agave Nectar's IF rating of \\"N/A\\" (neither inflammatory nor anti-inflammatory) ~ it was a health-conscious purchase.

There is sooooo much *sweet* to Agave Nectar that I am still learning to adjust *down* so as to avoid over-sweetening ~ most *definitely* a bang for my buck, considering both the good taste & the health benefits also.

--------------------------------------------------------------
FOR THOSE INTERESTED IN AVOIDING INFLAMMATORY FOODS, HERE'S A BRIEF PRIMER:

IF (INFLAMMATION FACTOR) RATING
The IF (Inflammation Factor) Rating(tm) estimates the inflammatory or anti-inflammatory potential of individual foods or combinations of foods by calculating the net effect of different nutritional factors, such as fatty acids, antioxidants, & glycemic impact.

How to interpret the values: Foods with positive IF Ratings are considered anti-inflammatory, those with negative IF Ratings are considered inflammatory. The higher the number, the stronger the effect.

The goal is to balance negative foods with positive foods so that the combined rating for all foods eaten in a single day is positive.

It's almost too thin. If you brew a strong cup and use more coffee it's better but at that point I'd rather just brew a normal amount of the 454 for a better taste.

Not bad. But not the best I've had from Kicking Horse so far.

review_body:

product_title: POPCORNERS Carnival Kettle, Popped Corn Chips, Gluten Free, Non-GMO
review_body: If you like jalapeno cheese, popcorn and chips this is a trinity mix of the three. The texture is almost quilted. For a chip, it is quite healthy. These are gluten free and low in sugar and salt. Only 9% of fat recommendation, which is low. One serving is 150 calories. Zero cholesterol, too. They have a little kick to them so you will want a cool beverage nearby when you are snacking.  They are a pretty guilt-free snack. Love the flavor and texture. Good dipped in guacamole, too! Like their sea salt, white cheddar and kettle chips if you want to try those.  Here's the ingredients list from the company for the jalapeno chips:  INGREDIENTS: Enriched Yellow Corn (Yellow Corn, Niacin, Iron, Thiamine Mononitrate, Riboflavin, Folic Acid), Canola Oil, Extra Virgin Olive Oil, Jalapeno Peppers, Natural Cheddar Cheese Flavor (Whey, Reduced Lactose Whey, Maltodextrin, Cheddar and Blue Cheese (Cultured Milk, Salt, and enzymes), Canola Oil, Salt, Disoldium Phosphate, Citric Acid, Lactic Acid), Jalapeno Spice (Parsley Flakes, Dextrose, Jalapeno Pepper Powder, Onion Powder, Garlic Powder, Spices and Natural Flavors).  Contains dairy ingredients  May contain Soy Ingredients

product_title: Salted Nut Roll: 5LBS
review_body:
This was one of my favorite candy bars when I was growing up.
I had not seen them for many years. Happy to find again on Amazon. Taste just the same. Another generation can enjoy this fine Pearson's candy.

product_title: KIND PLUS Gluten Free Bars
review_headline: BEWARE: AVOID IF PREGNANT or BREASTFEEDING
review_body:
It really upsets me that there isn't a disclaimer on the Kind bars about not eating this product while pregnant!! I've been eating these as a healthy snack while pregnant and had NO idea until I decided to google one of the ingredients: chicory root fiber.

\\"The use of chicory root extract is not safe during pregnancy. Chicory root may stimulate uterine bleeding and can cause fetal death. For these reasons, expectant and breastfeeding mothers should not use chicory root extract\\"

This company should be ashamed!

product_title: Gerrit's Satellite Wafers, Filled with  Assorted Candy Beads, 10.5 Oz.  240-Count Boxes (Pack of 2)

product_title: Camomile Herbal Tea

product_title: Gloria Jean's Keurig K-Cups
review_headline: Gloria Jean's coffee seems to be my favorite
review_body: I've tried other brands, but Gloria Jean's is still my favorite. Tastes natural, where other brands have off-tastes to them.

product_title: King Arthur Flour Multipurpose Flour, Gluten Free, 24-ounces
review_body: We use this one for baking sweets -- where we can't use some other gluten free flours. This one is truly the best replacement for normal flour that I've found. But, because it is more costly we save it for those recipes where we need to make sure we get it just right.

product_title: Bell Plantation PB2 Powdered Peanut Butter and PB2 with Premium Chocolate, 6.5 Ounce
review_body: Seller shipped fast and the items arrived in perfect condition. 5 stars for service. As for the taste, I just had the chocolate pb and it's aite, doesn't beat regular creamy pb though. Also 2 tbsp + 1tbsp water is too much for just one slice of bread.

product_title: Bauducco Gran Natalee Special Pantone Cake, 31.7 Ounce
review_body: Every year  we buy Panettone for Christma morning this time I have the idea that I can order this and save time Ohhh God and very sorprised when we eat this the bread is very dry and no flavor...I go and buy one in the store close of my house for New Year and is so good and for 1/4 of the price that I pay in Amazon never order again

review_body: it was nice flowers but they didnt ship it accurately as i specified the delevary date to be on the valentien day... they deliver it 9 days before valentine day! me n my fiancee were totally upset..

product_title: Prince Of Peace Organic Oolong Tea

review_body: I like this tea.  I purchased this on December 19, 2012 for 4.99 w/Prime, now that I'm out I go to re-order and the price doubled to $10.  Good tea, but the unstable pricing model will have me shopping elsewhere.

product_title: Crystal Light Lemonade (Makes 32-Quart), 4-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 3)
review_body: Yes, I got what I payed for but it took longer than I had hoped. It waS worth it though because it was a good deal so thank you!

product_title: Alaska Smokehouse Smoked Sockeye Salmon Fillet In Gold, 8 Ounce Gift Box
review_body:
First, to clarify the description: this is *hot* smoked salmon, not cold smoked.

This has *a lot* of salt in it. One 2oz piece has 23% of your daily recommended salt intake. So an ungenerous dinner portion of 4oz would have nearly half your daily salt in it, and you can really taste it. To my taste, it is too salty.

The flavor (besides the saltiness) is OK, I'd rank it in the bottom third of all smoked salmons I'd ever tasted. That's just a matter of personal preference, of course. For reference, I have eaten many smoked salmons (hot and cold).

The presentation is OK. Don't expect to put it on a platter to show off to guests. For a Tuesday night family dinner (as we just had) it was fine.

Bottom line: I wont buy this again.

product_title: Lambertz Mozart Kugeln Gift 200g
review_body: As a true marzipan connoisseur, this is one of the best Mozart Kugelins I've tasted.  Rich and yummy!!  Highly recommend it.

product_title: 3 Box (36packets) Italian Roast Starbucks VIA Ready Brew Instant Coffee
review_body: Arrived quickly and exactly as ordered.  The last time I ordered via and thought I was getting 3 packs of 12, I actually got 3 packs of 3 so thanks for sending me what I actually purchased.

product_title: Organically Processed, Unrefined Natural Sea Salt, Hand Harvested, 100% Natural, Eco-Friendly.
review_body: I love salt! The good stuff that is... Typically I use the Himalayan variety so at first I was a bit skeptical. But this stuff rocks! No pun intended. It's got a smooth yet complex taste and the size and texture is perfect for both direct consumption, cooking or finishing. The picture of the salt is a bit whiter than when you see it in person.

product_title: Sam Mills Pasta D'Oro Gluten Free, Lasagne Corte, 1-Pound (Pack of 6)
review_body:
Pasta D'oro is my favorite gluten free pasta. Similar texture to wheat noodles. But don't let the name fool you. Its not a lasagna noodle. This is a small flat noodle. Its great for casseroles, soups, any dish you would want a flat noodle in.
The package arrived quickly and was in great shape. I would buy again when I run out.

product_title: Big Train Spiced Chai, 1.9-Pound Cans (Pack of 2)
review_headline: Big Train Spiced Chai, 1.9-lb cans (pack of 2)
review_body: I have ordered this chai several times before, and have enjoyed it each time. Great buy. My order arrived quickly and what I expected.

product_title: Puntini Italian Jujubes Frutti Assortiti 2lb (SUGAR)
review_body: Small but packs a punch. I love the apple and blueberry flavors together. Strawberry is good too. Orange is okay and lemon is nasty, which they would get rid of that flavor. Very expensive, but a nice splurge once and a while.

this cereal is delicious

product_title: SUPER Big Bol Candy Bubble Gum (240 count)

product_title: Stash Tea Fruity Herbal Tea Six Flavor Assortment, 18-20 Count Tea Bags in Foil (Pack of 6)
review_body: Fruity flavors, but not really that great. They're a bit bitter and bland, so I was a bit disappointed. I've had better.

product_title: Body Choice Wild Berry Smoothie, 16-Ounce Bottles (Pack of 12)
review_headline: Seems very sparse on the juice
review_body:
The one reviewer that listed the ingredients omitted the parentheses around the juices meaning that all of them together are the same weight or more than the sugar. It also has 0% vitamin A (C is added). From the taste of this, I would bet it is around 8% juice (1/4 cup per bottle) and they do not state on the bottle or their web site. I would definitely prefer more juice and less/no sugar (it has sucralose); this might also reduce the 'kool-aide' type flavor (the juice flavor is very muted compared to the sweet).

I do like that they did not put Acelfame Potassium nor artificial colors in this product.

Product does not state where it is made.

product_title: Newman's Own Special DECAF Coffee Keurig 4 Boxes of 24 K-Cups
review_body: I have to drink decaf coffee, most of which taste like warm water.  Newman"s tastes like regular coffee.  It's all I use.

product_title: Mint Juleps Candy-2 1/2 lbs.
review_headline: Takes me back to the early sixties.
review_body: I have hunted for these for years, They are great. Just like I remembered them; except for the wrappers, then they were light green and white. I'll order again when I can.

product_title: Seitenbacher Musli, #5 Choco Max, 16-Ounce
review_body: The taste and the texture of this muesli is addictive. Try it with some flaked coconut and even more so...if you're buying this to add fiber to your diet then go for it, but it may end up adding extra calories too-it is simply impossible to adhere to the serving size due to the fact it is irresistible.

product_title: Pamela's Products Chunky Chocolate Chip Cookies
review_headline: Good in general, not just good for gluten free
review_body: These cookies don't taste like regular store-bought Peanut Butter Cookies, so if you go into it not expecting a certain flavor or texture, you will really like these. I'm new to GF and may return to a diet that includes gluten, but I still like these. If they were on sale and I were eating gluten, I'd still buy them. The peanut butter flavor isn't too powerful, it's a light cookie. Both my kids enjoyed them too.

product_title: Pumpkin Seed Kernels Light Sea Salt - 2 Pound Deal
review_body:
Pumpkin Seed Kernels Light Sea Salt - 2 Pound Deal (no shells)
Ordered for a healthy snack for me but the whole family enjoyed them. This \\"rate your purchases\\" from Amazon just reminded me to order some more. Recommended not only for an easy healthy snack but they really do taste better than any other shelled pumpkin seeds I've ever tried...and my picky teenagers agreed.

product_title: Simpli Naked Oat Beverage, the Delicious Alternative to Dairy and Soy
review_body: This is the best oatmilk on the market. We cannot drink soy or nutmilk so oatmilk is a staple at my house. We have tried many brands and this is the best tasting and has the best consistency that we have ever tried.

product_title: Food For Life, 7 Grains Bread, Sprouted, Organic, 24oz
review_headline: Good Bread/But cheaper at your local store.
review_body: I buy this bread at my local Festival Foods and it's only 4 or 5 dollars, why they are charging $14 on Amazon is beyond me. But if you can get your hands on it at your local store, it is probably the healthiest bread you can get. It is just grains so it works as a bread for eating purposes, but also goes toward your whole grain allotment for the day. and it tastes very good with Almond Butter. I make my own Almond Butter at home, I roast 1 lb Organic Almonds at 350 degrees for 15 minutes or less sometimes 10. Put into food processor, count on it taking 15 minutes or so. After it turns to butter I add 1 tablespoon local Honey, it will clump temporarily, just let it run until it returns to smooth butter consistency.

product_title: Native Forest Organic Coconut Milk
review_headline: Native Forest Organic Classic Coconut Milk
review_body: Excellent for making cream of butternut squash soup and cream of tomato/basil soup.  Good quality...not 'runny' as some i have used in the past.  I will order it again!

product_title: 5 FRAGRANT Paperwhite Daffodil Flower Bulbs
review_body: I like to decorate with flowers. When my flowers can double as an air freshener, it's heaven. These smell great!

product_title: IZZE Fortified Sparkling Juice, Pomegranate, Pack of 24, 8.4 oz Cans
review_headline: Great deal when it is on!
review_body: I always loved izze. Its real juice instead of sugar after all. With the 50% off deals, this is great! if you don't like not so sweet sodas, this is not for you. but if you like natural juice soda, this is it!

product_title: RiseBar Energy Organic, 12-Count Bars
review_body:
I love these bars for the variety, nutrition and taste. They are also a good value.
It's all good and healthy

product_title: Hydro Herbal 50g Spearmint Hookah Shisha Tobacco Free Molasses
review_body: A lot of shisha flavors are not very dramatic and are very faint, this is not the case with this one. It's very prominent, and it's GOOD. It's similar to double-mint gum. I originally picked it up because I tried this brand on a whim at a smoke shop, and it ended up being very very good. It's tobacco, tar, and nicotine free, no weird after-taste that you get with some of the starbuzz flavors, and it's cheaper. I decided to get this smaller pack just to try out the flavor, but I will probably order a larger tin now. For those wondering, it's 50g, which is about 1/5 of what the normal tins contain (about 2/5 if it's starbuzz).

product_title: Sour Patch Kids Candy
review_body: Purchased these for my son.  I can't find the Blue Raspberry in the store and was happy to finally find then on line.

product_title: Quaker Real Medleys Cherry Pistachio Oatmeal +,  (Pack of 12)
review_body: This tasted a bit on the crunchy side. I'm not sure if that's how it's supposed to turn out, but how it turned out for me. It tasted really good though with the fruit chunks in it. A nice change from regular oatmeal and I can see this as being great for work or if you are in a hurry in the morning as you dont have to mess with a bowl. Just throw out the container! (I hope the material is biodegradeable?) I had the Cherry Pistachio.

product_title: Cappuccino Classics Gift Collection
review_headline: Best Christmas present for a coffee drinker
review_body: I'm always trying to find something a little different for my husband at Christmas.  He loves coffee and has developed a liking for Cappuccino.  This gift collection had variety and the option to make just a cup or two.

product_title: Emeril's Jazzed Up Decaf Coffee, K-Cup for Keurig Brewers
review_body: Best Keurig decaf to date. Still not strong & rich enough for me, but with this type of maker, I guess the bar is set pretty low.

product_title: Ova Easy Egg Crystals, 4.5 oz/Bag
review_body:
I made a batch of scrambled eggs using fresh eggs and one batch made with this Ova Easy egg product and neither I or my husband could tell the difference. They are so good and the prep couldn't be easier. 2 parts water to 1 part egg product, mix well and cook. De-lish!
We are going to order more for sure. We are lucky in that the producers of this wonderful product is in our backyard almost so we can get it directly from them.
We tried the Mountain House eggs and bacon and it was terrible! Rubber.
This Ova Easy is the real thing with a long shelf life.
I ordered from the company directly and they have this 4.5 oz envelope for only .01 shipping so you can try it with practically free shipping. What a great deal. I can guarantee though, that if you try it, you will like it and get more!

product_title: Green Mountain Coffee French Vanilla,  K-Cup Portion Pack for Keurig K-Cup Brewers, 24-Count
review_body: This k cup coffee flavor has a pleasant taste. I recommend it over the French vanilla flavor. Green Mountain k cup coffees are mostly very good

product_title: Trader Joe's Vanilla Meringues Cookies
review_body:
These cookies are guilt free pleasure. I guess if you don't have a Trader Joe's within reasonable travel distance you will pay anything. Certainly it's cheaper then an airplane ticket or a 4 hour ride (figure in gas/time). The price listed here is about 3x's what Trader Joe's sells them for in the store. My nearest TJ's is about 45 minute drive and I buy 6 to 10 at a time. Serving size is 4 cookies, 7 servings in a 7.39 container. Ingredients: sugar, egg whites, natural flavor, vanilla extract. That's it . . . . . no preservatives or artificial color, low sodium and gluten free. I gave this 5 stars to rate the product, not the price
These are worth the trip, they melt in your mouth all the while your taste buds are begging for more . . . . hmmmmmmmm good!

product_title: Mochi Sweet Rice Cake Topping - White 300g 10.58oz
review_body: I bought these after trying them at pinkberry. They are just as delicious and make a lovely surprise for that pinkberry addict in your life.
