review_body: Great product! I use it for my greens, beans, and string beans. I recommend this seasoning to family and friends.

product_title: Quaker Real Medleys (Pack of 12)
review_body: Received this product as a sample from Influenster, and I'm glad I did! This is a great, high quality oatmeal with great flavor and taste. Great for me since I travel - I can grab it in the morning put in boiling water and it's ready to eat when I am. Also it's just as good if not better than some of the coffee shop oatmeals!

product_title: Oregon Kombucha Pear Ginger Black Tea Basic Starter Kit
review_body: The little square of "starter" came in a sealed pack and I let it rest. A few days later I brewed some THAI tea, mixed in some pure cane sugar, the "little guy" "scoby, covered w. a towel and left it in peace. Today, scoby has spawned at least 3 children and PAPA SCOBY is the size of a frisbee. I take him out of fluid and give him a good washing under cold water, he has specks of THAI tea all over and has about 10 layers of growth. I swear he has a personality. I treat him like a favorite guest in the house. He just chugs along in his new home producing "kids". I will do business with this seller again. Thank you for the joy.

product_title: Pepsi Cola, 12-Ounce Cans (Pack of 24)
review_headline: a lot, cheap, but almost no CO2 when arrives

product_title: Community Coffee Private Reserve Whole Bean Coffee, Louisiana Blend, 12-Ounce Bags (Pack of 3)
review_body: Ordered it and was thinking of my visits to Louisiana. tasted it this mornign and remembered why I ordered it. I am thinking of Louisiana again.

review_body:

product_title: La Tourangelle Avocado Oil, 16.9-Ounce Tins (Pack of 2)
review_body: Because of its high smoking point, this makes the best oil for cooking on the stove top. It has a really neutral flavor too.

product_title: Nutiva Coconut Sugar 1 lb Pkg
review_body: Great taste!  Much different taste from regular sugar and honey and gives a great sweetness with the same amount used.  It is supposed to have a variety of health benefits, but it is still a sweetener, so use lightly.

product_title: David Rio Power Chai (non dairy) 14 oz. Chai Mix Canister
review_body: This is the best Chai tea latte powder!!! Pairs very well with a milk frother. I will definitely re-order this item!

product_title: Nature's Bakery Whole Wheat Fig Bar, 6 Count (Pack of 12)
review_body:
2 servings/package. 110 calories/cookie. 2g protein/cookie.

These fig bars are just about right in terms of sweetness - not terribly sweet, but they have a \\"sweet tooth\\" satisfaction to them. They also aren't too dry like some other fig cookies. As compared to the standard fig bar, these are tastier & seem more filling even though they are about the same size.

In my opinion, the main drawback is that the calorie content is high versus the size of the cookie/bar. There is a slight amount of protein, but not enough to overcome the calorie content.

product_title: Hansen's Diet Soda Cans (Pack of 24)
review_body: Cherry flavor Hansen's is better without vanilla. The combination of flavors makes the vanilla taste artificial. It has an aftertaste.

product_title: Sees Candies Dark Chocolates
review_body: See's never disappoints. The product is fresh and yummy. In the summer, they pack it with an ice pack. I have to put it in the fridge to keep myself from eating it all in a few days. YUM I repeat YUM!

product_title: Thai Kitchen Onion Instant Noodle, 1.6000-Ounce (Pack of 12)
review_body: Good flavor with lots of noodles also easy and quick to prepare. Will buy again when this batch is finished.

product_title: Hawaii Roasters 100% Kona Coffee, Medium Roast, Whole Bean, 14-Ounce Bag
review_body: This is some very good coffee, but still a bit pricy for me.  I wish Kona coffee was more affordable.

product_title: Pastariso Instant Rice Mac and Cheese Meal Cup, 2 Ounce (Pack of 6)
review_body:
I am not a big fan of most gluten free products, or products that come in little cups and cook in the microwave. But since I have family members who visit who NEED to eat gluten free, I decided to take a taste.

This has a tiny line (like most of these cups) around 3/4-1 inch below the rim. You fill the cup with water to that line, then microwave it for 3.5 minutes. You then stir it and let it sit for at least a minute. I waited till it cooled to my eating temperature.

This tastes similar to the mac and cheese individual packets, so it is very well done to match it. Some of the liquid spilled over when mine was heating, and I found mine to be a bit dry. So I added a spoonful of butter. If you are going to eat a comfort food like mac and cheese, butter is always a nice addition. ;-)

After I added butter I liked it - not as much as home made, but still, very OK.

For those on a gluten free diet, you will not be disappointed, this really does taste like your old favorite, and it comes in a convenient individual portion, so your family can have the old fashioned stuff, and you can eat this.

product_title: Chef Paul Prudhomme's Magic Seasoning Blends ~ No Salt & No Sugar Seasoning Blends: Toasted Onion & Garlic
review_body: I had the pleaure of meeting Chef Paul years ago at the Chicago NRA show. Have been using his products for years. Was really happy to see that they finnally started selling salt and surgar free products. Same great herbs and blends and no salt or sugar!

product_title: Tuscan Dairy Whole Vitamin D Milk, Gallon, 128 oz
review_body: As it states in the fine print on the label, \\"Call your doctor if you have an erection lasting more than 4 hours after drinking Tuscan whole milk.\\"  They should really make this warning more obvious.  Six hours into my boner I passed out and awoke covered in Tuscan whole milk.

product_title: Vegemite Jar
review_body:
Well, if you have tasted vegemite you already know what you are in for. There is not much to say here ... I just love vegemite (not marmite or others).
I normally buy the 400gr jar and a couple of tubes. I do a fair amount of camping, hiking, travelling overall, and the tubes are perfect for this. I can take them anywhere I want and space/weight are not really an issue. Only when I ran out of my 400gr jar I use this at home.
I don't have any kids (well, one is on the way) but I imagine that this is something kids can take with them to sleepovers, camping trips, etc...
If you like vegemite and sometimes have issues with carrying even small jars with you ... the tubes are the answer.

product_title: Arabian Mocha Sanani Roasted Coffee - 5 Lb Whole Beans
review_body: I have purchased this coffee from Bradford Coffee for several years now.  I have no idea what the berater is talking about.  I have found that it is easy to use too much coffee, thus it is bitter.  Too little and it is weak.  When you're brewing pot ratio is determined through experimentation you will be satisfied.  The way you grind the bean is also a factor to reckon with.  Bradford is quick to ship and the bag they use is the one way valve type.  Very standard in the industry.  The only complaint I have is that their email address is not working so you can't contact them via email.  Phone only.  Enjoy your Sanani.  When brewed correctly it is great and satisfying. [...].  I am simply a customer and have no other relationship with Bradford Coffee.

product_title: Walker's Toffee Selection 400g
review_headline: A little bit of everything and a hammer on top!
review_body: Ideal gift for the toffee lovers out there. Creamy and delicious, no artificial ingredients and also gluten free. Great for expats missing the taste of real British toffee!

product_title: Eight O'Clock Coffee Decaffeinated Whole Bean Coffee, 36-Ounce
review_body: We can't drink regular coffee at night, but we can drink this at night.  A pot gets made at dinner time and lasts through the evening.

product_title: Haribo Kinder Schnuller (Pacifiers) -200g
review_body: This product was an item that we got as a child in Germany.  I haven't seen it in the US.  I pad the price though! $6.00 a bag! A little too expensive!

product_title: Sorbee Sugar Free Chewy Candy, Cherry Bites, 5-Pound Bag
review_body: I am a diabetic and the use of sugar free candy allows me to enjoy non-harmful entrees to my diet and allows me to keep my glucose levels under control.

product_title: Montebello Kitchens De-Fatted Peanut Flour with Prebiotics, 8 Ounce
review_headline: So delicious, but so healthy too!
review_body:
What an amazing nutty taste - perfect for fat free peanut butter (just add water, and salt or sugar if you desire), but light enough tasting to substitute for regular flour in your baking! review_body:

I filled an old 16 oz Planters Peanuts jar and keep it on the shelf to have a handful or two at a time. It's very satisfying that way and takes the edge off hunger. The main benefits are fiber (5g) and protein (5g) per half cup. I dinged a star because the sugar content is high at 13g; this granola really doesn't need to be as sweet as it is. It also carries 5g of fat, .5 of those saturated. There are modest amounts of Calcium, Iron, Thiamin, Phosphorus, Magnesium and Potassium.

Ingredients: Whole grain rolled oats, whole grain rolled wheat, brown sugar, raisins, canola oil, whey, inulin, almonds, nonfat dry milk, glycerin, whey protein concentrate, honey, natural flavor (contains coconut components), sunflower oil, natural mixed tocopherols (added to preserve freshness).

I am especially happy to note that The Center for Science in the Public Interest (CSPINET), which previously listed inulin as a food additive to avoid, now lists it as safe. Yay! Lastly, it's true, as other reviewers have noted, that you do have to pick this stuff out of your teeth, but I'm really not going to hold that against it.

product_title: Schar Pasta Tagiatelle, 12-Ounce (Pack of 10)
review_body:
Due to my wife's gluten sensitivity, our family has spent the last year learning about all of the products in our pantry packed with gluten. Initially, my wife would prepare two dinners - one for her and one for the rest of us (me plus two kids). We slowly introduced GF sweets to the kids to win them over on the concept. But the two biggest problems we ran into were breads and pasta. My wife keeps her own Udi's GF bread loaf in the freezer and we occasionally order pizza from Domino's (they have a decent GF crust, though expensive), but we could never find a GF pasta that anyone liked, including my wife. Then we tried Schar Penne Pasta. It was good enough for everyone to eat, as long as the flavor of the sauce was strong, and you ignored the after taste. It did not reheat well at all, though.

Eventually, we gave the Tagliatelle noodles a try and were thrilled. The noodles cook quickly and taste great, even with just a little butter and parmesan cheese. There is no awkward after taste and the texture is just like regular noodles. They still don't reheat well, but do better than the Penne. Be warned, once they are cooked, they look paper thin and almost clear, but they are still substantial enough for spaghetti and casseroles.

Pros: Cooking ease, taste, texture

Cons: Price, reheating, availability

Our family now eats Schar GF Tagliatelle noodles almost exclusively. Our local stores carry it for $4.50 a box and it is often out of stock, so ordering in bulk from Amazon (we eat two boxes a week) at $3.50 a box plus free (Prime) shipping is a great solution for us. I just wish they would add this product to Subscribe-and-Save.

The five-star rating is based on the GF nature of the product. If that were not a factor, it would get four stars due to the cons listed above.

product_title: Amazing Grass Green Superfood
review_body:
I have been using Amazing Grass powders for about 3 years now, mostly during the winters when I am more prone to getting sick. I drink it almost daily during the winter for an energy boost and to prevent common winter time illness. I normally drink 2 scoops when I feel like I am getting sick. I didn't take it everyday because the texture is horribly gritty, so much so that I would dry heave from time to time after drinking it. But it's better than being sick for a week or two with a cold. I drink it and my cold is completely gone within 2-3 days, and I get a good energy boost, so the benefit is worth it to me.

I was elated when I found the capsules. No more gritty texture and all the health benefits I thought. So this past month when I woke up with a nasty cold, I started my usual regimen of 2-3 servings/day of this stuff. I took a total of 10-15 capsules/day. Usually when I drink the powder, I wake up the next day feeling a great deal better better. Not this time. I woke up a whole lot worse. Day 2, woke up worse than the day before. Day 3...I felt horrible! All while taking the capsules. I also did not notice an energy boost like I would get with the powder. A few weeks later when I got yet another cold, I tried it again thinking maybe I had just a really strong virus....nope...it was like I had never taken anything at all. Sick for almost 2 weeks! I don't want to give this product a horribly low rating, because I do think that the powders are really great. I don't know if they do anything differently to the product to put it in capsules, but for me, it just doesn't seem to work. Will be trying out a new capsule supplement, because I just can't do the gritty texture of the powders anymore. If worse comes to worse and I can't find anything, I probably would go back to drinking the powders again.

product_title: Lipton Herbal Pyramid Tea Bags, Blackberry Vanilla, 18 Count
review_headline: Lipton's attempt at a high-end tea
review_body:
This is the latest in Lipton's attempts to produce more of a high-end product.

The tea is in triangular bags just as some of the higher end stuff (think [[ASIN:B004AGU1AO Tea Forte Large Tin Sampler Collection]] and [[ASIN:B000PGQQFC Harney & Sons Fine Teas Hot Cinnamon Spice - 50 Tea bags]]) but Lipton's bags aren't true silk.

The tea itself has pieces of fruit (in this case hibiscus) but also \\"natural flavors\\". I am sensitive to corn, and the vanilla flavor that's added to this tea is definitely corn-based because my skin (it generally is noticeable on my face when I consume corn) became red immediately.

This doesn't happen when I consume high-end teas that contain natural flavors that don't have corn in them such as aforementioned Tea Forte or some of the varieties of [[ASIN:B000GC42TC Mighty Leaf Variety 15 Bags]].

Here are the ingredients from the ingredients list on the box: hibiscus flowers, rosehips, sweet blackberry leaves, natural flavor, dried black currant (misspelled as \\"current\\" on my box) pieces, sunflower lecithin.

This is certainly a right step in the right direction, but please try harder at having real ingredients and no corn in your teas, Lipton.

product_title: UCC - Special Blend 3 in 1 Coffee Mix (10 Sachets)
review_headline: My Favourite Just Add Water Coffee
review_body:
I was introduced to this convenient sweet instant coffee when I was in Japan. Mainly because of flavour and then ease of use, it quickly became my favourite instant coffee. I just pour in hot water and stir, just the right combination of coffee, cream and sugar are already inside each packet. No messing around with jars of stale crystals, and little packets of sugar and cream spilling all over. It is a mellow, sweet coffee in taste, but it seems to be loaded with caffeine for a good morning or afternoon pick me up. It is the perfect companion when traveling, hiking or camping as it only takes minutes to whip up. And, it can even be mixed and enjoyed cold or iced! I add it to ice water or my water bottle and just shake it up. I find it very refreshing. When mixed with hot milk it makes a tasty frothy latte, with foamy top.

It is made by the most trusted brand in Japanese coffee, UCC, who invented the canned coffee (both hot and cold) that are available seemingly in every nook and corner in Japan in vending machines. I think the individual vacuum sealed envelopes are a brilliant idea as the coffee stays fresh and hermetically sealed for a long time. Those jarred instant coffees seem to go stale by the time you get to the bottom, especially if you buy a larger more economical size. And of course, creamer and sugar are separate.

I buy these boxes of UCC coffee at Asian markets in the US for about $2.68 each when they are on sale, but normally they cost about $3.18. For the convenience of a nice cup of Joe whenever I feel like it, I think it is a good investment.

The taste is great, and with only five calories per serving, you can even add a splash of your favorite spirit and stay within your dietary goals. I really liked this product, the colder the better. I froze the mocktails into ice cubes, and then crushed them in my blender and poured them over a jigger of tequila, or even just served them alone with a sprig of mint. Of course, if you add the alcohol, you may be defeating the purpose of using this as a diet aid, but the taste is nice all on its own.

Recommended.

review_body:

Some of the almonds turned out great. However, at the price I was not happy about having to throw way an entire 4lb package of these because the quality was terrible. I shouldn't have to constantly sample almonds while preparing them. Next time I will purchase locally to ensure better quality nuts.

The price is low, but so is the quality.

product_title: Fiuggi Natural Mineral Water (6 Bottles)
review_body:
I was in italy when I was 12 years old in 1974 and remember visting a place called Fiuggi when I went to visit famliy there. It was supposed to have the best water ever and remember people buying it like crazy.
One day about a few months ago I started reminicing about my trip and the places i visited, and to my suprise I came accross this water that was being bottled and being sold in the US.
I had to try it even if it was just one time. I placed the order for 2 cases, shipping was a little rough but figured it would be worth it. It came out to about $5 a bottle with the shipping.
It was well worth it! After drinking all those basic Spring Waters and Purified Waters that are available in the US, I can taste the difference. This water is very light tasting with no after taste, very smooth.
It was a very enjoyable beverage at our dinner table for Thanksgiving. I wouldn't reccomend drinking it all the time because of the cost factor but for special occasions its a pleasure to know some things have'nt changed.
It is definately worth a try andwould highly reccomend it.

product_title: Bell Plantation PB2 Powdered Peanut Butter
review_body: I originally purchased PB2 products for travel food but I find that I tend to not mix them to eat when traveling.  Instead, I now use them in cooking experiments.  For example, I mixed powdered PB2 in with the dry ingredients when making pancakes and made peanut butter pancakes.  Powder in this case blended seamlessly with the batter.  I appreciate that it does not add as much fat to a recipe as conventional peanut butter.  I also have used this in cookie recipes when mixing up cookie batter in my mini bread machine.  I can add a scoop of peanut butter powder to add peanut flavor to a dozen cookies.  When mixing the butter to eat, you can choose if you want it thick or thin.  It can be nice to make it thin, like a dip.  I flavor is different than conventional peanut butter and it is not greasy, but it is a flavor I have come to like.  Just be aware that it tastes different.  I would like to learn more about how this product is created.  It probably doesn't count as a "whole" food, but I personally feel it is an acceptable processed food until I hear otherwise.

product_title: Heinz Baked Beans in Tomato Sauce
review_body:
Real beans! And on subscription, they're at normal food prices, instead of at "Look at this expensive British import" prices that one finds at specialty food retailers.

Recommended traditional usage:
Eating
Eating on toast
Eating with bacon & eggs
Eating with sausage & eggs

Clever thing I came up with:
Cut up bacon or sausage into smallish pieces, and fry in a small pot. Once the meat is cooked, drain off excess fat (If it's bacon, you can make your own lard this way!), and then add in a can of beans. Once the beans are well heated, add a small amount of grated British cheddar (Or any other cheese, if you can't get the good stuff), and stir it in until melted. Easy, filling breakfast!

Also, I had read that this type of tea is good for lowering cholesterol, so I went out to buy it after a trip to the doctor & an order to lower my cholesterol. review_body: I ordered the variety pack A and received it within two days for pick up across the border in Sumas,Wa as I live in Surrey,BC. I am happy to say it was still frozen solid. I am not sure what the fuss is about xanthan gum being used by one reviewer as it is a completely naturally derived vegan emulsifier/ stabilizer commonly used for sauce consistency. So I guess that makes it a gluten free alternative to flour as well. I also thought the use of oats in the turkey meatballs was great because most of the time a wheat product is used. I have to support a brand like this so I can find it on store shelves everywhere some day soon. There is a lot to like about Lyfe.

product_title: Kirkland Signature Extra Virgin Olive Oil
review_body:
So in the spirit of full disclosure I need to say that I bought this olive oil without particularly high expectations. My thought process had basically been this: I cook with olive oil a LOT. I go through a ton of it in a month. My local grocer only sells relatively small bottles at high prices... and I really don't need a particularly high quality olive oil just to saute a little garlic and such.

I did not buy this expecting it to be of a quality I'd be willing to use as an herbed oil dip for bread... or even of a quality that I'd be willing to use as a dressing for salad or tossed veggies.

So it was a very pleasant surprise to find that I can use it for both and still enjoy the taste!

Is this comparable to a specially pressed olive oil that has been lovingly prepared by ancestral monks in a remote abbey high in the mountains of Greece through a process handed down through a thousand generations and then sold only to those who are willing to pay a few thousand dollars AND walk through fire? Uh...no... and quite frankly, if you buy this expecting it to compare to a high grade olive oil, you probably shouldn't be allowed near the open-flame of a stove to begin with.

But if you are looking for a good olive oil to use in your day-to-day meal preparation that won't cost you an arm and a leg, then this is certainly a good buy and definitely of a good quality. If anything, it's of a much better quality than you would otherwise receive at this price-per-ounce.

I consider this to be one of the better purchases I've made this month.

product_title: Big Train Mocha 3.5 lb bulk
review_body:
I bought this & [[ASIN:B001ABTGF8 MOCAFE Frappe Wild Tribe Moka, Ice Blended Coffee, 3-Pound Tin]] at the same time & did a head-to-head comparison of the two. They are very comparable. I used the same amount of ice, milk & powder in each test. On a side note, if you're looking for something that tastes just like the McD's mocha frappe, neither of these are it, but they're both excellent.

The texture was similar, perhaps a bit smoother but thicker with the Big Train. The chocolate flavors were slightly different (Big Train slightly more bitter like a Ghiradelli & Mocafe smoother like a Symphony bar), but both were equally chocolatey. You can add more chocolate to it with a chocolate syrup, if you want it super chocolatey.

The result: this & Mocafe Wild Tribe are both really good mocha frappes. They both have a very small amount of coffee in them, so you can easily use them as a base by adding more coffee or espresso or even other flavors. Whichever one you'd prefer comes down to personal preference and probably whichever you started out drinking, I didn't find that one was considerably better than the other. Whichever one you go with, you won't be disappointed.

Since I was a barista, I thought I'd include tips how to prepare this:

Hot: Mix with hot (hotter the better) milk or coffee (some people use water). You can mix in blender or, if you have a pro-type steamer, you can use that (but make sure to mix powder with the liquid a bit first -- the powder will fly everywhere if you don't, trust me).

Cold: In your glass, fill with ice cubes. Add any liquid to the glass until it's about 3/4 full (you can add cold milk, cold coffee, extra flavours, or a mix). Add the powder to the blender -- about 1 scoop for a smaller sized drink, two for a large. Add your liquid & ice mix from your cup. Blend on low speed for about 20 seconds, then high until you get the consistency you want. For a less thick drink, use less ice cubes.

product_title: Thai Kitchen Rice Noodle Cart
review_body:
When I bought this, I saw the words \\"Gluten Free\\" on the front of the package, briefly scanned the back for any of the other things I couldn't eat, and threw it in my cart as emergency rations. After all, not only was it instant and on sale, but it was from a company I trusted would sell me a quality product. I should have read the ingredients more thoroughly.

One thing that is common among most types of instant noodles is that they contain wheat--the main source of gluten--as their primary ingredient. However, the noodles in this instant \\"pad Thai\\" are \\"rice noodles\\". I cannot call them actual rice noodles, though, as they aren't just rice and water; they also contain potato starch, amylase, and lactic acid. The potato starch serves to keep the noodles together, but it has an unfortunate side effect of imparting a rather strong flavor to the noodles, one that I could smell from the instant I opened the package (and one that made me wonder whether or not the noodles had been spoiled, because the odor was completely unexpected). I assume the amylase (not a normal food additive as far as I am aware) is responsible for the sweet flavor of the noodles, as it occurs naturally in saliva and is designed to break down carbohydrates into sugar. And the lactic acid is disappointing, too, as I assumed this product was entirely nondairy.

These noodles could not possibly function with any pad Thai sauce that could be called even remotely authentic, and the inauthenticity of the sauce does not disappoint. Sure, it's made with fish sauce and lemon extract, but it's also made with sugar (as the primary ingredient of the sauce!), tomato, corn starch, hydrolized soy protein, and smoke flavor. It isn't remotely like a pad Thai.

The vegetables, thankfully, tasted like they should, and though I would not call them \\"high quality\\", they are at least both on par with the freeze-dried vegetables in other instant dishes and taste as expected; I couldrecognize the carrots and bok choy by taste, and they tasted like dehydrated carrots and bok choy.

This product isn't entirely AWFUL. It just isn't remotely what it advertises. If you're used to budget Chinese takeout and instant ramen, and don't care to appreciate the subtleties of authentic Asian cuisine, this dish serves nicely as a gluten-free alternative to cheap Chinese food. If anything, it's an Asian fusion dish--if you're not expecting pad Thai (or Thai food in general) when you taste this, it will come off as a generically sweet and crunchy Asian dish, and if that's what you're looking for, this serves its purpose. I wouldn't pay all that much for one of these things, though. It isn't even that big.

product_title: Navitas Organics Cashews, 1 Pound Pouch (Pack of 2)
review_headline: Perfect for home-roasting without added oil: No turning back!
review_body:
These are excellent quality for home roasting where you can control what is added (almost nothing) to achieve the perfect roasted cashews. Don't let the number of steps put you off...it's really simple. Here's all you do:

1. Dump a bag of Navitas Naturals Raw Cashews into a bowl
2. Add 1 - 2 tablespoons water (it should NOT pool at the bottom of the bowl)
3. Add 1/4 - 1/2 teaspoon sea salt (or your other favorite)
4. STIR WELL
5. Let marinate for 6-8 hours; YES, 6-8 HOURS ... go live your life and do other things :-) ... stir every so often when you or someone else in the family passes by the bowl.
6. After 6-8 HOURS, add another 1/4 -1/2 teaspoon sea salt (or other favorite) while cashews are still slightly damp so salt sticks...again, STIR WELL
6. Dump marinated cashews onto non-stick foil lined rimmed baking sheet into SINGLE LAYER
7. Plop into 285-degree oven for 15 minutes (YES, EXACTLY 285-degrees, or you are on your own and I cannot take blame for burnt or under-roasted cashews)
8. Take out cashews and give them a good stir
9. Plunk back into 285-degree oven for another 15 minutes: DO NOT OVERCOOK; these babies can go from golden to burnt quickly; give them the attention they deserve and they will not disappoint you; same as with people :-)
10. Remove cashews, let them cool and \\"re-harden\\" thoroughly for 45-60 minutes
11. Good luck keeping these little gems around for very long :-)

I know that these have \\"kept\\" perfectly on the counter in a TIGHTLY SEALED GLASS container (see Pyrex or Rubbermaid for good options) for 1 week, and were gobbled up by that time._

1. Soak the berries for 12 hours
2. Drain, rinse, and let sprout for 12 hours
3. Prepare the soil in the tray (or whatever growing medium) and spread the sprouts out evenly. Then water well and cover for 24 hours.
4. Depending on the depth of your soil, you may have to water. Remove the cover once the growing grass lifts it off

product_title: Ener-G Egg Replacer -- 16 oz
review_body:
On the box it states it doesn't work well with most boxed mixes but I used it just fine! For cupcakes I used it with Betty Crocker's Devil's Food Cake mix with success. Some tips: 1) Mix all the ingredients before adding this. It should be the last thing added at the end, mixed in, then immediately put what you're baking in the oven. 2) When it gives you the ratio of mix to water, I added just a tiny bit extra...like 1/2 tsp. 3) When mixing it to the water, use WARM water and remember to mix it with the water in a separate bowl until the lumps come out before adding it to your batter. It will be thick and a bit frothy. 4) Keep in mind eggs would normally add substance and structure to what you bake so without the eggs the end product is super light and airy....a little too much so at time. I personally recommend adding a little fruit/veggie to the batter to add substance and nutrition. (Black beans or zucchini for chocolate, apple or pumpkin for a spice bread, beets to a red velvet cake, cherry pie filling, etc.)5) What you're making won't rise much with this so fill your cake/cupcake tins a little bit more than you would if you weren't using this product....until you get a feel for how much your baked goods will rise with it in there I'd be safe and put foil or something under the pan in case there is spillage. For my cakes/cupcakes I usually fill them about 3/4 of the way up and they come out just right.

***Update: We still use this regularly for baking because it is so much more convenient to buy than all of the ingredients in it individually. I've found that using either a stand or hand mixer to really work some air into your batter before adding the powder/water slurry helps what you're baking rise so much better. You can also help it along by adding 1/2 tsp baking powder + 1/2 tsp lemon juice. You won't taste the lemon juice in the baked good but it boosts the rising power. Thus far the best success we've had is with the devil's food cake mix from the store plus a can of cherry pie filling in place of the oil, and then the slurry made from this stuff in place of eggs. Perfection!he store plus a can of cherry pie filling in place of the oil, and then the slurry made from this stuff in place of eggs. Perfection!

review_headline: Pretty good-just have to give it a chance.
review_body: No one in my family is allergic but I have a friend whose child has a peanut/treenut allergy.  We were discussing the pros and cons of a peanut ban at schools-although ours hasn't yet, I said well then what would my child eat. I understand the true and serious risk to an allergic person, but I still worry about what I would serve as an alternative, as I had heard that many substitutes were just not very good. Our doctor had even told us to have my son eat peanut butter to help boost his protein intake as has sensitivities to most meat products.  Ny friend suggested we try WOWButter, just even a couple times to see if he liked it.  I purchased one container of the creamy version at a local walmart. I have very open tastes and never hesitate to try anything new, so I figured I might like the flavor well enough; but I was a little leery of what the consistency and texture would be like.  And of course the real test was whether my son would eat it!  Well I was very pleasantly surprised.  I tried it first-the taste definitely has a little of the 'roast' flavor, but I think its quite good, and it's a rich flavor.  It definitely has a nutty taste-in my opinion more like a different nut than peanut-but not bad at all.  I was very pleased with the texture as well.  It doesn't need stirred or get greasy, and to me I could not tell a difference in the consistency when spreading it on bread or crackers or when eating it.  I think it tastes just fine by itself and on bread with or without jelly.  I haven't tried to cook or bake with it, but I never did that with peanut butter either, so I can't compare it on for those purposes.  Now that I have used it several times myself, I find that I like the richness of the taste better than peanut butter.  The real test of course is whether my son would eat it.  The first couple times I gave it to him I made a sandwich with regular PB and this swirled together, he ate it fine. For the next few sandwiches I did the same thing only reducing the regular PB each time.  He ate it fine and didn't say anything to me about it, so I switched to just WOWbutter. He has been eating it fine. One time he saw the jar and noticed it was different that what we had had.  I said I had just gotten a different brand because they were out of the other.  He said, oh, I thought it tasted a little different.  I asked if it was ok and he said yes he liked it fine.  So...can you tell a difference?  Yes.  Is it 'exactly' like peanut butter? No. But, in my mind it is a perfectly reasonable substitute and really quite good-if you don't expect a perfect peanut butter taste.  I thought the texture and consistency was fine, and it was not either dry or greasy.  I told my friend she was right, and am now using this in his lunches all the time. product_title: Mango Ginger Habanero Sauce
review_headline: Pure sugar! Nothing but sweeeeeeeet!!!! BLECH!
review_body:
Three of us recently purchased a bottle of this sauce, looking for and expecting a Mango sauce base with a ginger and a habanero kick. Instead, we were punched in the face with probably some of the sweetest, most uninteresting and obnoxious sauce we've ever had the displeasure of tasting. One of my friends actually rinsed his mouth out after tasting a teaspoon of this stuff. At > $8 a bottle, we expected a heck of a lot more than 16oz of toxically-sweet goop. This stuff would make excellent ant poison, if you were to add just a little Borax to the mix... or perhaps hummingbird nectar, if diluted 1:100 with water. Seriously, though, we have no idea what these guys were thinking when they came up with this monstrosity. There's ZERO Mango, ZERO Ginger, and absolutely no Habanero anywhere to be found in this sauce. As naturally sweet as Mangoes are, it seems very strange to us that Fischer & Wieser felt the first ingredient in this sauce needed to be \\"sugar\\" - and boy, they weren't kidding.

This sauce was incredibly far off the mark. The rest of this so-called \\"handcrafted goodness\\" was dumped down the drain with a promise that we won't be making THAT mistake again.

Ingredients: Sugar, Sugar, Sugar, Sugar, Sugar, Mango (allegedly), Water (allegedly), Apple Cider Vinegar (allegedly), Honey, Ginger (allegedly), Red Pepper Flakes (allegedly), Habanero Pepper (yeah, right!!).

review_body:

Now, as other reviewers mentioned in newer reviews...the coconuts used now are from Indonesia. The taste is not horrible but is different. I don't like it as much..has a tang to it that is not great in comparison..for me anyway. I was so happy with naked and now this is the second brand to change their coconut sourcing on me. I think this will be my last case of coconut water. I am bored with trying to jump around and figure out which one uses Brazilian and if they'll change that, or if ill get a funky batch in general.. If I were going to stick with it I'd stay with naked. It guess ill just eat more bananas and occasionally drink coconut oil in warm water like I used to. If I can get my hands on some real coconuts..that would be nice! I lowered my original rating from 5 stars to 3.

product_title: The Good Bean Chickpea Snacks, Smoky Chili & Lime, Gluten and Nut Free, 2.5-Ounce (Pack of 6)
review_body:
*****
These are my very favorite snacks, and this flavor--the smoky chili & lime--is the one I like best. They are very, very hot, spicy, and intense--but I LOVE that. They are crunchy too. If you like to munch on snacks, you'll like this one, I think.

Each bag comes with two servings in it for a total of (if you eat both servings, which I do) 280 calories, 4g fat, 46g carbohydrates, and 14g protein. This snack is gluten-free and uses non-gmo garbanzo beans. The ingredients are roasted chickpeas, evaporated can juice (ie, sugar), coarse salt, lime juice concentrate, gum arabic, expeller-pressed canola oil (non-gmo), and Vitamin E. Half of the package (or one serving) isn't that much food, plus then you have the problem of keeping the rest of the package crunchy--if you leave them out in a bowl they will be not so crunchy the next day. I'm not sure why they add the sugar, but the taste is really fantastic without being sweet, so maybe it keeps them from being bitter.

Sometimes if I just want to have a delicious snack and I'm hungry and able to handle the carbs, I have these. They take a while to eat (they can be a bit hard on your teeth as they are very, very crunchy) and fill you up, plus if you drink lots of water (or other beverage) with it, you'll be really full afterwards.

They can be purchased alone in a six-pack here or as part of the sampler set. I have ordered them both ways. I have noticed mixed reviews here, so they are not to everyone's tastes; if you're not sure you'll like them, you can always order them as part of the sampler.

Highly recommended.

product_title: SeaBear Ready-to-Eat Pink Salmon, 3.5-Ounce Units   (Pack of 4)
review_body: Mild flavor, tender, delicious and best of all convenient! No can opener required so can toss in my backpack and go.  Mild flavor is packed with protein but nothing artificial (I don't mind skipping the red dye and preservatives other brands use!)

product_title: Taylors of Harrogate Yorkshire Gold
review_body: This is a huge box of the finest tea money can buy. Sometimes I can't resist opening the box just for the heavenly aroma. One bag in 5 minutes brews a nice big 10 to 12 ounce mug. Other reviewers have basically said it all - a strong, dark blend which holds up to adding milk, sugar, etc. This is my first try with the Red label - before I had the Yorkshire Gold. After doing a side by side comparison of the two here is what I thought. As great as the Red is, the Gold is even better! The Gold is more refined & balanced, with a more lingering sweetness, and of course more expensive. Both are so smooth, with Red being a bit harsher though. Either one will titillate your senses with everything you love about tea, taking your enjoyment to the next level. Caution: you may get hooked on Yorkshire and never be able to go back to anything else. I've got about 100 perfectly good Dilmah ceylon bags sitting in the pantry, which is a great tea as well... but I keep reaching for the Gold... I mean, Red. Cheers!

product_title: Mexican Style Fajita Marinade 16 0z(pack of 3)
review_headline: not only changed cap and logo color
review_body: Ordered this fajita marinade, the picture showed the old packaging blue bottle.  Had bought the Mexican Style with the new yellow cap in store and didn't like the taste at all.  Was so happy to find the blue cap Fajita sauce online.  Received the order and I now have 6 bottle of the new yellow cap.  It is too spicy and kind of bitter.  Very disappointed, now I have 6 bottle of marinade that no one in my family likes.  Hope that the company that has taken over World Harbor will bring the old recipe back.  I see now that it shows the Blue capped marinade out of stock.  Boohoo

product_title: Kirkland Signature Pure Vanilla, 16 Ounce
review_body: It's a good value but we find this a 4 star, along with most available in big box stores. Altho it \\"OK', we're spoiled by what we consider a 5 star, \\"Molina Vanilla\\", which we can't find around here.

product_title: Dr. Oetker Vanilla Pudding 3 Pack
review_body: We are able to satify our pudding cravings by cooking Dr oetker's pudding mix with non-dairy (almond for us) milks. Tastes like regular pudding to me.

product_title: Walkers Prawn Cocktail Crisps - 1.2 oz - Pack of 6
review_body: Walkers prawn cocktail flavour are delicious and if you haven't ever tried them - you should!  They were nice and cheap even though they were imported!

product_title: Pomona's Universal Pectin, 1.1 Ounce Box (Pack of 6)
review_body:
Excellent pectin! This easy berry recipe using Pomona's Pectin works every time:
2 lb pkg Frozen Wild Blueberries, 1 1/2 12-oz pkgs Frozen Dark Cherries, 1/3 cup Black Cherry Concentrate (like syrup).

Slice cherries to check for pits, briefly rinse blueberries, combine berries and cherries in a large pot, add 1 cup water and 1/3 cup concentrate.
Stir, then heat until steaming slightly, slowly sprinkle in 3 tsp pectin while stirring (5-10 min.), stir in 3 tsp calcium water.
Remove from heat and allow to cool, then refrigerate overnight.

product_title: Alwadi Al Akhdar Baba Ghannouge, Eggplant Dip, 12.75-Ounce Cans (Pack of 12)
review_body:
We love our homemade babaganoush but it takes a while to prepare and the local eggplants don't always look great. So last month when time was particularly tight I decided to try alwadi babaganoush. We had used their tahini and found it excellent.

[[ASIN:B000I07884 Alwadi Al Akhdar Baba Ghannouge, Eggplant Dip, 12.75-Ounce Cans (Pack of 12)]]

But still, canned babaganoush? How good could that possibly be any good?

One big question was how they flavored it. How would their balance of tahini, lemon, oil, herbs and spices turn out to be? Well, it was only 12 small cans, and if I didn't like it my husband would probably still eat it.

Another question for me was whether it would contain ingredients I can't eat as a gluten-free person. Fortunately Amazon let me see the ingredients list, and there's nothing in there I would put in in my own kitchen - pretty amazing for today's prepared foods.

When it came, we tested it right away by having some for lunch. We ate it with rice crackers. Wow, the taste was great. In fact, the taste was just like homemade. This product is going to stay on my subscription list at Amazon.

That little can lasted for two meals for the two of us eating all we wanted. I'm delighted with this product, another alwadi success, and recommend it to anyone who loves eggplant.

product_title: Taste Nirvan, Coconut Water, (Pack of 12)
review_body: I love this stuff. I am a runner and I drink one of these a day. I have not had a cramp since.

product_title: Marley Coffee & Tea
review_headline: A very fine coffee full of flavor and aroma.
review_body: 100% Ethiopian Yirgacheffe - means a very distinctive aroma and flavor that may not be familiar to many American consumers. This coffee brews up a nice medium roast with exotic floral and berry notes. The pods work well, as intended, and the company certainly tries to spread around the positivity. The individual foil packets keeps each pod fresh and ready to use. I have since tried several of their different coffees, and yet this remains my favorite!

product_title: Tamanishiki Super Premium Short Grain Rice, 15-Pound
review_headline: The best sticky rice out there
review_body: I love Tamanishiki rice, it's some of the best quality rice you can get. True it's a little more expensive, but a large bag like this lasts a while and I find it to be worth the cost for a rice-lover like myself.

product_title: 16 Count - Limited Edition Variety Coffee K-Cups for Keurig Brewers - Green Mountain Island Coconut, Green Mountain Pumpkin Spice, Donut Shop Coconut Mocha, Tully's Kona
review_body: I love all these flavors.  The Tully's Kona is the strongest tasting.  I didn't really taste the tropical flavor from the Tully's Kona Blend, but it was still good.  The Donut Shop Coconut Mocha and Green Mountain Island Coconut are my favorites. They smell so good and the taste is great as the beautiful aroma after brewing.  all I add is  some sugar and it's delicious.  I do agree with some of the reviews that say the taste could be stronger, it's not a deal breaker for me. It is a lighter coffee.  I would say that the price per cup is a little pricey for this batch of k-cups.  I only bought because I wanted to try all these particular flavors.  I most likely will not be re-purchasing this same batch.  I've run across another brand Called Timothy's that has a k-cup called \\"German Chocolate Cake\\".  I hear it's has a stronger taste and It's cheaper per cup.  I'm going to try that next.  I love the taste and smell of coconut.

product_title: Chocolate Pecan Biscotti 5.oz Sugar Free From Lilly's Home Style Bake Shop
review_body: I order a box every few weeks. One or two of these are pretty good with my morning coffee eating low carb/sugar/wheat.

review_body: I'm all about good coffee. I try different kinds from time to time, but I always return to Caribou. review_body: We could no longer find these chips at our local grocery store,so having them arrive at our door was sure was tempting. Shipment took longer than expected,about two weeks. review_body: This is, without a doubt, the best Turkish Coffee I have ever tried.  Very sophisticated taste.  Unfortunately, I am not a coffee connoisseur.  But I prefer this to anything made at Starbucks, Peetes or Diedrichs.  If you love the taste of coffee and haven't tried any Turkish Coffee before, this is the genuine article.  I just brew mine in a simmering pot over the stove.  No fancy gizmos.  Not that I wouldn't love to try to make it in one of those tiny pots, but my house is filled with every Ronco infomercial kitchen appliance since 1989 and I don't have any more room.  Plus, its like 3 of those pots to one of my coffee cups.  Finally, this stuff lasts forever and a day. It should take me a month or two to finish it.

product_title: Polar Pumpkin 100% Pure, No Sugar Added 15 Oz/24 Pack
review_headline: Not like any pjmpkin in a can I've used before
review_body: Because I make frozen pumpkin treats for my dogs, I was thrilled to find Polar Pumpkin at $1.00 per can.  When I opened the first can, however, my elation quickly subsided.  The contents may be a squash-like product but it's not like any pumpkin I've ever purchased before. It's darker and thicker, and it smells far different from my usual brands. review_body: Not only am I vegan but I'm a biologist and work outside a lot.  Buying these bars in bulk is a nice way of always having snacks. I have tried a few of their flavors and this one along with blueberry and coconut are my favorite.  I was not a fan or the raspberry one.  But to each their own. product_title: Progresso Panko Bread Crumbs, Italian Style, 8 oz (Pack of 12)
review_body:
This is probably the best crumb that has graced the top of my little pannikins of homemade Mac and Cheese that I've ever used. The crumbs were perfectly sized and heavily spiced. In the oven they browned perfectly, and my husband loved them.

SIZE:
I love the size of these breadcrumbs. They are larger than the bread 'dust' that you find in Progresso's regular Italian breadcrumbs, and much smaller than the crumb 'boulders' that is regular Japanese Panko.

(I realize these other sorts of breadcrumbs have their purpose, but for casseroles I think the Progresso Panko is ideal. They aren't powdery, and they aren't so large that they are too crunchy and distracting.)

TASTE:
You should know that these are very salty and very seasoned. If I were going to use them on chicken fillets I-personally wouldn't salt the meat first. Compared to the equivalent in bread-dust, I would say that these are more flavorable.

OTHER:
These are made with Canola oil and are 120 calories per 1/4 cup. I found them moist enough that I didn't have to add any butter. At a 350-degree oven they stayed moist after 20 minutes.

Really, if you like to cook, try picking up a box of these Panko styled crumbs with a mind to adding some variation to your favorite recipes.

Pam T~

review_body: This is the best cider I have ever had! It is absolutely DELICIOUS! Some 'instant' drinks have a weird after taste, and this does not at all. It has a creamy taste to it, I think because of the caramel.

review_body: I really enjoyed the pepper pistachios. I would like to order another bag.  When can I get another bag?  They weren't too salty and my grand children enjoyed them too.

product_title: Ener G Gum, Xanthan Gum, 6-Ounce (Pack of 1)
review_body: I have been baking gluten free for years. I normally use a different brand but was trying to save a few bucks. You all know gluten free baking is expensive!  So I make cupcakes to take to a picnic. I have used this recipe 100 times if not more. Never had an issue. Batch 1, a total disaster. I try again because I figure I was distracted. Batch 2 another flop.  I go, cupcakeless to the picnic. I try again Monday morning when everything is quiet and STILL a disaster. I order my normal brand and it gets here Wed. (thank you Amazon Prime ;) ) and use the same recipe and it turned out great!  I was shocked that a different brand could lead to such drastic differences in the final product!

product_title: RiceSelect Texmati-Mushroom and Vegetable Medley Rice Blend, 12.7-Ounce Jars (Pack of 6)
review_body: Great taste and easy to prepare. Have tried other like products, but this one is by far the best tasting.

product_title: Celsius Calorie Reducing Drink, 12 Ounce Cans
review_body: Excellent Energy drink, I drink one-a-day before I go for my daily walk, gives me a nice boost!  I like the taste, may take a few too get used to it!  No jitters just a boost!

product_title: Wolfgang Puck Coffee K-Cups for Keurig Brewers
review_body: I tried this product solely for the fact it has Wolfgang's name on it.  I should have stuck with Timothy's brand.  This was way too strong to be labeled a breakfast coffee, more like a dinner coffee.  I will not be buying this again, also way too expensive compared to the others.

product_title: Nagatanien Instant Miso Soup Sampler - 6 Flavors, 12 Servings
review_body:
If you like Miso Soup you must have this. The price is fair, the delivery is perfect, the product is a 'must have' in Japanese comfort food. Why get fat for lunch when you can get Nagatanien Instant Miso Soup?
6 flavors and 2 servings, just remember that a Japanese 'cup' is 160 ml, not a 250ml US cup. If you have never
tried it get a couple (2 to 4) little sushi and make a bowl of this soup. With a cup of tea you'll have all the lunch you want, and all the lunch you need. Is this why the Japanese outlive us? Who knows? but this sure is good. If you travel this is one you can pack a few bowls of, a bowl, a spoon and a little water boiler. When you stop at the Rats Nest Hotel for the night you have a great little meal (no need to mess with that Motel coffee that looks like it's been there since the last owner left). Give it a try. :-D

product_title: Matteo's Rear Trauma Hot Sauce 6 Oz
review_body: Why did they stop making the BEST hot sauce ever? Someone please tell me! My poor Hubby is still having withdrawals. He needs his fix of this awesome sauce.

product_title: Haywards Traditional Onions 400 grams
review_body: Always the best!!  Getting too expensive for me, but not the manufacturer's fault.

product_title: Bari Life Caramel Nut Protein Bar - 7/Box
review_body: I love these and appreciate how good they are for you.  I sometimes have low blood sugar and keep them in my purse for a quick burst of protein.  On days when I don't have time for lunch, I have one of these and it gets me through the afternoon.  No more guilt about having chocolate on my diet.  These are filling, tasty and satisfying.  What more do you need?

product_title: Big Train Spiced Chai, 1.9-Pound Cans (Pack of 2)
review_body: I am addicted to frozen blended chai frapps and wherever they are available I will order one! I was looking for a powder mix so I could start making them at home and save some money, and this was it! I am so happy with my purchase, and I now look forward to my mornings. The recipe on the tin for a frozen chai calls for water, but I use milk instead and add a little bit of almond flavoring syrup and it is perfect!! It can be a little sweet, but I like that, and you don't have to add any additional sweetener to it which is nice. If you like the iced or frozen chais that you order at cafes, then this is the product you need. Highly recommend it!

product_title: Whole White Popcorn
review_body:
I am a fan of popcorn and we eat it on a regular basis. I became concerned about GMOs in the popcorn I was buying, so I decided to try Bob's Red Mill. [They have a no-GMO policy in all of their products, whether they are organic or not].

This popcorn was awesome! Fluffy, white, and very tasty. Also, I cook my popcorn the \\"old fashioned way\\" in a pan with a lid on top of the stove. This popcorn had almost a 100% pop rate. Out of an entire large pan, 5 kernels were left unpopped. With all of the other brands I've tried, I always had WAY more unpopped kernels.

You can't go wrong with this popcorn - I love it!

product_title: Maranatha No Stir Peanut Spread with Calcium & Omega-3s, Creamy, 12-Ounce Jars (Pack of 4)
review_body:
I thought I was ordering something else, the organic variety, but got this instead and it was awful. I now order the organic kind from Vitacost. This is very expensive peanut butter, but it's delicious. Thicker than Jif, but the best organic peanutbutter available. I mention Jif because it was my favorite before going all organic. This does have a similar flavor, but it's not super light and fluffy like Jif. Jif boasts (hahaha!) Fully Hydrogenated Vegetable Oil. MaraNatha organic has none of that.

This people butter with calcium and omega 3s is nothing close to the organic.

product_title: Raw Revolution Organic Live Food Bars, 1.8-Ounce Bars (Pack of 12)
review_body: The taste is NOT what you would expect.  I have had better tasting products. For it to be a heavy, chocolate tasting bar, it tasted more like the agave nectar than the chocolate.  Very disappointed.

product_title: Sans Sucre Cheesecake Mousse Mix - Gluten Free

product_title: Duff - Buttercream Fondant 2Lb, Red
review_body: This fondant is delicious and easy to use.  I made cupcakes for my granddaughter's birthday party and they were a BIG hit! I recommend them highly and will use it again.

product_title: Mount Hagen Organic Freeze Dried Instant Coffee, 3.53-Ounce Jars (Pack of 6)
review_body: I like the Starbucks Via instant coffee, but would rather support another company instead of Starbucks every day, and I wanted to have organic coffee. product_title: KIND PLUS Gluten Free Bars
review_body: I have tried many snack and nutritional bars, and these are my current favorite. The combination of flavors not only satisfies my hunger but also satisfies my desire for something sweet. product_title: Guayaki Yerba Mate, 16 Ounce (12 Pack)
review_headline: stop drinking coffee and start drinking this!
review_body:
I'm not going to tell you what yerba mate is and all that. I just want to tell you that this stuff is amazing. The cans, the bottles, the tea bags: they're all great.
I can (and have) chug an entire can of guayaki yerba mate and feel amazing. it gives me a tingly sensation throughout my body, makes me mentally aware of everything (try drinking it in a nice shady park or something), and never ever makes me crash like coffee or energy drinks do.
The price might be a little high, but I feel it is worth it. It also depends where you buy it. I've seen the cans go for as high as $2.50, but i have found a place that sells them for only $2 a can! i'm not going to tell you where though! it's all mine! all mine!
the cans and bottles are my favorite. they have great flavors.
for the cans, the flavors, from greatest to least greatest:
lemon elation
enlighten mint

product_title: Bombay Basmati Brown Rice, 10-pounds Sack
review_headline: Rice itself looks to be of good quality, but packaging is terrible.
review_body: I purchased this brown basmati rice after trying a small package purchased at a grocery store. The price certainly is good, 10 lbs for under $15.00 which is really good for basmati rice from India. When I received the shipment, which was delivered promptly, I found that the burlap sack it comes in has a zipper at the top, but when un-zipped it is stitched shut and needs to be cut open. This is not a problem, as the sack says it is \\"tamper proof\\", however the inner plastic bag containing the rice was already open and small particles of burlap threads must have fallen onto the rice whilst cutting open the sack. Not to mention a large quantity of rice had already spilled outside the inner bag. When I attempted to remove the inner plastic bag it burst open and about half of the rice fell all over the floor. So I had to spend the next 20 min. cleaning up this huge mess of rice. I can't believe how tissue-thin the inner plastic bag is! Now I have to go buy a large container to transfer the remaining rice into. The rice itself looks to be of good quality, and I will probably end up ordering more of this rice in the future because the price can't be beat. But be forewarned about the packaging.

review_body: I can't add much to the other reviews. This is a very good product. I was going to add a list of ingredients, but I see Amazon has added this since I bought it. About the only thing I can add is that the quick set method works just fine. This stuff dissolves almost instantly in only 1C of boiling water. Then just add 1C of ice cubes and water and stir until the ice melts. This will set much faster in the fridge. You can also use 4 small juice glasses instead of a bowl, which will help it set even faster and helps with portion control. I don't know about others, but if I make this in a bowl, it usually only makes 2 servings (or maybe only one). But if I have 4 small servings already separated, they usually last for 4 servings, which does save money as this is a bit expensive, but well worth the cost.

product_title: Arrowhead Mills Gluten-Free Organic Maple Buckwheat Flakes - 10 oz
review_headline: Love buckwheat flour and other Arrowhead Mills products
review_body:
Arrowhead Mills products are outstanding, and their buckwheat flour is one of our kids all time favorites - especially in buckwheat pancakes where we do little more than add water, a little vanilla, water, and stir... so we figured 'what could be better than our favorite buckwheat pressed into flakes'? Well... almost.

These flakes have a great texture and are very crispy, and they do not lose their crispiness quickly when in the bowl with milk. There is also a hint of maple glaze about them that might add to keeping them from getting soggy.

They are really great with ripe, sweet peaches cut up and added to them, and they are excellent with strawberries and raspberries. However, by when served alone, with no fruit to sweeten the offering, they just do not get an A+ grade from us. Again, the texture and crispness is excellent, but the taste just falls flat -- they do not scream \\"Buckwheat\\" at all... instead, they are kinda like a better frosted flakes product without the added sugar.

In our humble opinion, buy these instead of buying store bought frosted flakes but make sure that you have a nice, sweet, natural accompaniment to go with them. If you don't expect the earthy buckwheat flavor to really show itself, then you will not be disappointed. Glad we tried them and would do it again if another free shipping deal comes along.

product_title: Ideal Sweetener No Calorie 10.6 Oz 6 Packs
review_headline: One of the best natural sweeteners available. Just IDEAL.
review_body:
If you are looking for a natural sweetener, and stevia changes the taste, or has a mild bitter aftertaste to you, than xylitol can be a good option. And among the many xylitol options IDEAL is the best for our family. Other xylitol products may cause stomach discomfort (which is not uncommon for sugar alcohols in general). But not with IDEAL Sweetener. Perhaps it is in how the manufacturer sources the xylitol, or how it is manufactured and mixed with a bit of sucralose? We've not experienced stomach discomfort, and we use it just like sugar. Xylitol has none of the bad effects of sugar. For example, sugar has a glycemic index of anywhere from 85 to 100, but xylitol only 7; an important benefit for people with diabetes. Also, xylitol helps protect teeth. While sugar does the opposite. Xylitol is found in fruits and vegetables, and even made by the human body; thus the claim to it being natural. (99% natural for the IDEAL brand, since the manufacturer does in fact add a bit of sucralose. Perhaps this is why, in our experience, the IDEAL version of xylitol is far better tolerated than the 100% xylitol brands at health stores.)

We have a 6 year old at home, and we don't want her exposed to too much sugar, or even artificial sweeteners. There are several stevia brands now that could have been good natural sweetener options for us, but a few of us in the household detect a mild bitter aftertaste. So xylitol is our \\"go-to\\" natural sweetener, and IDEAL is our favorite brand. It goes with almost anything that needs sugar, and cooks/bakes well. (Depending on the cooking/baking project, sometimes 100% substitution works, but more often, not. Thus, when cooking/baking with it, try first at 75% sugar + 25% IDEAL. If successful, see if 66/33 works, and then 50/50% sugar and IDEAL. And so on. For most of our cooking/baking projects, most can't tell that we substituted up to half of the sugar with IDEAL.) Our next project is to try making ice-cream with 100% IDEAL instead of sugar.

It is unfortunate that Stop & Shop does not carry it. And A&P used to, but stopped making it available. So, we buy from Amazon.

product_title: Blue Lotus - Masala Chai - Ready to Savor in a Moment…
review_headline: THE best chai...and it's instant, unsweetened & all organic!
review_body:
This is hands down THE best chai - IF you like your chai spicy (and what's the point if it's not spicy?). Bonus, it's instant! Don't be deterred by the price of this small can - you use just 1/8 (yes, that's right...one-eighth) of a teaspoon per cup, add hot water, milk & sweetner and instantly you have a cup of hot, spicy chai goodness. I LOVE that there is no milk or artificial milk or sweetner of any kind, so I can customize my own cup and don't have to deal with any unwanted goodies.

The company seems really conscientious and only uses ORGANIC herbs/spices. If you go to their website they list each spice detailing the health benefits. When I gave up coffee I became a chai fanatic and darn near went broke drinking a local brand that comes liquid in bottles (at $10/qt!). Plus it was sweetened, so I couldn't control the sweetness - pre-sweetened is ALWAYS too sweet for me. I went online and ordered every unsweetened chai I could find and started brewing my own. I kept thinking \\"why doesn't someone take the liquid and dehydrate it\\"? This was the only company that did and it just happened that it was the best tasting! You can buy this in one-pound bags as well, so as soon as I'm finished with my can (which I've had for over a month now), I'll start buying in bulk to fill my cans. The cans are the perfect size too - they fit easily in your purse for chai-on-the-go.
